Inputs are CARE data with $Q=C^*C\succeq0$, $R\succ0$, a supplied stabilizing gain $K_0$, a nonnegative integer outer budget $N$, and either exact or safeguarded-inexact solve mode. Each exact-mode pass takes an admissible control packet for [[alg-bartels-stewart-sylvester-equation]]: pivot threshold $\tau_{\rm BS}\ge0$, a fixed $c_0>0$, nonnegative integer Schur sweep budgets $N_A,N_B\le c_0n$, and Schur controls for each coefficient matrix (deflation tolerance, positive integer stagnation period, finite exceptional-shift tables, arithmetic/range controls, and any supplied encoding or evaluator). Use its bounded-controller mode with a supplied nonnegative integer instruction budget $K_{\rm BS}$ and its built-in discriminant-sign controller. In inexact mode, also supply a nonnegative integer line-search limit $L$; each pass takes a Hermitian proposal $\widetilde P_j$, a stored candidate $\widehat X_j$ and approximate inverses for the finite Lyapunov systems below, and finite factorization witnesses for each trial. Stored inputs and point-solve proposals in this mode are exact dyadics; derived gains and coefficients are retained as exact rational expressions. Every point call uses the operationwise controller of [[alg-point-verified-linear-system-certifier]]; every scalar enclosure uses a finite outward evaluator with a declared work budget. Write $S(K)=Q+K^*RK$ and $\mathcal L_A(P)=A^*P+PA$.

For $j=0,\ldots,N-1$, put $A_j=A-BK_j$. In exact mode, call [[alg-bartels-stewart-sylvester-equation]] with coefficient matrices $A_j^*,A_j$, right-hand side $-S(K_j)$, and that pass's complete control packet to solve
$$\mathcal L_{A_j}(X_j)=-S(K_j).$$
If it does not return success, stop with its status. Otherwise set $K_{j+1}=R^{-1}B^*X_j$, append the gain and residual, and continue.

In safeguarded-inexact mode, $X_j$ denotes the unique exact solution of $\mathcal L_{A_j}(X_j)=-S(K_j)$; it exists because $K_0$ is stabilizing and every previously accepted trial has a Hurwitz witness. Under column vectorization, use the point matrix $I_n\otimes A_j^*+A_j^T\otimes I_n$ for $\mathcal L_{A_j}$, as in [[lem-sylvester-vectorization-isometry-and-kronecker-identity]]. Before the current-cost point call, clear a common positive integer denominator $d_j$ from this exact rational coefficient matrix and from $-\operatorname{vec}(S(K_j))$. Call [[alg-point-verified-linear-system-certifier]] on the resulting dyadic system, with the supplied inverse proposal for the scaled coefficient and $\widehat X_j$ as the solution proposal. Scaling both sides by $d_j$ preserves the exact solution $X_j$; if the scaled entries cannot be stored exactly in the declared point format, return `range-failure`. A `range-failure` returns that status; an `inconclusive` result returns `safeguard-inconclusive`. Let its solution ball have center $\widehat X_j$ and radius $s_j$, replacing the center by its Hermitian part if needed. Set $D_j=\widetilde P_j-\widehat X_j$ and compute the outward Gershgorin upper bound
$$\eta_j=s_j+\max_i\left((D_j)_{ii}+\sum_{k\ne i}|(D_j)_{ik}|\right).$$
For Hermitian $D_j$, the maximum row bound above is at least $\lambda_{\max}(D_j)$, by applying the eigenvector equation at a coordinate of maximal modulus. Define $\widetilde K_j=R^{-1}B^*\widetilde P_j$ and inspect the finite line-search list $\theta_\ell=2^{-\ell}$, $0\le\ell\le L$. For each trial $K_\ell=K_j+\theta_\ell(\widetilde K_j-K_j)$, let $A_\ell=A-BK_\ell$ and use its supplied exact factor witnesses $W_\ell=L_\ell^*L_\ell$ with nonsingular $L_\ell$, and $Z_\ell$ satisfying
$$A_\ell^*W_\ell+W_\ell A_\ell\preceq-\mu_\ell I,$$
where $\mu_\ell>0$ and $-A_\ell^*W_\ell-W_\ell A_\ell-\mu_\ell I=Z_\ell^*Z_\ell$. Verify these exact factor identities; otherwise reject the trial and continue. Vectorize $\mathcal L_{A_\ell}$ using the same coefficient matrix as for $A_j$. Outward-evaluate $I-R_\ell\mathcal L_{A_\ell}$ and let $q_\ell$ be a Frobenius upper bound. If no finite enclosure is available or $q_\ell\ge1$, reject the trial and continue. Set $\kappa_\ell=\|R_\ell\|_F/(1-q_\ell)$; the Neumann estimate and $\|T\|_2\le\|T\|_F$ give $\kappa_\ell\ge\|\mathcal L_{A_\ell}^{-1}\|_{F\to F}$. Separately outward-evaluate the raw residual and set $r_\ell$ to an upper bound for
$$\mathcal L_{A_\ell}(\widetilde P_j)+Q+K_\ell^*RK_\ell,$$
with Frobenius norm. Accept the first trial satisfying $\eta_j+\kappa_\ell r_\ell\le0$; then set $K_{j+1}=K_\ell$, append the accepted gain and its certificates, and proceed to pass $j+1$. If no trial passes, return `safeguard-inconclusive` without changing $K_j$. Any unavailable outward bound is inconclusive. The inverse bound above follows from the Neumann estimate, and $r_\ell$ bounds the raw residual separately; the preconditioned residual in [[def-verified-linear-residual-certificate-data]] is a different quantity. All certificate witnesses and bounds use the finite outward evaluator; a non-finite operation returns its range status. After at most $N$ accepted updates return the gain sequence, solve residuals, cost-matrix data and terminal status. An arbitrary approximate Lyapunov solve is never accepted without the separate stability and descent checks above.

Let $A\in F^{n\times n}$, $B\in F^{n\times m}$, $C\in F^{p\times n}$, $R=R^*\succ0$, $Q=C^*C$, and $G=BR^{-1}B^*$. Assume $(A,B)$ is continuously stabilizable and $(A,C)$ is continuously detectable, using [[def-lqr-stabilizability-and-detectability]]. Then the CARE of [[def-standard-continuous-and-discrete-riccati-equations]] has exactly one Hermitian positive-semidefinite solution $X$. Its closed-loop matrix $A_c=A-GX$ is Hurwitz, and for every initial state $x_0$ the infinite-horizon value
$$\inf_u\int_0^\infty\bigl(x(t)^*Qx(t)+u(t)^*Ru(t)\bigr)\,dt=x_0^*Xx_0$$
is attained by $u(t)=-R^{-1}B^*Xx(t)$. Controls are locally square-integrable and states are locally absolutely continuous solutions of $\dot x=Ax+Bu$. A finite value also forces the terminal term $x(T)^*Xx(T)$ to tend to zero; this transversality is proved below.

Let $A\in F^{n\times n}$ be Hurwitz and let $Q=Q^*\in F^{n\times n}$. Then the improper matrix integral

$$
X=\int_0^\infty e^{tA}Qe^{tA^*}\,dt
$$

converges and is the unique solution of $AX+XA^*+Q=0$. If $Q\succeq0$, then $X\succeq0$. If $Q\succ0$, then $X\succ0$. For $Q\succeq0$, $X\succ0$ if and only if there is no nonzero $v$ for which $e^{tA^*}v\in\ker Q^{1/2}$ for every $t\ge0$.

Let $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ be Hurwitz, let $\alpha=-\max\{\operatorname{Re}\lambda:\lambda\in\sigma(A)\}>0$, and write $e^{tA}=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}t^kA^k/k!$. If $A=UTU^*$ is a unitary Schur triangularization and $T=D+N$ with $D$ diagonal and $N$ strictly upper triangular, then for every $t\ge0$,

$$
\|e^{tA}\|_2\le e^{-\alpha t}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{(t\|N\|_2)^k}{k!}.
$$

For real Hurwitz $A$, the same bound holds for its real matrix exponential, with the complex operator norm of its realification equal to the real one.

Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $A\in F^{n\times n}$, $B\in F^{n\times m}$, $C\in F^{p\times n}$, and $R=R^*\in F^{m\times m}$ be positive definite. Write $Q=C^*C$ and $G=BR^{-1}B^*$. The inverse $R^{-1}$ is well-defined: [[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]] supplies an invertible factor $R=LL^*$, so $R^{-1}=L^{-*}L^{-1}$. Thus $v^*Gv=\|L^{-1}B^*v\|_2^2\ge0$ and $v^*Qv=\|Cv\|_2^2\ge0$. The symbol $^*$ is transpose over $\mathbb R$ and conjugate transpose over $\mathbb C$.

The **continuous algebraic Riccati equation (CARE)** is
$$A^*X+XA-XGX+Q=0.$$
Its residual is $F_c(X)=A^*X+XA-XGX+Q$, its feedback is $K_c(X)=R^{-1}B^*X$, and its closed-loop matrix is $A_c(X)=A-BK_c(X)=A-GX$.

For $X=X^*\succeq0$, $S_X:=R+B^*XB$ is positive definite because
$v^*S_Xv=v^*Rv+(Bv)^*X(Bv)>0$ for every nonzero $v$. The **discrete
algebraic Riccati equation (DARE)** is
$$X=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA.$$
Its residual is $F_d(X)=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA-X$. Whenever $X=X^*$, the matrix $R+B^*XB$ is positive definite if $X\succeq0$. Its feedback and closed-loop matrix are
$$K_d(X)=(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA,\qquad A_c(X)=A-BK_d(X).$$
A CARE solution is **stabilizing** when it is Hermitian and $A_c(X)$ is Hurwitz. A DARE solution is **stabilizing** when it is Hermitian, $R+B^*XB\succ0$, and $A_c(X)$ is Schur stable. No inverse of $A$ is part of either definition.

For Hermitian $X$ with $S_X$ invertible, multiplication gives
$$(I+GX)^{-1}=I-BS_X^{-1}B^*X,\qquad X(I+GX)^{-1}=X-XB S_X^{-1}B^*X.$$
In either product, the additional coefficient of $B$ is
$R^{-1}-S_X^{-1}-S_X^{-1}(B^*XB)R^{-1}=0$, because
$S_X=R+B^*XB$. Thus the DARE is equivalently
$X=Q+A^*X(I+GX)^{-1}A$, and its closed-loop matrix is
$A_c(X)=(I+GX)^{-1}A$.

The associated homogeneous symplectic pencil is
$$N=\begin{bmatrix}A&0\\-Q&I\end{bmatrix},\qquad M=\begin{bmatrix}I&G\\0&A^*\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathcal P(\alpha,\beta)=\beta N-\alpha M.$$
The homogeneous-coordinate convention is that a finite eigenvalue
$\lambda$ is $[\alpha:\beta]=[\lambda:1]$ and $[1:0]$ denotes infinity.

derivations.claim: Suppose $A_j$ is Hurwitz. By [F3], the exact solution $X_j$ of the policy Lyapunov equation is $X_j=\int_0^\infty e^{tA_j^*}(Q+K_j^*RK_j)e^{tA_j}\,dt\succeq0.$ For $\Delta_j=K_{j+1}-K_j$, expansion using $B^*X_j=RK_{j+1}$ gives $A_{j+1}^*X_j+X_jA_{j+1}+Q+K_{j+1}^*RK_{j+1}=-\Delta_j^*R\Delta_j.$ If $A_{j+1}v=\lambda v$ with $\operatorname{Re}\lambda\ge0$, the quadratic form of the left side is $2\operatorname{Re}(\lambda)v^*X_jv+v^*Qv+(K_{j+1}v)^*R(K_{j+1}v)\ge0,$ while the right side is nonpositive. Equality forces $K_{j+1}v=0$ and $\Delta_jv=0$, hence $K_jv=0$ and $A_jv=Av=\lambda v$, contradicting that $A_j$ is Hurwitz. Starting from $K_0$, induction proves every $A_j$ Hurwitz and every $X_j\succeq0$.

Subtracting the Lyapunov equations for $X_j$ and $X_{j+1}$ after expressing both under $A_{j+1}$ gives $A_{j+1}^*(X_j-X_{j+1})+(X_j-X_{j+1})A_{j+1}=-\Delta_j^*R\Delta_j.$ The Lyapunov integral [F3] therefore yields $X_j-X_{j+1}\succeq0$. The decreasing sequence is bounded below by zero, so each quadratic form converges. Evaluating at $e_i$, $e_i+e_j$, and $e_i+\mathrm i e_j$ shows convergence of every matrix entry to a Hermitian limit $X_\infty\succeq0$. Since $K_{j+1}=R^{-1}B^*X_j$, the gains also converge. Passing to the limit in the policy Lyapunov equation gives the CARE for $X_\infty$; [F2] identifies this positive-semidefinite root as $X_*$.

Let $E_j=X_j-X_*$ and $A_*=A-BR^{-1}B^*X_*$. Put $D_j=K_{j+1}-K_*=R^{-1}B^*E_j$. Subtract the CARE identity at $X_*$ from the policy Lyapunov equation under $A_{j+1}$ to obtain $A_{j+1}^*E_{j+1}+E_{j+1}A_{j+1}=-D_j^*RD_j.$ By [F2], $A_*$ is Hurwitz. Choose $W=\int_0^\infty e^{tA_*^*}Ie^{tA_*}\,dt\succ0$ using [F3], so $A_*^*W+WA_*=-I$. Since $A_{j+1}\to A_*$, for all large $j$ one has $A_{j+1}^*W+WA_{j+1}\preceq-\tfrac12I$. Along $\dot x=A_{j+1}x$, differentiation gives $\frac{d}{dt}(x^*Wx)\le-\frac12\|x\|_2^2\le-\frac{1}{2\|W\|_2}x^*Wx.$ Consequently $\|e^{tA_{j+1}}\|_2\le M e^{-\alpha t}$ with $M=(\|W\|_2/\lambda_{\min}(W))^{1/2}$ and $\alpha=1/(4\|W\|_2)$, uniformly for all sufficiently large $j$. Applying the Lyapunov integral to the error equation yields $\|E_{j+1}\|_F\le\left(\int_0^\infty M^2e^{-2\alpha t}\,dt\right)\|R\|_2\|R^{-1}B^*\|_2^2\|E_j\|_F^2.$ The integral is finite and supplies the stated local quadratic constant.

$$H=\begin{bmatrix}A&-G\\-Q&-A^*\end{bmatrix},\qquad A_c=A-GX.$$
Then
$$H\begin{bmatrix}I\\X\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}I\\X\end{bmatrix}A_c.$$
Moreover, $H$ has exactly $n$ eigenvalues in the open left half-plane and $n$ in the open right half-plane, none on the imaginary axis, and $\operatorname{Ran}\begin{bmatrix}I\\X\end{bmatrix}$ is its stable invariant subspace.

Let $X\succeq0$ be the stabilizing DARE solution, $G=BR^{-1}B^*$, and

Then
$$N\begin{bmatrix}I\\X\end{bmatrix}=M\begin{bmatrix}I\\X\end{bmatrix}A_c.$$
The pencil $(N,M)$ is regular. Its homogeneous determinant has n roots strictly inside the unit disk and n roots strictly outside the closed unit disk, with infinite roots counted in the latter group. Thus it has no unit-circle roots, even if $A$ is singular, and $\operatorname{Ran}\begin{bmatrix}I\\X\end{bmatrix}$ is its stable deflating graph.

derivations.claim: In either case, $U_2=XU_1$, so $U=[I;X]U_1$. If $H U=U T$ in the CARE case, right multiplication by $U_1^{-1}$ gives $H[I;X]=[I;X](U_1TU_1^{-1})$. The top block fixes the restriction matrix as $A-GX$; the bottom block reads $-Q-A^*X=X(A-GX)$, which is exactly $A^*X+XA-XGX+Q=0$.

If $NU=MU T$ in the DARE case, the same normalization gives $N[I;X]=M[I;X](U_1TU_1^{-1})$. The top block is $A=(I+GX)(U_1TU_1^{-1})$, so invertibility of $I+GX$ gives restriction matrix $(I+GX)^{-1}A$. The lower block is $X-Q=A^*X(I+GX)^{-1}A$, which is the DARE by [F3]. No claim survives an unverified leading-block inverse or a subsequent nonzero symmetry residual.

Let $A\in F^{n\times n}$, $B\in F^{n\times m}$, $C\in F^{p\times n}$, $R=R^*\succ0$, and $Q=C^*C$. Assume $(A,B)$ is discretely stabilizable and $(A,C)$ discretely detectable, using [[def-lqr-stabilizability-and-detectability]]. Then the DARE of [[def-standard-continuous-and-discrete-riccati-equations]] has exactly one Hermitian positive-semidefinite solution $X$. For the equivalent Riccati map $f(P)=Q+A^*P(I+GP)^{-1}A$, its finite-horizon iterates $P_0=0$, $P_{k+1}=f(P_k)$ satisfy $0\preceq P_k\uparrow X$. For all Hermitian positive-semidefinite $Y,Z$,
$$f(Y)-f(Z)=A_c(Y)^*(Y-Z)A_c(Z),\qquad A_c(Y)=(I+GY)^{-1}A.$$
The solution satisfies $R+B^*XB\succ0$, and its closed loop $A_c=A-B(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA$ is Schur stable. For each $x_0$, the infinite-horizon discrete cost
$$\inf_{(u_k)}\sum_{k=0}^\infty(x_k^*Qx_k+u_k^*Ru_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k,$$
over sequences with finite cost equals $x_0^*Xx_0$ and is attained by $u_k=-K_dx_k$. Singular $A$ is allowed throughout; no inverse of $A$ is used.

For Hermitian $G,H\succeq0$, define $\Phi_G(X)=X(I+GX)^{-1}$ and $f(X)=H+A^*\Phi_G(X)A$ on $X\succeq0$. One step of the exact inverse recurrence in [[alg-finite-budget-structure-preserving-doubling-for-dare]] is well-defined, preserves $G_j,H_j\succeq0$, and its updated triple satisfies
$$f\circ f(X)=H_1+A_1^*X(I+G_1X)^{-1}A_1,$$
where
$$A_1=A(I+GH)^{-1}A,\quad G_1=G+A(I+GH)^{-1}GA^*,\quad H_1=H+A^*H(I+GH)^{-1}A.$$
Consequently, starting from $(A,G,H)$, the exact recurrence satisfies $H_j=f^{2^j}(0)$ after $j$ updates. These claims concern exact arithmetic; the rounded branch has only its separately reported diagnostics.

Let $M\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ be Schur stable and let $r$ satisfy $\rho(M)<r<1$. For the Euclidean induced operator norm there is a finite $C_r$ such that
$$\|M^k\|_2\le C_r r^k\qquad(k\ge0).$$
For a real matrix, interpret the same statement on its complexification.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space and let
$T:V\to V$ be non-negative. Then there exists a unique non-negative operator
$R:V\to V$ such that

$$R^2=T.$$

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$, and
let $\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_r>0$ be the positive singular values of
$A$, where $r=\operatorname{rank}A$; write $\sigma_1=0$ when $r=0$.

1. **Spectral formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_2=\sigma_1$, where $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ is
   the operator norm of [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]].
2. **Frobenius formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_F=\bigl(\sigma_1^{2}+\cdots+\sigma_r^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$.
3. **Unitary invariance.** For every unitary $U\in M_m(\mathbb F)$ and
   $V\in M_n(\mathbb F)$ (over $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$: orthogonal matrices),
   $$\lVert UAV\rVert_2=\lVert A\rVert_2,\qquad \lVert UAV\rVert_F=\lVert A\rVert_F.$$
4. **Sharp rank comparison.**
   $$\lVert A\rVert_2\;\le\;\lVert A\rVert_F\;\le\;\sqrt{r}\,\lVert A\rVert_2.$$
   The lower inequality is an equality exactly when $r\le 1$; the upper
   inequality is an equality exactly when $\sigma_1=\cdots=\sigma_r$, that is,
   when all nonzero singular values coincide. In particular
   $\lVert A\rVert_F\le\sqrt{\min(m,n)}\,\lVert A\rVert_2$.

derivations.claim: By [F2], $H_j=P_{2^j}$ and $G_j,H_j$ remain positive semidefinite. Since [F1] gives $P_k\to X_*$, the subsequence $H_j=P_{2^j}$ also converges to $X_*$. No inverse of $A$ is used.

Put $M=A_c(X_*)$. By [F1], $M$ is Schur stable; [F3] therefore makes $W=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(M^*)^kM^k$ converge in norm. It is positive definite, $W\succeq I$, and $M^*WM=W-I$. If $w=\|W\|_2$, then $v^*M^*WMv\le(1-w^{-1})v^*Wv$, so the induced $W$-norm $\|M\|_W:=\|W^{1/2}MW^{-1/2}\|_2$ is at most $q_0=\sqrt{1-w^{-1}}<1$. Choose $q$ with $q_0<q<1$. Since $P_k\to X_*$ and $A_c(P_k)$ is continuous on $P_k\succeq0$, choose $k_0$ so $\|A_c(P_k)\|_W\le q$ for all $k\ge k_0$.

Let $E_k=X_*-P_k\succeq0$. The Riccati-map difference identity in [F1] gives $E_{k+1}=M^*E_kA_c(P_k).$ Define $\|E\|_{F,W^{-1}}=\|W^{-1/2}EW^{-1/2}\|_F$. By [F5], for $k\ge k_0$, $\|E_{k+1}\|_{F,W^{-1}}\le\|M\|_W\|A_c(P_k)\|_W\|E_k\|_{F,W^{-1}}\le q^2\|E_k\|_{F,W^{-1}}.$ Iteration gives $\|E_k\|_{F,W^{-1}}\le\|E_{k_0}\|_{F,W^{-1}}q^{2(k-k_0)}$. Taking $k=2^j$ and setting $C=\max\{1,\|E_{k_0}\|_{F,W^{-1}}q^{-2k_0}\}$ proves the displayed envelope for all $2^j\ge k_0$. Since $C>0$, direct calculation gives $\epsilon_{j+1}=Cq^{2^{j+2}}=\epsilon_j^2/C$.

citations.quote:
Let $X\succeq0$ be the stabilizing DARE solution, $G=BR^{-1}B^*$, and
$$N=\begin{bmatrix}A&0\\-Q&I\end{bmatrix},\qquad M=\begin{bmatrix}I&G\\0&A^*\end{bmatrix},\qquad A_c=A-B(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA.$$
Then
$$N\begin{bmatrix}I\\X\end{bmatrix}=M\begin{bmatrix}I\\X\end{bmatrix}A_c.$$
The pencil $(N,M)$ is regular. Its homogeneous determinant has n roots strictly inside the unit disk and n roots strictly outside the closed unit disk, with infinite roots counted in the latter group. Thus it has no unit-circle roots, even if $A$ is singular, and $\operatorname{Ran}\begin{bmatrix}I\\X\end{bmatrix}$ is its stable deflating graph.

Let $(A,B)$ be a regular pencil of order $n$. A **complex generalized Schur
form** is a factorisation
$$Q^*AZ=S,\qquad Q^*BZ=T,$$
where $Q,Z\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ are unitary in the sense of
[[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]], and $S,T$ are
upper triangular as in
[[def-triangular-and-diagonal-matrices-over-a-commutative-ring]]. For its
$i$th one-by-one diagonal block, $[s_{ii}:t_{ii}]$ is the
**diagonal homogeneous pair**.

For real $A,B$, a **real generalized Schur form** has
$$Q^TAZ=S,\qquad Q^TBZ=T,$$
where $Q,Z$ are orthogonal, $S$ is block upper triangular with diagonal blocks
of size one or two, and $T$ is upper triangular. Each one-by-one diagonal
block has a nonzero real homogeneous pair. For a two-by-two diagonal block
$(S_{kk},T_{kk})$, the **diagonal homogeneous roots** are the zeros of
$\det(\beta S_{kk}-\alpha T_{kk})$ in $[\alpha:\beta]$; such a block has a
nonreal conjugate pair of finite roots. A singular pencil is outside this
definition.

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces, and let $r$ be the number of positive singular values of $T$.
Then there exist orthonormal bases $(e_1,\dots,e_n)$ of $V$ and
$(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ of $W$, together with singular values

$$s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_r>0,$$

such that

$$Tv=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j\langle v,e_j\rangle f_j$$

for every $v\in V$.

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let
$A=(a_{ij})\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$. The **Frobenius norm** of $A$ is

$$\lVert A\rVert_F\;:=\;\Bigl(\,\sum_{i<m}\sum_{j<n}|a_{ij}|^{2}\Bigr)^{1/2},$$

where $|\cdot|$ is the absolute value on $\mathbb R$
([[def-abs-value]]) for $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ and the modulus on $\mathbb C$
([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) for
$\mathbb F=\mathbb C$, and the outer power is the nonnegative real square root.

**The displayed quantity is a norm.** Regard $A$ as the element of the
coordinate space $\mathbb F^{mn}$ whose $j+in$-th entry is $a_{ij}$. The
standard coordinate inner product of [[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]
satisfies $\langle A,A\rangle=\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}\overline{a_{ij}}$, which equals
$\sum_{i,j}|a_{ij}|^{2}$ because $z\overline z=|z|^{2}$
([[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]). Thus $\lVert A\rVert_F$ is
exactly the inner-product norm of [[def-inner-product-norm]] evaluated at $A$,
and the three norm axioms hold for $\lVert\cdot\rVert_F$ because they hold for
every inner-product norm. For real matrices the same sum is
$\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}^{2}$, since $|x|^{2}=x^{2}$ for real $x$ by the two cases of
[[def-abs-value]].

The Frobenius norm is the Euclidean norm of the full entry list, not the
largest factor by which the matrix stretches a single vector. It can coincide
with an induced $2$-norm in one-row or one-column cases, but in general it is a
different matrix norm from the induced operator norms used on this page. Its
relation to the spectral norm, its unitary invariance and its singular-value
formula are
[[thm-spectral-and-frobenius-norms-are-unitarily-invariant-with-singular-value-formulas-and-rank-comparison]].

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$, and
let $\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_r>0$ be the positive singular values of
$A$, where $r=\operatorname{rank}A$; write $\sigma_1=0$ when $r=0$.

1. **Spectral formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_2=\sigma_1$, where $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ is
   the operator norm of [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]].
2. **Frobenius formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_F=\bigl(\sigma_1^{2}+\cdots+\sigma_r^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$.
3. **Unitary invariance.** For every unitary $U\in M_m(\mathbb F)$ and
   $V\in M_n(\mathbb F)$ (over $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$: orthogonal matrices),
   $$\lVert UAV\rVert_2=\lVert A\rVert_2,\qquad \lVert UAV\rVert_F=\lVert A\rVert_F.$$
4. **Sharp rank comparison.**
   $$\lVert A\rVert_2\;\le\;\lVert A\rVert_F\;\le\;\sqrt{r}\,\lVert A\rVert_2.$$
   The lower inequality is an equality exactly when $r\le 1$; the upper
   inequality is an equality exactly when $\sigma_1=\cdots=\sigma_r$, that is,
   when all nonzero singular values coincide. In particular
   $\lVert A\rVert_F\le\sqrt{\min(m,n)}\,\lVert A\rVert_2$.

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces,

$$\lVert ST\rVert\le \lVert S\rVert\,\lVert T\rVert.$$

For every such linear map $T$,

$$\lVert T^*T\rVert=\lVert T\rVert^2.$$

Let $M\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ be Schur stable and let $r$ satisfy $\rho(M)<r<1$. For the Euclidean induced operator norm there is a finite $C_r$ such that
$$\|M^k\|_2\le C_r r^k\qquad(k\ge0).$$
For a real matrix, interpret the same statement on its complexification.

Let $X$ be a normed space over $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and assume
$X$ admits an ordered basis of finite length. Then $X$ is a Banach space in the
sense of [[def-banach-space]].

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space and let
$T:V\to V$ be non-negative. Then there exists a unique non-negative operator
$R:V\to V$ such that

$$R^2=T.$$

Let $n_1,n_2\ge1$, $n=n_1+n_2$, and let $A,B\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ be
block upper triangular with the same two-block partition of sizes $n_1,n_2$,
with diagonal blocks $A_{11},A_{22}$ and
$B_{11},B_{22}$. For every $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb C$,
$$\det(\beta A-\alpha B) =\det(\beta A_{11}-\alpha B_{11})\det(\beta A_{22}-\alpha B_{22}).$$
Every endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space over an algebraically closed field has a Jordan canonical form over that field, including the endomorphism of the zero space.

Let $E\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, $n\ge1$, and let $0\le q<1$ satisfy $\|E\|_2\le q$. Then $I-E$ is invertible and
$$
\|(I-E)^{-1}\|_2\le \frac1{1-q}.
$$

For $n\ge1$ and $A,B\in M_n(R)$ over a commutative ring,
$$\det(AB)=\det(A)\det(B).$$
Let $D$ be an integral domain. A nonzero polynomial $f\in D[x]$ of degree $n$ has at most $n$ distinct roots in $D$.

Let $n\ge1$, let $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$A,B\in\mathbb F^{n\times n}$. The **matrix pencil** determined by $(A,B)$ is
$A-\lambda B$. Its determinant polynomial is
$f(\lambda)=\det(A-\lambda B)$, with real coefficients viewed as complex
coefficients when $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$. The pencil is **regular** if $f$ is
not the zero polynomial; otherwise it is **singular**.

For $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb C$ not both zero, put
$$p(\alpha,\beta)=\det(\beta A-\alpha B).$$
A **homogeneous generalized eigenvalue pair** is an equivalence class of such
pairs satisfying $p(\alpha,\beta)=0$, where $(\alpha,\beta)$ and
$(c\alpha,c\beta)$ represent the same pair for every $c\in\mathbb C\setminus
\{0\}$. If $\beta\ne0$, the associated finite generalized eigenvalue is
$\lambda=\alpha/\beta$; if $\beta=0$, the pair is an infinite generalized
eigenvalue. The pair $(0,0)$ is never an eigenvalue pair.
Write $\sigma(A,B)$ for the set of finite ratios $\alpha/\beta$ among these
homogeneous eigenvalue pairs.

The QZ results on this page assume a regular pencil. They make no assertion
about Kronecker structure or eigenvalues of a singular pencil.

derivations.claim: By [F1], the regular base DARE pencil has an $n+n$ stable/outside split, and the ordered representation [F2] puts the stable roots in the leading blocks and the outside roots in the trailing blocks. Write trailing diagonal pairs as $(s_i,t_i)$ and leading ones as $(p_j,q_j)$. Disjoint homogeneous roots give $p_jt_i-s_iq_j\ne0$ for every $i,j$, including $t_i=0$. In the system $S_{22}Y-ZS_{11}=C$, $T_{22}Y-ZT_{11}=D$, process rows $i=n,n-1,\ldots,1$ and within each row columns $j=1,\ldots,n$; upper triangularity makes all other terms involve already determined $Y_{kj}$ with $k>i$ or $Z_{i\ell}$ with $\ell<j$. The two unknowns $(Y_{ij},Z_{ij})$ have coefficient matrix $\begin{bmatrix}s_i&-p_j\\t_i&-q_j\end{bmatrix}$ with determinant $p_jt_i-s_iq_j\ne0$, so the lower-oriented generalized Sylvester map is bijective. Its minimum singular value [F3] is therefore $\gamma>0$, and its inverse norm is $\kappa=\gamma^{-1}$.

Define $C_Y=S_{11}+E_{11}+(S_{12}+E_{12})Y$ and $D_Y=T_{11}+F_{11}+(T_{12}+F_{12})Y$. Block multiplication gives $(S+E)[I;Y]=[I;Z]C_Y$ and $(T+F)[I;Y]=[I;Z]D_Y$ exactly when $\mathcal L(Y,Z)=(S_{22}Y-ZS_{11},T_{22}Y-ZT_{11})$ equals $(-E_{21}-E_{22}Y+ZE_{11}+Z(S_{12}+E_{12})Y,\,-F_{21}-F_{22}Y+ZF_{11}+Z(T_{12}+F_{12})Y)$. On the product radius-$r$ ball, the right side has norm at most $\delta+2\delta r+(h+\delta)r^2$: the constant pair is bounded by $\delta$, the two linear pairs by $\delta\|Y\|_F$ and $\delta\|Z\|_F$, and the quadratic pair by $(h+\delta)\|Z\|_F\|Y\|_F$. Splitting the quadratic difference into its $Y$ and $Z$ changes bounds the Lipschitz constant by $2\delta+2(h+\delta)r$. Applying $\mathcal L^{-1}$ gives a self-map and contraction under the stated inequalities; iteration from zero has geometrically summable increments, so completeness [F8] gives a limit in the closed ball, continuity gives a fixed point, and contraction gives uniqueness. For $r=2\kappa\delta$ and $\theta=\kappa\delta$, substitution gives self-map ratio $\kappa[\delta+2\delta r+(h+\delta)r^2]/r=1/2+2\theta+2\kappa h\theta+2\theta^2$ and contraction constant $2\theta+4\kappa h\theta+4\theta^2$; the displayed strict condition implies both. For $\delta=0$, the exact pair $Y=Z=0$ solves the graph equations.

Set $R_Y=\begin{bmatrix}I&0\\Y&I\end{bmatrix}$ and $L_Z=\begin{bmatrix}I&0\\-Z&I\end{bmatrix}$. They are invertible shears of determinant one, and the graph equations from step 2.1 give $L_Z(S+E)R_Y=\begin{bmatrix}C_Y&S_{12}+E_{12}\\0&A'\end{bmatrix}$ and $L_Z(T+F)R_Y=\begin{bmatrix}D_Y&T_{12}+F_{12}\\0&B'\end{bmatrix}$, where $A'=S_{22}+E_{22}-Z(S_{12}+E_{12})$ and $B'=T_{22}+F_{22}-Z(T_{12}+F_{12})$. Unitary invariance, $\|M\|_2\le\|M\|_F$ [F5], and submultiplicativity [F6] give $\|C_Y-S_{11}\|_2,\|A'-S_{22}\|_2\le a$ and $\|D_Y-T_{11}\|_2,\|B'-T_{22}\|_2\le b$. Every leading stable root is finite, so $T_{11}$ is invertible and $K_s=T_{11}^{-1}S_{11}$ is upper triangular with diagonal moduli below one. Every trailing outside root has nonzero first homogeneous coordinate, so $S_{22}$ is invertible and $K_u=S_{22}^{-1}T_{22}$ is upper triangular with diagonal moduli below one, including zero for infinity; thus both are Schur stable. By [F7], $W_j=\sum_{k\ge0}(K_j^*)^kK_j^k$ converges for $j=s,u$, is positive definite, and satisfies $W_j-K_j^*W_jK_j=I$. The two Neumann margins and [F12] make $D_Y,A'$ invertible with inverse norms at most $\|T_{11}^{-1}\|_2/(1-\|T_{11}^{-1}\|_2b)$ and $\|S_{22}^{-1}\|_2/(1-\|S_{22}^{-1}\|_2a)$. The identities $D_Y^{-1}C_Y-K_s=D_Y^{-1}[(C_Y-S_{11})-(D_Y-T_{11})K_s]$ and $A'^{-1}B'-K_u=A'^{-1}[(B'-T_{22})-(A'-S_{22})K_u]$ give exactly the stated $\epsilon_s,\epsilon_u$ bounds.

Put $P_Y=(I+Y^*Y)^{-1/2}$. Since $V=[U\ V_2]$ is unitary, $(U+V_2Y)^*(U+V_2Y)=I+Y^*Y$, so $\widehat U^*\widehat U=I$ and $U^*\widehat U=P_Y$. Therefore $(\widehat U-U)^*(\widehat U-U)=2(I-P_Y)$. The largest eigenvalue of $Y^*Y$ is $y^2$, so [F3], [F5], and [F9] give the exact norm $\|\widehat U-U\|_2=\beta(y)$. The scalar function $g(t)=t-2(1-(1+t)^{-1/2})$ has $g(0)=0$ and $g'(t)=1-(1+t)^{-3/2}\ge0$ for $t\ge0$, proving $\beta(y)\le y\le r$. Also $(I-UU^*)\widehat U=V_2YP_Y$, whose largest singular value is $y/\sqrt{1+y^2}$ by [F3] and [F5].

If $K$ is either quotient in step 3.1 and $\|H\|_2\le\epsilon$, then $W-(K+H)^*W(K+H)=I-(K^*WH+H^*WK+H^*WH)$. The subtracted Hermitian term has norm at most $\|W\|_2(2\|K\|_2\epsilon+\epsilon^2)<1$, so the left side is positive definite; an eigenvector of $K+H$ with eigenvalue $\lambda$ gives $(1-|\lambda|^2)v^*Wv>0$, hence $|\lambda|<1$. Applied to $D_Y^{-1}C_Y$ and $A'^{-1}B'$, this makes the leading perturbed roots finite and stable, and the trailing roots outside, with zero eigenvalues of $A'^{-1}B'$ representing infinity. The shears have determinant one, so [F13] preserves the homogeneous determinant under their left/right transformations; [F10] factors it across the diagonal blocks. Since $D_Y$ and $A'$ are invertible, both diagonal pencils are regular and their product is a regular pencil with the claimed $n+n$ root split. The regular base and perturbed determinant polynomials have finite root sets by [F14]; choose $\lambda_0\in\mathbb C$ outside their union. Put $\mathcal R=(N'-\lambda_0M')^{-1}M'$ for $N'=L_Z(S+E)R_Y$ and $M'=L_Z(T+F)R_Y$. Then $N'-\lambda M'=(N'-\lambda_0M')[I-(\lambda-\lambda_0)\mathcal R]$, so [F13] expresses the pencil determinant as a nonzero constant times $\det(I-(\lambda-\lambda_0)\mathcal R)$. Jordan form [F11] factors the latter into $\prod_j(1-(\lambda-\lambda_0)\mu_j)$ over the eigenvalues $\mu_j$ of $\mathcal R$, with algebraic multiplicity. Thus each finite root maps injectively to $\mu=1/(\lambda-\lambda_0)$, and the polynomial degree is the number of nonzero $\mu_j$, counted with algebraic multiplicity. Its homogeneous form is $\det(\beta N'-\alpha M')=\beta^{2n}\det(N'-(\alpha/\beta)M')$; by [F15], its multiplicity at $[1:0]$ is $2n$ minus that degree, exactly the multiplicity of the zero eigenvalue of $\mathcal R$. The matrix $\mathcal R$ is block upper triangular with diagonal blocks $(C_Y-\lambda_0D_Y)^{-1}D_Y$ and $(A'-\lambda_0B')^{-1}B'$, whose spectra are disjoint because their pencil-root groups are disjoint and the projective map is injective. For a generalized eigenvector $[x;y]$ belonging to a leading-block eigenvalue $\mu$, its trailing equation is $(\mathcal R_{22}-\mu I)^k y=0$; disjoint spectra force $y=0$. Conversely, Jordan form [F11] supplies a basis of generalized eigenvectors of the leading $n\times n$ block, which embed as $[x;0]$ and span exactly the full leading-root generalized eigenspace. Undoing the graph shears and unitary factors identifies this right subspace with $V[I;Y]$ and its matching left deflating graph with $Q[I;Z]$.

Write $\Delta U=\widehat U-U$. Under the strict chart margin, $\widehat U_1=U_1(I+U_1^{-1}\Delta U_1)$ and $\|U_1^{-1}\Delta U_1\|_2\le\|U_1^{-1}\|_2\beta(y)<1$. By [F12], $\widehat U_1$ is invertible and $\|\widehat U_1^{-1}\|_2\le(\|U_1^{-1}\|_2^{-1}-\beta(y))^{-1}$. Using $U_2=XU_1$ gives $\widehat U_2\widehat U_1^{-1}-X=(\Delta U_2-X\Delta U_1)\widehat U_1^{-1}$; [F6] yields the stated chart estimate. Since $\beta$ is increasing and $\beta(y)\le\beta(r)$, the stronger margin $\|U_1^{-1}\|_2\beta(r)<1$ gives the computable weaker bound. An independently rotated orthonormal basis of the same space is $\widehat U R_0$ for unitary $R_0$ and has the same chart because $(\widehat U_1R_0)^{-1}=R_0^{-1}\widehat U_1^{-1}$. The proof assumes no structure on $E,F$, so it gives no Riccati residual, symmetry, positivity, or post-symmetrization stability certificate.

As $\delta\to0$ with $r=2\kappa\delta$, $\theta\to0$, $a,b\to0$, and $\epsilon_s,\epsilon_u\to0$; hence the contraction, Neumann, and both Stein margins in the Statement hold for all sufficiently small $\delta$. If $U_1$ is invertible, also $\|U_1^{-1}\|_2\beta(r)<1$ for all sufficiently small $\delta$, so the computable chart margin holds. [given, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

No arbitrary Axiom of Choice is used: all constructions are finite-dimensional scans, norm-convergent series, or selections from complements of finite subsets of $\mathbb C$.

risk_review.notes: Reviewed all seven steps and fifteen suppliers, and LAPACK Users Guide nodes 102/104 for the two separation orientations. The lower-oriented paired map is inverted by bottom-up rows and left-right columns, with scalar determinant p_j t_i-s_i q_j nonzero even at infinity. Direct block graph equations give the stated self-map and Lipschitz bounds. Leading T11 and trailing S22 are invertible; separate Neumann and Stein margins retain both root groups. Homogeneous determinant/Jordan shift accounts for infinite multiplicity. Normalization gives beta(y) exactly; the physical chart bound retains its strict inverse-block margin. delta=0, singular A and independent basis rotations are handled. citations.quote:
Let $A\in F^{n\times n}$, $B\in F^{n\times m}$, $C\in F^{p\times n}$, $R=R^*\succ0$, $Q=C^*C$, and $G=BR^{-1}B^*$. Assume $(A,B)$ is continuously stabilizable and $(A,C)$ is continuously detectable, using [[def-lqr-stabilizability-and-detectability]]. Then the CARE of [[def-standard-continuous-and-discrete-riccati-equations]] has exactly one Hermitian positive-semidefinite solution $X$. Its closed-loop matrix $A_c=A-GX$ is Hurwitz, and for every initial state $x_0$ the infinite-horizon value
$$\inf_u\int_0^\infty\bigl(x(t)^*Qx(t)+u(t)^*Ru(t)\bigr)\,dt=x_0^*Xx_0$$
is attained by $u(t)=-R^{-1}B^*Xx(t)$. Controls are locally square-integrable and states are locally absolutely continuous solutions of $\dot x=Ax+Bu$. A finite value also forces the terminal term $x(T)^*Xx(T)$ to tend to zero; this transversality is proved below.

Let $A\in F^{n\times n}$, $B\in F^{n\times m}$, $C\in F^{p\times n}$, $R=R^*\succ0$, and $Q=C^*C$. Assume $(A,B)$ is discretely stabilizable and $(A,C)$ discretely detectable, using [[def-lqr-stabilizability-and-detectability]]. Then the DARE of [[def-standard-continuous-and-discrete-riccati-equations]] has exactly one Hermitian positive-semidefinite solution $X$. For the equivalent Riccati map $f(P)=Q+A^*P(I+GP)^{-1}A$, its finite-horizon iterates $P_0=0$, $P_{k+1}=f(P_k)$ satisfy $0\preceq P_k\uparrow X$. For all Hermitian positive-semidefinite $Y,Z$,
$$f(Y)-f(Z)=A_c(Y)^*(Y-Z)A_c(Z),\qquad A_c(Y)=(I+GY)^{-1}A.$$
The solution satisfies $R+B^*XB\succ0$, and its closed loop $A_c=A-B(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA$ is Schur stable. For each $x_0$, the infinite-horizon discrete cost
$$\inf_{(u_k)}\sum_{k=0}^\infty(x_k^*Qx_k+u_k^*Ru_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k,$$
over sequences with finite cost equals $x_0^*Xx_0$ and is attained by $u_k=-K_dx_k$. Singular $A$ is allowed throughout; no inverse of $A$ is used.

Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $A\in F^{n\times n}$, $B\in F^{n\times m}$, $C\in F^{p\times n}$, and $R=R^*\in F^{m\times m}$ be positive definite. Write $Q=C^*C$ and $G=BR^{-1}B^*$. The inverse $R^{-1}$ is well-defined: [[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]] supplies an invertible factor $R=LL^*$, so $R^{-1}=L^{-*}L^{-1}$. Thus $v^*Gv=\|L^{-1}B^*v\|_2^2\ge0$ and $v^*Qv=\|Cv\|_2^2\ge0$. The symbol $^*$ is transpose over $\mathbb R$ and conjugate transpose over $\mathbb C$.

The **continuous algebraic Riccati equation (CARE)** is
$$A^*X+XA-XGX+Q=0.$$
Its residual is $F_c(X)=A^*X+XA-XGX+Q$, its feedback is $K_c(X)=R^{-1}B^*X$, and its closed-loop matrix is $A_c(X)=A-BK_c(X)=A-GX$.

For $X=X^*\succeq0$, $S_X:=R+B^*XB$ is positive definite because
$v^*S_Xv=v^*Rv+(Bv)^*X(Bv)>0$ for every nonzero $v$. The **discrete
algebraic Riccati equation (DARE)** is
$$X=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA.$$
Its residual is $F_d(X)=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA-X$. Whenever $X=X^*$, the matrix $R+B^*XB$ is positive definite if $X\succeq0$. Its feedback and closed-loop matrix are
$$K_d(X)=(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA,\qquad A_c(X)=A-BK_d(X).$$
A CARE solution is **stabilizing** when it is Hermitian and $A_c(X)$ is Hurwitz. A DARE solution is **stabilizing** when it is Hermitian, $R+B^*XB\succ0$, and $A_c(X)$ is Schur stable. No inverse of $A$ is part of either definition.

For Hermitian $X$ with $S_X$ invertible, multiplication gives
$$(I+GX)^{-1}=I-BS_X^{-1}B^*X,\qquad X(I+GX)^{-1}=X-XB S_X^{-1}B^*X.$$
In either product, the additional coefficient of $B$ is
$R^{-1}-S_X^{-1}-S_X^{-1}(B^*XB)R^{-1}=0$, because
$S_X=R+B^*XB$. Thus the DARE is equivalently
$X=Q+A^*X(I+GX)^{-1}A$, and its closed-loop matrix is
$A_c(X)=(I+GX)^{-1}A$.

The associated homogeneous symplectic pencil is
$$N=\begin{bmatrix}A&0\\-Q&I\end{bmatrix},\qquad M=\begin{bmatrix}I&G\\0&A^*\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathcal P(\alpha,\beta)=\beta N-\alpha M.$$
The homogeneous-coordinate convention is that a finite eigenvalue
$\lambda$ is $[\alpha:\beta]=[\lambda:1]$ and $[1:0]$ denotes infinity.

Let $X\succeq0$ be the stabilizing CARE solution from [[thm-care-stabilizing-psd-solution-and-value]], let $G=BR^{-1}B^*$, and define
$$H=\begin{bmatrix}A&-G\\-Q&-A^*\end{bmatrix},\qquad A_c=A-GX.$$
Then
$$H\begin{bmatrix}I\\X\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}I\\X\end{bmatrix}A_c.$$
Moreover, $H$ has exactly $n$ eigenvalues in the open left half-plane and $n$ in the open right half-plane, none on the imaginary axis, and $\operatorname{Ran}\begin{bmatrix}I\\X\end{bmatrix}$ is its stable invariant subspace.

Let $X\succeq0$ be the stabilizing DARE solution, $G=BR^{-1}B^*$, and
$$N=\begin{bmatrix}A&0\\-Q&I\end{bmatrix},\qquad M=\begin{bmatrix}I&G\\0&A^*\end{bmatrix},\qquad A_c=A-B(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA.$$
Then
$$N\begin{bmatrix}I\\X\end{bmatrix}=M\begin{bmatrix}I\\X\end{bmatrix}A_c.$$
The pencil $(N,M)$ is regular. Its homogeneous determinant has n roots strictly inside the unit disk and n roots strictly outside the closed unit disk, with infinite roots counted in the latter group. Thus it has no unit-circle roots, even if $A$ is singular, and $\operatorname{Ran}\begin{bmatrix}I\\X\end{bmatrix}$ is its stable deflating graph.

For $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $A\in F^{m\times m}$, $B\in F^{n\times n}$ with $m,n\ge1$, define the Sylvester operator $\mathcal S_{A,B}:F^{m\times n}\to F^{m\times n}$ by

$$\mathcal S_{A,B}(X)=AX+XB.$$

Equip $F^{m\times n}$ with the Frobenius norm of [[def-frobenius-matrix-norm]]. The column-vectorization isometry of [[lem-sylvester-vectorization-isometry-and-kronecker-identity]] identifies this norm with the Euclidean norm on $F^{mn}$. Define

$$\operatorname{sep}(A,-B):=\sigma_{\min}(\mathcal S_{A,B})=\min_{\|X\|_F=1}\|AX+XB\|_F.$$

Here $\sigma_{\min}$ denotes the smallest singular value of the finite-dimensional linear map under these inner products. The finite-dimensional singular value decomposition [[thm-singular-value-decomposition]] ensures this minimum is well-defined. The argument $-B$ is part of the conventional label: the operator being measured is $X\mapsto AX+XB$.

Let $\widehat X=\widehat X^*$ be a CARE candidate, $\widehat A_c=A-G\widehat X$, and
$$\mathcal L(E)=\widehat A_c^*E+E\widehat A_c,\qquad F_c(X)=A^*X+XA-XGX+Q.$$
Assume $\widehat A_c$ is certified Hurwitz, $\mathcal L$ is invertible on Hermitian matrices, and outward-verified bounds satisfy
$$\kappa\ge\|\mathcal L^{-1}\|_{F\to F},\quad r\ge\|F_c(\widehat X)\|_F,\quad g\ge\|G\|_2,$$
with $\rho>0$ such that
$$\kappa(r+g\rho^2)\le\rho,\qquad 2\kappa g\rho<1.$$
Then there is exactly one Hermitian CARE root in the closed Frobenius ball $\|X-\widehat X\|_F\le\rho$.

If also a verified Hermitian $W\succ0$ and $\gamma>0$ satisfy
$$-(\widehat A_c^*W+W\widehat A_c)\succeq\gamma I,\qquad 2\|W\|_2g\rho<\gamma,$$
then that root is Hurwitz-stabilizing. Under the standard CARE hypotheses of [[thm-care-stabilizing-psd-solution-and-value]], it is the unique stabilizing positive-semidefinite solution.

Let $\widehat X=\widehat X^*$ be a DARE candidate, $S(X)=R+B^*XB$, $K(X)=S(X)^{-1}B^*XA$, $A_c(X)=A-BK(X)$, and let
$$F_d(X)=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB S(X)^{-1}B^*XA-X.$$
Suppose $S(\widehat X)\succeq\delta_0I$ is outward-certified. For a proposed radius $\rho>0$ put
$$a=\|A\|_2,\quad b=\|B\|_2,\quad m=\|\widehat X\|_F+\rho,\quad \delta=\delta_0-b^2\rho.$$
Require $\delta>0$ and define
$$L_K=\frac{ab}{\delta}+\frac{ab^3m}{\delta^2},\quad M_c=a+\frac{ab^2m}{\delta},\quad L_c=bL_K,\quad L_D=2M_cL_c.$$
Let $D(E)=A_c(\widehat X)^*EA_c(\widehat X)-E$ be invertible on Hermitian matrices, with outward-certified $\kappa\ge\|D^{-1}\|_{F\to F}$ and $r\ge\|F_d(\widehat X)\|_F$. If
$$\kappa(r+L_D\rho^2/2)\le\rho,\qquad \kappa L_D\rho<1,$$
there is exactly one Hermitian DARE root in the closed Frobenius $\rho$-ball, and $R+B^*XB\succeq\delta I$ throughout that ball.

For the stabilizing branch, additionally suppose $\widehat A_c=A_c(\widehat X)$ is Schur stable and an outward-certified $W\succ0$ satisfies
$$W-\widehat A_c^*W\widehat A_c\succeq\gamma I.$$
If, with $\eta=L_c\rho$,
$$\|W\|_2(2M_c\eta+\eta^2)<\gamma,$$
then the root is Schur-stabilizing. Under the standard DARE hypotheses of [[thm-dare-stabilizing-psd-solution-and-value]], it is the unique stabilizing positive-semidefinite solution.

Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $m,n\ge1$, $A\in F^{m\times m}$ and $B\in F^{n\times n}$. Spectra of real matrices are taken over $\mathbb C$. The map $\mathcal S_{A,B}$ of [[def-sylvester-operator-and-separation-number]] is invertible if and only if

$$
\sigma(A)\cap(-\sigma(B))=\varnothing.
$$

Equivalently, for every $C\in F^{m\times n}$, the equation $AX+XB=C$ has a unique solution if and only if this spectral condition holds. The same condition is equivalent to $\operatorname{sep}(A,-B)>0$.

Let $X$ be a normed space over $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and assume
$X$ admits an ordered basis of finite length. Then $X$ is a Banach space in the
sense of [[def-banach-space]].

Let $M\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ be Schur stable and let $r$ satisfy $\rho(M)<r<1$. For the Euclidean induced operator norm there is a finite $C_r$ such that
$$\|M^k\|_2\le C_r r^k\qquad(k\ge0).$$
For a real matrix, interpret the same statement on its complexification.

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces,

$$\lVert ST\rVert\le \lVert S\rVert\,\lVert T\rVert.$$

For every such linear map $T$,

$$\lVert T^*T\rVert=\lVert T\rVert^2.$$

Let $A\in F^{n\times n}$ be Hurwitz and let $Q=Q^*\in F^{n\times n}$. Then the improper matrix integral

$$
X=\int_0^\infty e^{tA}Qe^{tA^*}\,dt
$$

converges and is the unique solution of $AX+XA^*+Q=0$. If $Q\succeq0$, then $X\succeq0$. If $Q\succ0$, then $X\succ0$. For $Q\succeq0$, $X\succ0$ if and only if there is no nonzero $v$ for which $e^{tA^*}v\in\ker Q^{1/2}$ for every $t\ge0$.

Let $(N,M)$ be the order-$2n$ DARE pencil in [[prop-dare-symplectic-pencil-graph-and-stable-spectrum]], with $n\ge1$. Work over $\mathbb C$, also for real input. Suppose exact unitary matrices $Q,V$ give an ordered complex generalized Schur pair
$$Q^*NV=S=\begin{bmatrix}S_{11}&S_{12}\\0&S_{22}\end{bmatrix},\qquad Q^*MV=T=\begin{bmatrix}T_{11}&T_{12}\\0&T_{22}\end{bmatrix},$$
where each diagonal block has order $n$, all four diagonal blocks are upper triangular, the leading homogeneous roots are strictly inside the unit disk, and the trailing roots are strictly outside its closure, including infinity. This ordered representation is an explicit input; existence of an unordered generalized Schur form is not an ordering certificate.

Give pairs of $n\times n$ matrices the product Frobenius norm
$$\|(Y,Z)\|_P=(\|Y\|_F^2+\|Z\|_F^2)^{1/2},$$
and define the lower-oriented generalized Sylvester separation
$$\gamma=\min_{\|(Y,Z)\|_P=1}\|(S_{22}Y-ZS_{11},T_{22}Y-ZT_{11})\|_P.$$
Then $\gamma>0$. Write $\kappa=\gamma^{-1}$, $h=(\|S_{12}\|_2^2+\|T_{12}\|_2^2)^{1/2}$. For arbitrary pencil perturbations $\Delta_N,\Delta_M$, put $E=Q^*\Delta_NV$, $F=Q^*\Delta_MV$, and $\delta=(\|E\|_F^2+\|F\|_F^2)^{1/2}=(\|\Delta_N\|_F^2+\|\Delta_M\|_F^2)^{1/2}$. If $r>0$ satisfies
$$\kappa[\delta+2\delta r+(h+\delta)r^2]\le r,\qquad \kappa[2\delta+2(h+\delta)r]<1,$$
there is a unique pair $(Y,Z)$ in the product radius-$r$ ball for which the right and left graphs $V[I;Y]$ and $Q[I;Z]$ form matching deflating spaces of the perturbed pair. In particular $\|Y\|_F,\|Z\|_F\le r$. For $\delta>0$, a sufficient choice is $r=2\kappa\delta$ whenever, with $\theta=\kappa\delta$,
$$4\theta+4\kappa h\theta+4\theta^2<1.$$
For $\delta=0$, take $Y=Z=0$.

Here are separate sufficient margins identifying these graphs as the stable spaces. Set
$$a=\delta+(\|S_{12}\|_2+\delta)r,\qquad b=\delta+(\|T_{12}\|_2+\delta)r,$$
$$K_s=T_{11}^{-1}S_{11},\qquad K_u=S_{22}^{-1}T_{22}.$$
The inverses exist and $K_s,K_u$ are Schur stable. For $j=s,u$, choose $W_j\succ0$ with $W_j-K_j^*W_jK_j=I$; the convergent Stein series supplies such a matrix. Require
$$\|T_{11}^{-1}\|_2b<1,\qquad \|S_{22}^{-1}\|_2a<1,$$
and define
$$\epsilon_s=\frac{\|T_{11}^{-1}\|_2(a+b\|K_s\|_2)}{1-\|T_{11}^{-1}\|_2b},\qquad \epsilon_u=\frac{\|S_{22}^{-1}\|_2(b+a\|K_u\|_2)}{1-\|S_{22}^{-1}\|_2a}.$$
If
$$\|W_j\|_2(2\|K_j\|_2\epsilon_j+\epsilon_j^2)<1\qquad(j=s,u),$$
then the perturbed pencil is regular, has precisely $n$ stable roots and $n$ outside roots, and the constructed right graph is its stable deflating space. For fixed ordered input these margins hold for all sufficiently small $\delta$ with $r=2\kappa\delta$.

For normalized right bases, write $V=[U\ V_2]$ and
$$\widehat U=(U+V_2Y)(I+Y^*Y)^{-1/2},\qquad y=\|Y\|_2,\qquad \beta(y)=\sqrt{2\left(1-\frac1{\sqrt{1+y^2}}\right)}.$$
Then $\widehat U^*\widehat U=I$, $\|\widehat U-U\|_2=\beta(y)\le y\le r$, and
$$\|(I-UU^*)\widehat U\|_2=\frac{y}{\sqrt{1+y^2}}.$$
If the physical top block $U_1$ of $U=[U_1;U_2]$ is invertible, $X=U_2U_1^{-1}$, and $\|U_1^{-1}\|_2\beta(y)<1$, then $\widehat U_1$ is invertible and
$$\|\widehat U_2\widehat U_1^{-1}-X\|_2\le\frac{(1+\|X\|_2)\beta(y)}{\|U_1^{-1}\|_2^{-1}-\beta(y)}.$$
For the directly computable bound with $\beta(r)$, impose the stronger margin $\|U_1^{-1}\|_2\beta(r)<1$; replacing $\beta(y)$ by $\beta(r)$ then gives a valid weaker estimate. An independently rotated orthonormal basis of the same perturbed space produces the identical chart, so it need not be close to $U$ before alignment. The conclusion concerns an unstructured perturbed pencil; it does not certify Hermitian symmetry, Riccati residual, positive data, or the stabilizing Riccati branch after symmetrization.

derivations.claim: By [F3], expanding the CARE polynomial at a Hermitian $X$ gives $F_c(X+E)-F_c(X)=\mathcal L_c^X(E)-EGE,$ where $\mathcal L_c^X(E)=(A-GX)^*E+E(A-GX)$. For the DARE, set $f(X)=Q+A^*X(I+GX)^{-1}A$. Direct multiplication gives $\Phi_G(X+E)-\Phi_G(X)=(I+(X+E)G)^{-1}E(I+GX)^{-1},\quad \Phi_G(X)=X(I+GX)^{-1}.$ Taking the derivative at $E=0$ and multiplying by $A^*,A$ gives $Df(X)[E]=A_c(X)^*EA_c(X)$; since $F_d=f-X$, this gives $DF_d(X)[E]=A_c(X)^*EA_c(X)-E$.

Apply [F14] to the exact ordered unitary DARE pencil representation and the supplied perturbations of both pencil matrices. Its paired generalized Sylvester operator and contraction inequalities give the radius-$r$ right and left deflating graphs; its separate Neumann and Stein margins establish the perturbed stable split. Its normalized basis construction gives distance at most $\beta(r)\le r$, and its computable physical chart estimate retains the inverse graph-block norm and the strict margin $\|U_1^{-1}\|_2\beta(r)<1$. No part of this conclusion follows from QZ backward error alone.

For a CARE additive residual perturbation $\Delta$, write $X=X_c+E$ and let $\delta=\|\Delta\|_F$. Then $F_c(X_c)=0$ and step 1.1 makes the perturbed root equation equivalent to $E=-\mathcal L_c^{-1}\Delta+\mathcal L_c^{-1}(EGE).$ If $\rho$ satisfies $\kappa_c(\delta+\|G\|_2\rho^2)\le\rho$ and $2\kappa_c\|G\|_2\rho<1$, the map sends the closed radius-$\rho$ Hermitian ball to itself and has Lipschitz constant at most the second displayed quantity. Iteration from zero gives geometric successive differences; [F10] gives a limit in the ball, continuity gives a fixed point, and contraction gives uniqueness. Let $W_c=\int_0^\infty e^{tA_c^*}e^{tA_c}\,dt\succ0$; then $A_c^*W_c+W_cA_c=-I$. If also $2\|W_c\|_2\|G\|_2\rho<1$, then $\|EGW_c+W_cGE\|_2\le2\|W_c\|_2\|G\|_2\rho<1$. Hence $(A_c-GE)^*W_c+W_c(A_c-GE)\prec0$; an eigenvector $v$ with eigenvalue $\lambda$ gives $2\operatorname{Re}(\lambda)v^*W_cv<0$, so the perturbed loop is Hurwitz. For DARE, [F2] gives Schur stability and [F11] gives the Stein inverse $\mathcal L_d^{-1}(Y)=-\sum_{k\ge0}(A_c^*)^kYA_c^k$. On a sufficiently small ball, $S(X)=R+B^*XB\succeq\delta_S I$, where $\delta_S=\lambda_{\min}S(X_d)-b^2\rho>0$. Put $a=\|A\|_2$, $b=\|B\|_2$, and $m=\|X_d\|_F+\rho$. The resolvent identity gives $\|S(X)^{-1}\|_2\le\delta_S^{-1}$ and $\|S(X)^{-1}-S(Y)^{-1}\|_2\le b^2\delta_S^{-2}\|X-Y\|_F$. Splitting $K(X)-K(Y)$ into its $X$ and inverse-factor changes yields $\|K(X)-K(Y)\|_F\le L_K\|X-Y\|_F$, where $L_K=ab/\delta_S+ab^3m/\delta_S^2$; hence $\|A_c(X)\|_2\le M_c=a+ab^2m/\delta_S$ and $\|A_c(X)-A_c(Y)\|_2\le L_c\|X-Y\|_F$, $L_c=bL_K$. Since $DF_d(X)[E]=A_c(X)^*EA_c(X)-E$, subtraction gives $\|DF_d(X)-DF_d(Y)\|_{F\to F}\le2M_cL_c\|X-Y\|_F=:L_D\|X-Y\|_F$. Integrating this derivative along line segments gives $R(E)=F_d(X_d+E)-F_d(X_d)-\mathcal L_d(E)$ with $\|R(E)\|_F\le L_D\|E\|_F^2/2$ and $\|R(E)-R(F)\|_F\le L_D\rho\|E-F\|_F$ on the ball. Thus $E=-\mathcal L_d^{-1}(\Delta+R(E))$ is a self-map when $\kappa_d(\delta+L_D\rho^2/2)\le\rho$ and a contraction when $\kappa_d L_D\rho<1$. The same completeness argument gives its unique local root. For a separate stability margin, take $W_d=\sum_{k\ge0}(A_c^*)^kA_c^k\succ0$, so $W_d-A_c^*W_dA_c=I$ by [F11]. Put $\eta=L_c\rho$. Expanding the Stein form bounds its change by $\|W_d\|_2(2M_c\eta+\eta^2)$; choose $\rho$ so this is below $1$. Then $W_d-A_c(X)^*W_dA_c(X)\succ0$, and an eigenvector gives $(1-|\lambda|^2)v^*W_dv>0$, so the perturbed loop is Schur stable. For sufficiently small $\delta>0$, take $\rho=2\kappa_c\delta$ in CARE when $\|G\|_2>0$; the contraction and stability inequalities hold for small enough $\delta$, giving $\|E\|_F=O(\delta)$. If $G=0$, the equation is linear and this order bound is exact. In DARE, take $\rho=2\kappa_d\delta$ when $L_D>0$; for sufficiently small $\delta$ this satisfies the self-map, contraction, $S(X)\succ0$, and Stein-margin bounds, again giving $\|E\|_F=O(\delta)$. If $L_D=0$, the local equation is linear. The remainders are therefore $O(\delta^2)$, proving the first-order terms $-\mathcal L_c^{-1}\Delta$ and $-\mathcal L_d^{-1}\Delta$.

Put $T_X=[I\ 0;X_c\ I]$. Multiplying the Hamiltonian in [F4] on the right by $T_X$ and then on the left by $T_X^{-1}=[I\ 0;-X_c\ I]$, and using the CARE identity in [F3], gives $T_X^{-1}HT_X=\begin{bmatrix}A_c&-G\\0&-A_c^*\end{bmatrix}.$ The Sylvester map $\mathcal S(Y)=-A_c^*Y-YA_c$ has smallest singular value $\sigma=\operatorname{sep}(-A_c^*,A_c)>0$: [F9] applies because $\sigma(-A_c^*)$ lies in the right half-plane while $-\sigma(-A_c)=\sigma(A_c)$ lies in the left half-plane; [F6] gives inverse norm $\kappa_s=1/\sigma$. In the perturbed coordinates, write $Z=[Z_{ij}]$ and seek an invariant graph $[I;Y]$. Its lower-block graph equation is $-A_c^*Y-YA_c+Z_{21}+Z_{22}Y-YZ_{11}+YGY-YZ_{12}Y=0.$ Hence $Y$ is a fixed point of $\mathcal T(Y)=-\mathcal S^{-1}(Z_{21}+Z_{22}Y-YZ_{11}+YGY-YZ_{12}Y).$ On the Frobenius ball $\|Y\|_F\le2\theta$, each block norm of $Z$ is at most $\zeta$. The map norm is at most $\kappa_s[\zeta+2\zeta\|Y\|_F+(\|G\|_2+\zeta)\|Y\|_F^2]$, hence at most $\theta+4\theta^2+4\mu\theta^2+4\theta^3\le2\theta$ under the displayed smallness condition. Its Lipschitz constant is at most $2\theta+4\mu\theta+4\theta^2<1$. Completeness [F10] and iteration therefore give a unique fixed point in the ball. Returning through $T_X$ turns $[I;Y]$ into $[I;X_c+Y]$, proving the graph bound. Under [A2], the restriction has $n$ stable eigenvalues and the perturbed matrix has exactly $n$ stable eigenvalues in total. In a basis beginning with this invariant graph, the perturbed matrix is block upper triangular with this stable restriction as its first diagonal block; the quotient block therefore has no stable eigenvalues. A stable generalized eigenvector must project to a stable generalized eigenvector of the quotient, which is impossible, so every stable generalized eigenspace lies in the graph. Both spaces have dimension $n$, hence the graph is the stable spectral subspace.

Since $\widetilde U_1=U_1+\Delta U_1=U_1(I+U_1^{-1}\Delta U_1)$ and $\|U_1^{-1}\Delta U_1\|_2<1$, the Neumann geometric series makes the second factor invertible and gives $\|\widetilde U_1^{-1}\|_2\le(\|U_1^{-1}\|_2^{-1}-\|\Delta U_1\|_2)^{-1}$. Using $U_2=XU_1$, $\widetilde U_2\widetilde U_1^{-1}-X=(\Delta U_2-X\Delta U_1)\widetilde U_1^{-1}.$ Submultiplicativity [F12] proves the displayed basis-chart bound. This derivation uses only the graph equation, so it applies to both the CARE invariant graph and the DARE deflating graph; it does not convert a pencil backward error into a deflating-subspace error.

Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $A\in F^{n\times n}$, $B\in F^{n\times m}$, $C\in F^{p\times n}$, and $R=R^*\in F^{m\times m}$ be positive definite. Write $Q=C^*C$ and $G=BR^{-1}B^*$. The inverse $R^{-1}$ is well-defined: [[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]] supplies an invertible factor $R=LL^*$, so $R^{-1}=L^{-*}L^{-1}$. Thus $v^*Gv=\|L^{-1}B^*v\|_2^2\ge0$ and $v^*Qv=\|Cv\|_2^2\ge0$. The symbol $^*$ is transpose over $\mathbb R$ and conjugate transpose over $\mathbb C$.

The **continuous algebraic Riccati equation (CARE)** is
$$A^*X+XA-XGX+Q=0.$$
Its residual is $F_c(X)=A^*X+XA-XGX+Q$, its feedback is $K_c(X)=R^{-1}B^*X$, and its closed-loop matrix is $A_c(X)=A-BK_c(X)=A-GX$.

For $X=X^*\succeq0$, $S_X:=R+B^*XB$ is positive definite because
$v^*S_Xv=v^*Rv+(Bv)^*X(Bv)>0$ for every nonzero $v$. The **discrete
algebraic Riccati equation (DARE)** is
$$X=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA.$$
Its residual is $F_d(X)=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA-X$. Whenever $X=X^*$, the matrix $R+B^*XB$ is positive definite if $X\succeq0$. Its feedback and closed-loop matrix are
$$K_d(X)=(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA,\qquad A_c(X)=A-BK_d(X).$$
A CARE solution is **stabilizing** when it is Hermitian and $A_c(X)$ is Hurwitz. A DARE solution is **stabilizing** when it is Hermitian, $R+B^*XB\succ0$, and $A_c(X)$ is Schur stable. No inverse of $A$ is part of either definition.

For Hermitian $X$ with $S_X$ invertible, multiplication gives
$$(I+GX)^{-1}=I-BS_X^{-1}B^*X,\qquad X(I+GX)^{-1}=X-XB S_X^{-1}B^*X.$$
In either product, the additional coefficient of $B$ is
$R^{-1}-S_X^{-1}-S_X^{-1}(B^*XB)R^{-1}=0$, because
$S_X=R+B^*XB$. Thus the DARE is equivalently
$X=Q+A^*X(I+GX)^{-1}A$, and its closed-loop matrix is
$A_c(X)=(I+GX)^{-1}A$.

The associated homogeneous symplectic pencil is
$$N=\begin{bmatrix}A&0\\-Q&I\end{bmatrix},\qquad M=\begin{bmatrix}I&G\\0&A^*\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathcal P(\alpha,\beta)=\beta N-\alpha M.$$
The homogeneous-coordinate convention is that a finite eigenvalue
$\lambda$ is $[\alpha:\beta]=[\lambda:1]$ and $[1:0]$ denotes infinity.

derivations.claim: Substitution gives $2X-X^2+1=0$, or $(X-1)^2=2$. The two real roots are $X_+=1+\sqrt2$ and $X_-=1-\sqrt2$.
The corresponding closed-loop scalars are $1-X_+=-\sqrt2<0$ and $1-X_-=\sqrt2>0$. Thus $X_+$ is the only stabilizing branch; it is positive, whereas the other root is negative and unstable.

Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $n,m,p\ge1$, $A\in F^{n\times n}$, $B\in F^{n\times m}$, and $C\in F^{p\times n}$. A matrix is **Hurwitz** when every complex eigenvalue has strictly negative real part, as in [[def-hurwitz-matrix-and-continuous-lyapunov-equation]]. It is **Schur stable** when every complex eigenvalue has modulus strictly less than one.

The pair $(A,B)$ is **continuously stabilizable** if some $K\in F^{m\times n}$ makes $A-BK$ Hurwitz. The pair $(A,C)$ is **continuously detectable** if some $L\in F^{n\times p}$ makes $A-LC$ Hurwitz.

The pair $(A,B)$ is **discretely stabilizable** if some $K\in F^{m\times n}$ makes $A-BK$ Schur stable. The pair $(A,C)$ is **discretely detectable** if some $L\in F^{n\times p}$ makes $A-LC$ Schur stable. These are exact existential properties of the given finite matrices. A residual size or an approximate spectral estimate does not itself establish any of them.

Let $A\in F^{n\times n}$, $B\in F^{n\times m}$, $C\in F^{p\times n}$, $R=R^*\succ0$, $Q=C^*C$, and $G=BR^{-1}B^*$. Assume $(A,B)$ is continuously stabilizable and $(A,C)$ is continuously detectable, using [[def-lqr-stabilizability-and-detectability]]. Then the CARE of [[def-standard-continuous-and-discrete-riccati-equations]] has exactly one Hermitian positive-semidefinite solution $X$. Its closed-loop matrix $A_c=A-GX$ is Hurwitz, and for every initial state $x_0$ the infinite-horizon value
$$\inf_u\int_0^\infty\bigl(x(t)^*Qx(t)+u(t)^*Ru(t)\bigr)\,dt=x_0^*Xx_0$$
is attained by $u(t)=-R^{-1}B^*Xx(t)$. Controls are locally square-integrable and states are locally absolutely continuous solutions of $\dot x=Ax+Bu$. A finite value also forces the terminal term $x(T)^*Xx(T)$ to tend to zero; this transversality is proved below.

derivations.claim: First take $A=C=R=1$ and $B=0$. Then $Q=1$; every feedback leaves $A-BK=1$, so the pair is not stabilizable. The CARE is $2X+1=0$, whose only root is $X=-1/2$; it is not positive semidefinite and its closed loop remains $1$.

Next take $A=B=R=1$ and $C=0$, so $Q=0$. The pair is stabilizable, since $K=2$ gives $A-BK=-1$, but it is not detectable because $A-LC=1$ for every $L$. The CARE is $2X-X^2=0$, with positive-semidefinite roots $X=0$ and $X=2$; the first has unstable closed loop $1$ and the second stable closed loop $-1$. Since $Q=0$, zero control has zero cost for every initial state, so the value is zero rather than the stabilizing root $X=2$. Thus without detectability uniqueness among PSD roots and the stabilizing value conclusion in [F3] fail.

derivations.claim: The scalar CARE is $2\varepsilon X-X^2+\varepsilon^2=0$, with positive root $X_*=(1+\sqrt2)\varepsilon$ and stable closed loop $A_c(X_*)=-\sqrt2\varepsilon$. At the candidate, $\widehat A_c=-0.1\varepsilon<0$, the exact residual is $r=|F_c(\widehat X)|=1.99\varepsilon^2=1.99\cdot10^{-16}$, and $g=1$.

The scalar Lyapunov derivative is $\mathcal L(E)=2\widehat A_c E=-0.2\varepsilon E$, so its inverse norm is $\kappa=1/(0.2\varepsilon)=5\cdot10^8$. For every $\rho>0$, $r+\rho^2\ge2\sqrt r\,\rho$, so $\kappa(r+\rho^2)\ge2\kappa\sqrt r\,\rho>\rho$ because $2\kappa\sqrt r>14$. Thus no radius satisfies even the self-map condition, despite the absolute residual being below $2\cdot10^{-16}$ and the exact stabilizing root existing. The residual alone is inconclusive because the inverse Lyapunov factor is large near the imaginary axis.

Inputs are CARE data with $Q=C^*C\succeq0$, $R\succ0$, a supplied stabilizing gain $K_0$, a nonnegative integer outer budget $N$, and either exact or safeguarded-inexact solve mode. Each exact-mode pass takes an admissible control packet for [[alg-bartels-stewart-sylvester-equation]]: pivot threshold $\tau_{\rm BS}\ge0$, a fixed $c_0>0$, nonnegative integer Schur sweep budgets $N_A,N_B\le c_0n$, and Schur controls for each coefficient matrix (deflation tolerance, positive integer stagnation period, finite exceptional-shift tables, arithmetic/range controls, and any supplied encoding or evaluator). Use its bounded-controller mode with a supplied nonnegative integer instruction budget $K_{\rm BS}$ and its built-in discriminant-sign controller. In inexact mode, also supply a nonnegative integer line-search limit $L$; each pass takes a Hermitian proposal $\widetilde P_j$, a stored candidate $\widehat X_j$ and approximate inverses for the finite Lyapunov systems below, and finite factorization witnesses for each trial. Stored inputs and point-solve proposals in this mode are exact dyadics; derived gains and coefficients are retained as exact rational expressions. Every point call uses the operationwise controller of [[alg-point-verified-linear-system-certifier]]; every scalar enclosure uses a finite outward evaluator with a declared work budget. Write $S(K)=Q+K^*RK$ and $\mathcal L_A(P)=A^*P+PA$.

For $j=0,\ldots,N-1$, put $A_j=A-BK_j$. In exact mode, call [[alg-bartels-stewart-sylvester-equation]] with coefficient matrices $A_j^*,A_j$, right-hand side $-S(K_j)$, and that pass's complete control packet to solve
$$\mathcal L_{A_j}(X_j)=-S(K_j).$$
If it does not return success, stop with its status. Otherwise set $K_{j+1}=R^{-1}B^*X_j$, append the gain and residual, and continue.

In safeguarded-inexact mode, $X_j$ denotes the unique exact solution of $\mathcal L_{A_j}(X_j)=-S(K_j)$; it exists because $K_0$ is stabilizing and every previously accepted trial has a Hurwitz witness. Under column vectorization, use the point matrix $I_n\otimes A_j^*+A_j^T\otimes I_n$ for $\mathcal L_{A_j}$, as in [[lem-sylvester-vectorization-isometry-and-kronecker-identity]]. Before the current-cost point call, clear a common positive integer denominator $d_j$ from this exact rational coefficient matrix and from $-\operatorname{vec}(S(K_j))$. Call [[alg-point-verified-linear-system-certifier]] on the resulting dyadic system, with the supplied inverse proposal for the scaled coefficient and $\widehat X_j$ as the solution proposal. Scaling both sides by $d_j$ preserves the exact solution $X_j$; if the scaled entries cannot be stored exactly in the declared point format, return `range-failure`. A `range-failure` returns that status; an `inconclusive` result returns `safeguard-inconclusive`. Let its solution ball have center $\widehat X_j$ and radius $s_j$, replacing the center by its Hermitian part if needed. Set $D_j=\widetilde P_j-\widehat X_j$ and compute the outward Gershgorin upper bound
$$\eta_j=s_j+\max_i\left((D_j)_{ii}+\sum_{k\ne i}|(D_j)_{ik}|\right).$$
For Hermitian $D_j$, the maximum row bound above is at least $\lambda_{\max}(D_j)$, by applying the eigenvector equation at a coordinate of maximal modulus. Define $\widetilde K_j=R^{-1}B^*\widetilde P_j$ and inspect the finite line-search list $\theta_\ell=2^{-\ell}$, $0\le\ell\le L$. For each trial $K_\ell=K_j+\theta_\ell(\widetilde K_j-K_j)$, let $A_\ell=A-BK_\ell$ and use its supplied exact factor witnesses $W_\ell=L_\ell^*L_\ell$ with nonsingular $L_\ell$, and $Z_\ell$ satisfying
$$A_\ell^*W_\ell+W_\ell A_\ell\preceq-\mu_\ell I,$$
where $\mu_\ell>0$ and $-A_\ell^*W_\ell-W_\ell A_\ell-\mu_\ell I=Z_\ell^*Z_\ell$. Verify these exact factor identities; otherwise reject the trial and continue. Vectorize $\mathcal L_{A_\ell}$ using the same coefficient matrix as for $A_j$. Outward-evaluate $I-R_\ell\mathcal L_{A_\ell}$ and let $q_\ell$ be a Frobenius upper bound. If no finite enclosure is available or $q_\ell\ge1$, reject the trial and continue. Set $\kappa_\ell=\|R_\ell\|_F/(1-q_\ell)$; the Neumann estimate and $\|T\|_2\le\|T\|_F$ give $\kappa_\ell\ge\|\mathcal L_{A_\ell}^{-1}\|_{F\to F}$. Separately outward-evaluate the raw residual and set $r_\ell$ to an upper bound for
$$\mathcal L_{A_\ell}(\widetilde P_j)+Q+K_\ell^*RK_\ell,$$
with Frobenius norm. Accept the first trial satisfying $\eta_j+\kappa_\ell r_\ell\le0$; then set $K_{j+1}=K_\ell$, append the accepted gain and its certificates, and proceed to pass $j+1$. If no trial passes, return `safeguard-inconclusive` without changing $K_j$. Any unavailable outward bound is inconclusive. The inverse bound above follows from the Neumann estimate, and $r_\ell$ bounds the raw residual separately; the preconditioned residual in [[def-verified-linear-residual-certificate-data]] is a different quantity. All certificate witnesses and bounds use the finite outward evaluator; a non-finite operation returns its range status. After at most $N$ accepted updates return the gain sequence, solve residuals, cost-matrix data and terminal status. An arbitrary approximate Lyapunov solve is never accepted without the separate stability and descent checks above.

Consider a trial gain $K_t$ in the safeguarded-inexact branch of [[alg-finite-budget-newton-kleinman-policy-iteration]], with $A_t=A-BK_t$. Suppose outward certificates give $W\succ0$, $\mu>0$, $A_t^*W+WA_t\preceq-\mu I$, an inverse bound $\kappa\ge\|\mathcal L_{A_t}^{-1}\|_{F\to F}$, a residual bound $r$ for a Hermitian approximation $\widetilde P$ to
$$A_t^*P+PA_t+Q+K_t^*RK_t=0,$$
and an upper bound $\eta\ge\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde P-X_j)$ with $\eta+\kappa r\le0$. Then $A_t$ is Hurwitz, its exact cost matrix $P_t$ exists and is positive semidefinite, and $P_t\preceq X_j$. Thus every accepted line-search step preserves stability and does not increase the exact closed-loop cost matrix.

derivations.claim: At $K_0=2$, the closed loop is $-1$ and the exact Lyapunov equation gives $-2X_0+5=0$, hence $X_0=5/2$ and $K_1=5/2$. The next closed loop is $-3/2$, and its policy equation gives $-3X_1+1+25/4=0$, hence $X_1=29/12<5/2$.

Consider instead an unchecked approximate policy value $\widetilde P=0$, which proposes $\widetilde K=0$. A full step gives closed loop $A-B\widetilde K=1$, which is unstable. More generally, a line-search trial between $K_0=2$ and $0$ has $K\in[0,2]$. If $K\le1$ its closed loop $1-K$ is not Hurwitz. If $1<K<2$, its exact cost matrix is $P(K)=(1+K^2)/(2(K-1))$, and $P(K)-\frac52=\frac{(K-2)(K-3)}{2(K-1)}>0.$ Thus every nonzero trial either loses stability or increases cost; the certified safeguard rejects it.

citations.quote:
Input $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, dimensions $n,m,p\ge1$, standard DARE data $A\in F^{n\times n}$, $B\in F^{n\times m}$, $C\in F^{p\times n}$, and $R\in F^{m\times m}$ with $R=R^*\succ0$, a nonnegative integer iteration budget $N$, and the operationwise arithmetic/range controller. In finite mode the stored input entries are exact dyadics; also supply stored dyadic inverse and solution proposals for every recurrence and residual solve. In exact mode set $G_0=BR^{-1}B^*$, $H_0=Q=C^*C$, and $A_0=A$, the standard DARE coefficients of [[def-standard-continuous-and-discrete-riccati-equations]].

For finite-mode initialization, first solve $RV=B^*$ by the exact complete-pivoting elimination rule below, using order $m$ and the $n$ right-hand sides of $B^*$ in place of $M_j$ and $I$. Perform this preprocessing in exact rational arithmetic on the dyadic inputs. Form $BV$ and $C^*C$ exactly, then round each real and imaginary component once to the declared stored format (nearest, with ties to even), obtaining stored $G_0$ and $H_0$; set stored $A_0=A$. A zero pivot returns `inverse-inconclusive`; a component outside the controller's admitted range returns `range-failure`. On an initialization failure return the inputs, zero completed updates, any formed initial matrices and solve data, and unavailable for every unformed matrix or diagnostic. The finite-mode notation $G_0,H_0$ denotes these rounded matrices, not an assertion that $BR^{-1}B^*$ is dyadic. Record $V$ and the initialization rounding differences separately. This exact rational preprocessing has no asserted bit-cost bound and adds no point-certifier calls.

In exact mode, for each $j=0,\ldots,N-1$, form $M_j=I+G_jH_j$ and solve $M_jW_j=I$ by Gaussian elimination with complete pivoting: at stage $k$, scan the remaining submatrix, choose a nonzero entry of largest exact modulus with lexicographic tie-breaking, swap its row and column into pivot position, eliminate below it, and back-substitute for all columns of $I$, undoing the accumulated column permutation in the solution. If the remaining submatrix is exactly zero before all pivots, return `inverse-inconclusive`. This is a finite exact-arithmetic procedure; no bit-complexity bound is asserted.

In finite arithmetic, form the stored dyadic matrix $\widehat M_j=\operatorname{fl}(I+G_jH_j)$. For each standard basis vector $e_k$, call [[alg-point-verified-linear-system-certifier]] with $(\widehat M_j,e_k,R_j,\widehat w_{j,k})$, using the supplied stored dyadic inverse and solution proposals. Assemble the returned solution centers as $\widehat W_j$. If any call returns `range-failure`, return `range-failure`; if any call is `inconclusive`, return `inverse-inconclusive`; otherwise apply the recurrence updates below using $\widehat W_j$ and the declared operationwise arithmetic. The point certifier's solution balls are diagnostics for the stored solve and do not make the rounded recurrence an exact PSD-preserving recurrence.

In exact mode let $W_j$ be the exact solve result; in finite mode let $W_j=\widehat W_j$. The recurrence formulas are
$$
A_{j+1}=A_jW_jA_j,\qquad G_{j+1}=G_j+A_jW_jG_jA_j^*,\qquad H_{j+1}=H_j+A_j^*H_jW_jA_j.
$$
These formulas use no inverse of $A_j$. Any range failure while forming a stored matrix or applying an update returns `range-failure` with the current raw matrices.

After successful initialization, if all $N$ updates finish without a recurrence failure, return `budget-exhausted` with $N$ completed updates, including when $N=0$. This status records only completion of the prescribed budget; the diagnostics below remain required.

At initialization and after each update, preserve the raw matrices and report $\|G_j-G_j^*\|_F$ and $\|H_j-H_j^*\|_F$. To report the standard DARE residual, form $S_j=R+B^*H_jB$ exactly from the current $H_j$ and original input entries. In exact mode, $S_j$ need not be dyadic: independently solve $S_jV_j=I$ by the same exact elimination rule, using order $m$, and evaluate the residual from [[def-standard-continuous-and-discrete-riccati-equations]] exactly using $V_j$. In finite mode, $S_j$ is dyadic because the original inputs and current stored $H_j$ are dyadic; apply the point-certified solve rule to its $m$ columns with the separate residual proposal packet, and outward-evaluate the residual over the certified solution balls. If the residual solve or evaluation is unavailable or inconclusive, mark the residual unavailable without changing the recurrence status. Symmetrization may be used only to form a candidate and must be followed by fresh residual and positivity checks. On every exit return the current raw matrices, status, completed updates, symmetry defects, and available residual and solve certificates. No exact positive-semidefinite or structure-preserving backward-error claim is made from a rounded recurrence alone.

For Hermitian $G,H\succeq0$, define $\Phi_G(X)=X(I+GX)^{-1}$ and $f(X)=H+A^*\Phi_G(X)A$ on $X\succeq0$. One step of the exact inverse recurrence in [[alg-finite-budget-structure-preserving-doubling-for-dare]] is well-defined, preserves $G_j,H_j\succeq0$, and its updated triple satisfies
$$f\circ f(X)=H_1+A_1^*X(I+G_1X)^{-1}A_1,$$
where
$$A_1=A(I+GH)^{-1}A,\quad G_1=G+A(I+GH)^{-1}GA^*,\quad H_1=H+A^*H(I+GH)^{-1}A.$$
Consequently, starting from $(A,G,H)$, the exact recurrence satisfies $H_j=f^{2^j}(0)$ after $j$ updates. These claims concern exact arithmetic; the rounded branch has only its separately reported diagnostics.

derivations.claim: The inputs are positive semidefinite, and $I+G_0H_0=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\0&1\end{bmatrix},\qquad W_0=\begin{bmatrix}\tfrac12&-\tfrac12\\0&1\end{bmatrix}.$ Using [F1] gives $A_1=W_0,\qquad G_1=\begin{bmatrix}\tfrac32&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad H_1=\begin{bmatrix}\tfrac32&\tfrac32\\\tfrac32&\tfrac32\end{bmatrix}.$ Both updated symmetric blocks are positive semidefinite; $G_1$ is diagonal PSD and $H_1=\tfrac32(1,1)^T(1,1)$.

To illustrate the diagnostic, perturb only one stored off-diagonal entry by $\epsilon>0$ and report $\widetilde H_1=\begin{bmatrix}\tfrac32&\tfrac32+\epsilon\\\tfrac32&\tfrac32\end{bmatrix}$. Its symmetry defect is $\|\widetilde H_1-\widetilde H_1^*\|_F=\sqrt2\,\epsilon.$ Even its symmetrization has determinant $\frac94-(\frac32+\frac\epsilon2)^2<0$, so this perturbed stored block is not positive semidefinite. It must be reported and rechecked rather than treated as covered by the exact-arithmetic PSD invariant.

Let $C=[x\;B]\in\mathbb R^{r\times(q+1)}$, $r\ge1$, $q\ge0$, undergo a successful step of [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]], with $0<u<1$ and $ru<1$. Define
$$g_r=\frac{ru}{1-ru},\quad e_r=(1+u)^{r/2+3}-1,\quad d_r=e_r+u(2+e_r),\quad a_r=\frac{1+u}{(1-u)^r}-1,$$
$$c_r=2\bigl((1+a_r)(1+u)^2(1+g_r)-1\bigr),\qquad \kappa_r=\max\{e_r+8d_r,(1+u)c_r+3u\}.$$
There is an exact orthogonal $H$, the identity when $x=0$ and $H(v)=I-2vv^T/(v^Tv)$ otherwise, and a perturbation $E$ such that
$$H(C+E)=C_+,\qquad \|E\|_F\le\kappa_r\|C\|_F.$$
The constants increase with $r$ and are $O(ru)$ for fixed $r$ as $u\to0$. The column overwrite is included. For any real separate block $Y\in\mathbb R^{r\times t}$, $t\ge0$, successful application of the same stored $(v,\widehat\tau)$ without an annihilation overwrite has discrepancy from $H(v)Y$ at most $((1+u)c_r+3u)\|Y\|_F$.

derivations.claim: Put $x=qu$. The precision hypothesis gives $u\le1/(200q)$ and $0<x<1/200$. Since $q/2+3\le7q/2$, set $s=(q/2+3)u\le7x/2<7/400$. The power series gives $1+u\le e^u$ and, for $0\le z<1$, $e^z-1=\sum_{j\ge1}z^j/j!\le z/(1-z)$. Therefore $$e_q\le e^s-1\le\frac{s}{1-s} \le\frac{1400}{393}x<\frac{18}{5}x.$$ Also $ue_q\le(9/500)u$, so $$d_q=e_q+2u+ue_q \le\frac{18}{5}x+\frac{1009}{500}u \le\frac{2809}{500}x<\frac{57}{10}x.$$ Hence the first branch in [F1] satisfies $e_q+8d_q<(18/5+8\cdot57/10)x<50x$.

Bernoulli's inequality gives $(1-u)^q\ge1-qu=1-x$; for integer $q$, this follows by induction from $(1-u)(1-qu)=1-(q+1)u+qu^2\ge1-(q+1)u$. Since $u\le1/200$ and $x\le1/200$, $(1+u)^3\le1+4u$ by expansion, and $(1-x)^{-2}\le1+3x$ because $(1+3x)(1-x)^2-1=x(1-5x+3x^2)\ge0$. Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let
$A=(a_{ij})\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$. The **Frobenius norm** of $A$ is

$$\lVert A\rVert_F\;:=\;\Bigl(\,\sum_{i<m}\sum_{j<n}|a_{ij}|^{2}\Bigr)^{1/2},$$

where $|\cdot|$ is the absolute value on $\mathbb R$
([[def-abs-value]]) for $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ and the modulus on $\mathbb C$
([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) for
$\mathbb F=\mathbb C$, and the outer power is the nonnegative real square root.

**The displayed quantity is a norm.** Regard $A$ as the element of the
coordinate space $\mathbb F^{mn}$ whose $j+in$-th entry is $a_{ij}$. The
standard coordinate inner product of [[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]
satisfies $\langle A,A\rangle=\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}\overline{a_{ij}}$, which equals
$\sum_{i,j}|a_{ij}|^{2}$ because $z\overline z=|z|^{2}$
([[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]). Thus $\lVert A\rVert_F$ is
exactly the inner-product norm of [[def-inner-product-norm]] evaluated at $A$,
and the three norm axioms hold for $\lVert\cdot\rVert_F$ because they hold for
every inner-product norm. For real matrices the same sum is
$\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}^{2}$, since $|x|^{2}=x^{2}$ for real $x$ by the two cases of
[[def-abs-value]].

The Frobenius norm is the Euclidean norm of the full entry list, not the
largest factor by which the matrix stretches a single vector. It can coincide
with an induced $2$-norm in one-row or one-column cases, but in general it is a
different matrix norm from the induced operator norms used on this page. Its
relation to the spectral norm, its unitary invariance and its singular-value
formula are
[[thm-spectral-and-frobenius-norms-are-unitarily-invariant-with-singular-value-formulas-and-rank-comparison]].

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces. If $V=0$, define $\lVert T\rVert:=0$. If $V\ne0$, define the
**operator norm** of $T$ by

$$\lVert T\rVert:=\max\{\lVert Tv\rVert:\lVert v\rVert=1\}.$$

The next theorem proves that this maximum exists and equals the largest
singular value.

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$, and
let $\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_r>0$ be the positive singular values of
$A$, where $r=\operatorname{rank}A$; write $\sigma_1=0$ when $r=0$.

1. **Spectral formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_2=\sigma_1$, where $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ is
   the operator norm of [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]].
2. **Frobenius formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_F=\bigl(\sigma_1^{2}+\cdots+\sigma_r^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$.
3. **Unitary invariance.** For every unitary $U\in M_m(\mathbb F)$ and
   $V\in M_n(\mathbb F)$ (over $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$: orthogonal matrices),
   $$\lVert UAV\rVert_2=\lVert A\rVert_2,\qquad \lVert UAV\rVert_F=\lVert A\rVert_F.$$
4. **Sharp rank comparison.**
   $$\lVert A\rVert_2\;\le\;\lVert A\rVert_F\;\le\;\sqrt{r}\,\lVert A\rVert_2.$$
   The lower inequality is an equality exactly when $r\le 1$; the upper
   inequality is an equality exactly when $\sigma_1=\cdots=\sigma_r$, that is,
   when all nonzero singular values coincide. In particular
   $\lVert A\rVert_F\le\sqrt{\min(m,n)}\,\lVert A\rVert_2$.

derivations.claim: Expanding $\widehat G\widehat G^T=(G+E)(G+E)^T$ gives $$\widehat G\widehat G^T-GG^T=GE^T+EG^T+EE^T.$$

For any compatible matrices $A,B$, applying the definition of the operator norm to each column gives $$\|AB\|_F^2=\sum_j\|ABe_j\|_2^2 \le \|A\|_2^2\sum_j\|Be_j\|_2^2 =\|A\|_2^2\|B\|_F^2 \le \|A\|_F^2\|B\|_F^2.$$ Thus $\|GE^T\|_F,\|EG^T\|_F\le\|G\|_F\|E\|_F$ and $\|EE^T\|_F\le\|E\|_F^2$. The triangle inequality applied to step 1.1 proves the stated estimate.
