citations.quote:
On the grid of [[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]], let
$\Delta_h^{-1}:Q_h\to Q_h$ be the inverse from
[[lem-na-periodic-grid-pressure-laplacian-zero-mode-and-poincare]]. Define
$$ P_h:=I-G_h\Delta_h^{-1}D_h:V_h\to V_h. $$
Then $P_h$ is the mass-orthogonal projector onto
$Z_h=\ker D_h$. In the backward-Euler algorithm
[[alg-na-periodic-incremental-pressure-correction]], the velocity correction
satisfies $u^{n+1}=P_h\widetilde u^{n+1}$ and
$D_hu^{n+1}=0$ exactly.

On the periodic staggered grid of
[[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]], every admissible backward-
Euler step of [[alg-na-periodic-incremental-pressure-correction]] and every
admissible BDF2 step of
[[alg-na-bdf2-incremental-and-rotational-pressure-correction]] has a unique
predictor, a unique mean-zero pressure increment, and a unique updated pair.
Both algorithms preserve the zero-mean pressure gauge and exact discrete
incompressibility.

Use [[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]] with $h=1/N$. For a
smooth periodic vector field $u\in C^4(\mathbb T^d;\mathbb R^d)$, define
$R_hu$ by sampling component $i$ at each face centre $x_j+he_i/2$. For a
smooth periodic scalar $p\in C^3(\mathbb T^d)$, define $R_hp$ by sampling at
cell centres $x_j$. Put $\|r\|_{\widetilde Q_h}=(h^d\sum_jr_j^2)^{1/2}$ for all cell arrays $r$;
this agrees with $\|r\|_{Q_h}$ on $Q_h$. Then uniformly for $N\ge2$,
$$ \|D_hR_hu-R_h(\nabla\cdot u)\|_{\widetilde Q_h} +\|A_hR_hu-R_h(-\Delta u)\|_{M_h} +\|G_hR_hp-R_h(\nabla p)\|_{M_h} \le C h^2, $$
where $C$ depends only on $d$ and the suprema of the displayed fields'
derivatives through orders $4$ for $u$ and $3$ for $p$. Here the sampling of a
vector field is facewise componentwise. For any $g\in C^2(\mathbb T^d)$ with
zero integral, the cell-centred or face-centred midpoint samples have discrete
mean whose absolute value is at most $C_dh^2\|D^2g\|_\infty$.

Use the spaces and operators of
[[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]] with $d\ge1$, $N\ge2$,
and $h=1/N$. Then $\Delta_h=D_hG_h$ maps $Q_h$ bijectively to itself, the
kernel of $\Delta_h$ on all cell arrays consists exactly of the constants,
and $D_hv$ has zero mean for every $v\in V_h$. In addition, every $q\in Q_h$
satisfies the resolution-independent bound
$$ \|q\|_{Q_h}\le\sqrt d\,\|G_hq\|_{M_h}. $$

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$ and an integer resolution $N\ge2$, where
$N\in\mathbb N$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), and put $h=1/N$. Real scalar and
array operations use the field $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-reals-field]]). Let
$J_N=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}^d$; each coordinate index addition below is reduced
to the unique element of $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ congruent modulo $N$. The unit
torus $\mathbb T^d$ means the unit cube with opposite faces identified, so
fields and arrays are periodic across those faces. Write
$\mathbf 1=(1,\ldots,1)$ and let $e_i$ be the $i$th standard coordinate vector.
Cell $j$ has centre $x_j=h(j+\tfrac12\mathbf 1)$. The pressure value $q_j$ is
stored at that centre. Velocity component $i$ is stored at the right face of
cell $j$, with centre $x_j+\tfrac h2e_i$.

Let $\widetilde Q_h$ be all real scalar cell arrays and let
$Q_h=\{q\in\widetilde Q_h:h^d\sum_jq_j=0\}$. Let $V_h$ be the real vector
face arrays $v=(v_{i,j})_{1\le i\le d,\,j\in J_N}$. Give them the mass inner products
$$ (q,r)_{Q_h}=h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}q_jr_j,\qquad (v,w)_{M_h}=h^d\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N}v_{i,j}w_{i,j}. $$
Define the pressure gradient $G_h:\widetilde Q_h\to V_h$ and velocity
divergence $D_h:V_h\to Q_h$ by
$$ (G_hq)_{i,j}=\frac{q_{j+e_i}-q_j}{h},\qquad (D_hv)_j=\sum_{i=1}^d\frac{v_{i,j}-v_{i,j-e_i}}{h}. $$
The compatible pressure Laplacian is $\Delta_h=D_hG_h$; its restriction to
$Q_h$ is negative semidefinite, and $G_h$ annihilates constants. Define the
componentwise vector Laplacian by
$$ (\Delta_h^Vv)_{i,j}=h^{-2}\sum_{\ell=1}^d (v_{i,j+e_\ell}-2v_{i,j}+v_{i,j-e_\ell}),\qquad A_h=-\Delta_h^V, $$
and the discrete velocity-gradient seminorm by
$$ \|\mathcal G_hv\|_{M_h}^2=h^{d-2}\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{\ell=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N} |v_{i,j+e_\ell}-v_{i,j}|^2. $$
The fixed cell/face placement is part of the definition; collocated central
differences are a different discretization.

Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $m \ge 1$ and let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$.

1. **Fundamental theorem, second part, in $\mathbb{R}^{m}$.** Let
   $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ be differentiable at every point of $[a,b]$ as
   a function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]), and
   suppose $f' : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ is integrable. Then
   $$\int_a^b f' \;=\; f(b) - f(a).$$
2. **A bounded derivative gives a Lipschitz function.** Let
   $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ be continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable at
   every point of $(a,b)$, and let $M \ge 0$ satisfy
   $\lVert f'(t)\rVert_2 \le M$ for every $t \in (a,b)$. Then
   $$\lVert f(t) - f(s)\rVert_2 \;\le\; M\,|t-s| \qquad \text{for all } s,t \in [a,b],$$
   that is, $f$ is Lipschitz with constant $M$ as a map
   $([a,b], d_{\mathbb{R}}) \to (\mathbb{R}^{m}, d_2)$
   ([[def-lipschitz-holder-contraction]], [[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]],
   [[lem-metrics-on-rn]]).

Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $m \ge 1$, let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a \le b$
and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$. If $a<b$, assume that $f$ is integrable
([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]). Then:

1. if $a < b$, the real-valued function $t \mapsto \lVert f(t)\rVert_2$ is
   integrable on $[a,b]$ ([[def-darboux-integral]], [[def-p-norms-on-rn]]);
2. $$\Bigl\lVert \int_a^b f \Bigr\rVert_2 \;\le\; \int_a^b \lVert f\rVert_2 .$$

**The hypothesis $a \le b$ is not decoration.** With the orientation convention
of [[def-oriented-integral]] and
[[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]], interchanging the limits changes
the sign of the right-hand side but not of the left, so for $b < a$ the correct
statement is $\bigl\lVert\int_a^b f\bigr\rVert_2 \le \bigl|\int_a^b \lVert f\rVert_2\bigr|$;
the displayed inequality as written is false in that case. This is the same trap
the scalar inequality of
[[cor-integrability-of-absolute-values-products-and-lattice-operations]] carries.

**Clause 1 is a genuine obligation and is discharged before the estimate.** That
each $f_i$ is integrable does not by itself say that
$\sqrt{\sum_{i<m} f_i^{2}}$ is; the square root has to be brought in through
[[thm-composition-with-a-continuous-function]].

derivations.claim: Let $R_hu(t)$ denote the face samples and $R_hp(t),R_hf(t)$ the cell and face samples, respectively. For a face array $z$, write $\bar z_i$ for the discrete mean of component $i$ repeated on every $i$-face. The input force is $f_h(t)=R_hf(t)-\bar{R_hf(t)}$, so [F3] gives $\|f_h(t)-R_hf(t)\|_{M_h}\le C h^2$. Define the sampling residual $$ r_h(t)=R_hu_t(t)+\nu A_hR_hu(t)+G_hR_hp(t)-R_hf(t). $$ The continuous Stokes equation and [F3] imply $\|r_h(t)\|_{M_h}\le C h^2$, uniformly in $t$.

Define $v_h(t)=P_hR_hu(t)$ and let $L_h=-\Delta_h$ on mean-zero cell arrays. All coordinate shifts commute, so $A_hG_h=G_hL_h$ and $D_hA_h=L_hD_h$. Since $L_h=-\Delta_h$, it commutes with $\Delta_h^{-1}$ on $Q_h$. Substitution in $P_h=I-G_h\Delta_h^{-1}D_h$ gives $P_hA_h=A_hP_h$. Also $P_hG_hq=0$ for every mean-zero $q$, because $G_hq$ is orthogonal to $\ker D_h$ by the adjoint relation in [F1]. Applying $P_h$ to the residual equation in step 1.1 therefore yields $$ v_h'(t)+\nu A_hv_h(t)=P_hf_h(t)+\rho_h(t), $$ where $\rho_h=P_hr_h+P_h(R_hf-f_h)$. By [F1], $\|P_h\|\le1$, and hence $\|\rho_h(t)\|_{M_h}\le C h^2$.

Applying $P_h$ to the predictor equation and using $P_hA_h=A_hP_h$ and $P_hG_hp_h^n=0$ shows that the actual corrected velocity is exactly the backward-Euler step on $Z_h=\ker D_h$: $$ (I+k\nu A_h)u_h^{n+1}=u_h^n+kP_hf_h(t_{n+1}). $$ The projected reference $v_h$ obeys the differential equation in step 2.1.

Put $e_h^n=u_h^n-v_h(t_n)$. Integrating $v_h'$ over $[t_n,t_{n+1}]$ and using the equation in step 2.1 gives $$ (I+k\nu A_h)v_h(t_{n+1}) =v_h(t_n)+kP_hf_h(t_{n+1})+k\rho_h(t_{n+1})+\tau_h^{n+1}, $$ where $\tau_h^{n+1}=v_h(t_{n+1})-v_h(t_n)-kv_h'(t_{n+1})$. By [F7], $$\tau_h^{n+1}=\int_{t_n}^{t_{n+1}}\bigl(v_h'(s)-v_h'(t_{n+1})\bigr)\,ds.$$ The bounded-derivative clause of [F7] gives $\|v_h'(s)-v_h'(t_{n+1})\|_{M_h}\le (t_{n+1}-s)\sup_t\|v_h''(t)\|_{M_h}$ after the isometric identification $v\mapsto h^{d/2}v$ with Euclidean coordinates. Applying [F8] yields $$\|\tau_h^{n+1}\|_{M_h}\le\int_{t_n}^{t_{n+1}}(t_{n+1}-s)\sup_t\|v_h''(t)\|_{M_h}\,ds=\frac{k^2}{2}\sup_t\|v_h''(t)\|_{M_h}\le Ck^2,$$ because $P_h$ is a contraction and $h^dN^d=1$ bounds the weighted sample norm by the continuous supremum norm up to the fixed component factor.

For any face vector $z$, periodic summation by parts gives $(A_hz,z)_{M_h}\ge0$. Hence $$ \|(I+k
u A_h)z\|_{M_h}^2 =\|z\|_{M_h}^2+2k
u(A_hz,z)_{M_h}+k^2
u^2\|A_hz\|_{M_h}^2 \ge\|z\|_{M_h}^2. $$ Thus $(I+k
u A_h)^{-1}$ is a contraction. Subtracting the equations in steps 3.1–4.1 and applying this contraction gives $$ \|e_h^{n+1}\|_{M_h} \le\|e_h^n\|_{M_h}+Ckh^2+Ck^2. $$ Since $e_h^0=0$ and $M=T/k$, summing yields $\max_n\|e_h^n\|_{M_h}\le C_T(h^2+k)$.

Finally, $u_h^n-R_hu(t_n)=e_h^n+(P_hR_hu(t_n)-R_hu(t_n))$. The second term equals $-G_h\phi$ with $\phi=\Delta_h^{-1}D_hR_hu(t_n)$. By [F4] and [F5], $$ \|G_h\phi\|_{M_h}^2 =-(\phi,\Delta_h\phi)_{Q_h} =-(\phi,D_hR_hu)_{Q_h} \le\sqrt d\|G_h\phi\|_{M_h}\|D_hR_hu\|_{Q_h}. $$ If $G_h\phi=0$ the bound is immediate; otherwise divide by its norm. Since $\nabla\cdot u=0$, [F3] gives $\|D_hR_hu\|_{Q_h}\le Ch^2$, so the projection-sampling discrepancy is $O(h^2)$. Combining this with step 5.1 proves the stated estimate.

risk_review.notes: Reviewed all six steps and nine dependency statements/proofs as invoked. Constant coefficient shifts commute with A_h,G_h,D_h and the gauged inverse, so projection commutes with diffusion and removes pressure exactly. The sampled Stokes residual and force mean correction are O(h^2); projection is a contraction. The integral FTC and integral norm inequality apply to the finite Euclidean array after h^{d/2} scaling and give O(k^2) local defect from bounded u_tt. Positive predictor resolvent is contractive with no time-step restriction; summing M=T/k defects gives C_T(h^2+k). For the sampling projection discrepancy, negative adjoint, pressure Poincare and Cauchy–Schwarz give ||G phi||<=sqrt(d)||D R_h u||, with the zero-gradient case explicitly separated. Here div u=0, so the repaired consistency lemma applies within Q_h with the identical norm. M=1 and n=0 included; continuous regularity, gauged initialization and mean-zero forcing suffice. No pressure rate is inferred; no defect. cor-na-mini-element-pressure-mass-schur-.axiom_use: Axiom of Countable Choice (ACω) is explicitly assumed and carried through the named MINI, Korn, or Fortin suppliers. No full Axiom of Choice branch is invoked.

citations.quote:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz open set, where Lipschitz means that $\partial D$ has a finite rigidly moved graph-chart atlas. Here $H^1_0(D)$ is the $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(D)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). Since $D$ has finite measure, Holder makes every $L^2$ class integrable, so the zero-mean condition is well-defined ([[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]]). Define
$$V:=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d),\qquad Q:=L^2_0(D):=\{q\in L^2(D;\mathbb R):\int_Dq=0\}.$$
Equip $V$ with $\|v\|_V:=\|
abla v\|_{L^2(D)}$ and $Q$ with $\|q\|_Q:=\|q\|_{L^2(D)}$. The local Poincare inequality [[lem-na-homogeneous-dirichlet-poincare]] makes the first a norm equivalent to the usual $H^1$ norm. For $v\in V$, define $\varepsilon(v):=(
abla v+
abla v^T)/2$ and $b(v,q):=-\int_Dq\,\operatorname{div}v$. For viscosity $
u>0$, set $a_
u(u,v):=2
u\int_D\varepsilon(u):\varepsilon(v)$, where $X:Y=\sum_{i,j}X_{ij}Y_{ij}$. The continuous domain class is all bounded connected Lipschitz $D$; the exact mini-element mesh class is the narrower polygonal/polyhedral conforming affine simplicial class.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d=2$ or $3$, be a bounded connected Lipschitz polygonal/polyhedral domain with a conforming shape-regular affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$. On a simplex $K$ with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$, define the scalar interior bubble $b_K=(d+1)^{d+1}\prod_{i=0}^d\lambda_i$. Let
$$S^1_h=\{w\in C^0(\overline D):w|_K\in P_1(K)\},\quad S^1_{h,0}=S^1_h\cap H^1_0(D).$$
The **mini-element spaces** are
$$V_h=[S^1_{h,0}]^d\oplus\bigoplus_{K\in\mathcal T_h}b_K\mathbb R^d\subset H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d),\qquad Q_h=S^1_h\cap L^2_0(D).$$
Each bubble is extended by zero off its cell. The zero-boundary conformity of the piecewise affine part is supplied by [[thm-zero-boundary-piecewise-polynomials-in-w10p]]. The local/global dimensions are proved in the next dimension lemma.

Assume Countable Choice. For a nonempty connected conforming simplicial mesh in dimension $d=2$ or $3$, the local scalar velocity polynomial space $P_1(K)\oplus\operatorname{span}\{b_K\}$ has dimension $d+2$, the vector velocity dimension is $d(d+2)$, and the local pressure space $P_1(K)$ has dimension $d+1$. If the mesh has $N_v$ vertices, $N_{v,0}$ interior vertices and $N_K$ cells, then
$$\dim V_h=dN_{v,0}+dN_K,\qquad \dim Q_h=N_v-1.$$

Assume Countable Choice. For bounded open $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $v\in H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$, put $\varepsilon(v)=(
abla v+
abla v^T)/2$. Then
$$2\|\varepsilon(v)\|_2^2=\|
abla v\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}v\|_2^2,$$
so $\|
abla v\|_2\le\sqrt2\|\varepsilon(v)\|_2$.

On the mini-element spaces of [[def-na-mini-element-p1-bubble-p1-spaces]], there is a Fortin operator $\Pi_h:V\to V_h$ preserving $b(v,q_h)$ for every $q_h\in Q_h$, with $\|\Pi_hv\|_V\le C_F\|v\|_V$. The constant depends only on $d$ and the mesh shape-regularity bound, not on $h$. Consequently
$$\beta_h\ge (C_FC_{\rm div}(D))^{-1}.$$

Let $V,Q$ be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces with norms
$\|\cdot\|_V,\|\cdot\|_Q$. Let $a(v,w)=v^TAw$ be symmetric positive
definite, and let $b(v,q)=q^TBv$ be a bilinear constraint form, represented
by the matrices in
[[def-na-symmetric-saddle-point-system-and-block-preconditioners]]. Suppose
that, for constants $\alpha,\Lambda,C_b,\beta>0$,
$$ \alpha\|v\|_V^2\le a(v,v)\le\Lambda\|v\|_V^2, \quad |b(v,q)|\le C_b\|v\|_V\|q\|_Q, \quad \sup_{v\ne0}\frac{|b(v,q)|}{\|v\|_V}\ge\beta\|q\|_Q. $$
If $M_Q$ is the pressure mass matrix for $\|\cdot\|_Q$, then the positive
Schur matrix $S=BA^{-1}B^T$ satisfies, for every $q\in Q$,
$$ \frac{\beta^2}{\Lambda}q^TM_Qq \le q^TSq \le\frac{C_b^2}{\alpha}q^TM_Qq. $$
Thus pressure-mass Schur equivalence is conditional on the actual inf-sup,
continuity, and velocity stiffness scalings shown here.

For $x,y\in\mathbb R^n$ and $z,w\in\mathbb C^n$, the formulas

$$\langle x,y\rangle_{\mathbb R^n}=\sum_{k<n}x_ky_k,\qquad \langle z,w\rangle_{\mathbb C^n}=\sum_{k<n}z_k\overline{w_k}$$

define inner products, linear in the first argument. At $n=0$, the unique pairing on the zero space is an inner product.

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be
conjugate exponents, and let $f,g$ be measurable real-valued functions.

1. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $q<\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^q(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q.$$
2. If $p=1$ and $q=\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$ and
   $g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_1\|g\|_\infty.$$
3. If $p=\infty$ and $q=1$ with $f\in L^\infty(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_1.$$

In every case the right-hand side is finite, so $fg$ is integrable.

Let $n,m\ge1$, $V=M_{n\times1}(\mathbb R)$, and
$Q=M_{m\times1}(\mathbb R)$. Let $A\in M_n(\mathbb R)$ be symmetric
positive definite, let $B\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb R)$ have full row rank
(meaning $B^Tq=0$ implies $q=0$), and let
$M_Q\in M_m(\mathbb R)$ be symmetric positive definite. The saddle system
and its matrix are
$$ K=\begin{pmatrix}A&B^T\\B&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Au+B^Tp=f,\quad Bu=g. $$
Define the positive pressure Schur matrix
$$ S:=BA^{-1}B^T. $$
In the block-LU convention of [[def-block-lu-factorisation]], the trailing
Schur complement of $A$ in $K$ is $-S$. The exact block solve first solves
$Au_0=f$, then $Sp=Bu_0-g$, and finally $Au=f-B^Tp$; the theorem
[[thm-na-saddle-point-exact-schur-solve]] verifies this procedure and
well-definedness.

For a scaling $\gamma>0$, the pressure-mass block-diagonal preconditioner is
$$ P_\gamma=\operatorname{diag}(A,\gamma M_Q). $$
It is symmetric positive definite. If $P_\gamma=CC^T$ is its Cholesky
factorization with $C$ lower triangular and positive on the diagonal, the
symmetric preconditioned system is $C^{-1}KC^{-T}y=C^{-1}r$, with the usual
change of unknown. This is the symmetric-preconditioning convention of
[[def-left-right-and-symmetric-positive-definite-preconditioning]]. No
spectral bound, Krylov iteration count, complexity estimate, or generic speed
improvement is part of this definition.

Let $V_h\subset V$ and $Q_h\subset Q$, and suppose the continuous inf-sup constant of $b$ is $\beta>0$. If $Q_h=\{0\}$ the constraint assertion is vacuous. derivations.claim: Write $a=c=2\pi$. Direct differentiation gives $\nabla\cdot\widetilde u=-c\sin(ax)y(1-y)$. Define $$ g(y)=-\frac c{a^2}y^2+\frac c{a^2}y-\frac{2c}{a^4} +\frac{c}{a^3\sinh(a/2)}\cosh(a(y-1/2)),\qquad \phi(x,y)=\sin(ax)g(y). $$ Differentiating the polynomial and hyperbolic terms gives $g''-a^2g=-c y(1-y)$ and $g'(0)=g'(1)=0$. By [F2], this $\phi$ solves the stated Poisson problem and satisfies both Neumann conditions. Since $\widetilde u_y=0$ and $\partial_y\phi=0$ at the walls, the corrected normal velocity remains zero.

For uniqueness of its gradient, if two classical periodic Neumann solutions are given, their difference $w$ is harmonic with $\partial_yw=0$ on both walls. For each fixed $y$, one-dimensional integration by parts in $x$ gives $\int_{\mathbb T}w w_{xx}=-\int_{\mathbb T}w_x^2$ because the periodic endpoint terms cancel; integration by parts in $y$ gives $\int_0^1 w w_{yy}=[w w_y]_0^1-\int_0^1w_y^2=-\int_0^1w_y^2$ by the Neumann data. Integrating the latter equality in $x$ and using $\Delta w=0$ yields $\int_\Omega|\nabla w|^2=0$. Hence $\nabla w=0$, so the correction is independent of the pressure constant.

Since $\widetilde u_x(x,0)=0$, the corrected tangential trace at the lower wall is $$ u_x(x,0)=-\partial_x\phi(x,0)=-a\cos(ax)g(0). $$ At $x=0$, $$ g(0)=\frac c{a^4}\bigl(a\coth(a/2)-2\bigr)>0, $$ because $\coth(a/2)>1$ and $a=2\pi>2$. Therefore $u_x(0,0)=-a g(0)\ne0$, which proves the tangential no-slip defect.

Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$ and an integer resolution $N\ge2$, where
$N\in\mathbb N$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), and put $h=1/N$. Real scalar and
array operations use the field $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-reals-field]]). Let
$J_N=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}^d$; each coordinate index addition below is reduced
to the unique element of $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ congruent modulo $N$. The unit
torus $\mathbb T^d$ means the unit cube with opposite faces identified, so
fields and arrays are periodic across those faces. Write
$\mathbf 1=(1,\ldots,1)$ and let $e_i$ be the $i$th standard coordinate vector.
Cell $j$ has centre $x_j=h(j+\tfrac12\mathbf 1)$. The pressure value $q_j$ is
stored at that centre. Velocity component $i$ is stored at the right face of
cell $j$, with centre $x_j+\tfrac h2e_i$.

Let $\widetilde Q_h$ be all real scalar cell arrays and let
$Q_h=\{q\in\widetilde Q_h:h^d\sum_jq_j=0\}$. Let $V_h$ be the real vector
face arrays $v=(v_{i,j})_{1\le i\le d,\,j\in J_N}$. Give them the mass inner products
$$ (q,r)_{Q_h}=h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}q_jr_j,\qquad (v,w)_{M_h}=h^d\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N}v_{i,j}w_{i,j}. $$
Define the pressure gradient $G_h:\widetilde Q_h\to V_h$ and velocity
divergence $D_h:V_h\to Q_h$ by
$$ (G_hq)_{i,j}=\frac{q_{j+e_i}-q_j}{h},\qquad (D_hv)_j=\sum_{i=1}^d\frac{v_{i,j}-v_{i,j-e_i}}{h}. $$
The compatible pressure Laplacian is $\Delta_h=D_hG_h$; its restriction to
$Q_h$ is negative semidefinite, and $G_h$ annihilates constants. Define the
componentwise vector Laplacian by
$$ (\Delta_h^Vv)_{i,j}=h^{-2}\sum_{\ell=1}^d (v_{i,j+e_\ell}-2v_{i,j}+v_{i,j-e_\ell}),\qquad A_h=-\Delta_h^V, $$
and the discrete velocity-gradient seminorm by
$$ \|\mathcal G_hv\|_{M_h}^2=h^{d-2}\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{\ell=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N} |v_{i,j+e_\ell}-v_{i,j}|^2. $$
The fixed cell/face placement is part of the definition; collocated central
differences are a different discretization.

derivations.claim: Since $N$ is even, summing $(-1)^{j_1}$ over its $N$ values gives zero; the other coordinates simply repeat this sum. Hence $q$ has zero discrete mean. It is nonconstant because its values at $j_1=0$ and $j_1=1$ differ.

For $i=1$, [F2] gives $q_{j+e_1}=q_{j-e_1}$, so the first component of $G_cq$ is zero. For every $i>1$, the array is independent of coordinate $i$, hence again $q_{j+e_i}=q_{j-e_i}$. The defining centred difference therefore gives $G_cq=0$ in every component, proving the nonconstant zero-mean pressure mode is invisible.

[[def-na-symmetric-saddle-point-system-and-block-preconditioners]], and set
$$ a_\gamma=\frac{\beta^2}{\Lambda\gamma},\qquad b_\gamma=\frac{C_b^2}{\alpha\gamma},\qquad \lambda_\pm(s)=\frac{1\pm\sqrt{1+4s}}2. $$
Let $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m$ be the eigenvalues, with multiplicity, of
$(\gamma M_Q)^{-1/2}S(\gamma M_Q)^{-1/2}$. Then
$a_\gamma\le\mu_j\le b_\gamma$, and the symmetric square-root-preconditioned
saddle matrix has eigenvalues
$$ \{\lambda_-(\mu_j),\lambda_+(\mu_j):1\le j\le m\} \quad\text{and }1\text{ with multiplicity }n-m. $$
Consequently its spectrum is contained in
$$ [\lambda_-(b_\gamma),\lambda_-(a_\gamma)]\;\cup\; \{1\}\;\cup\; [\lambda_+(a_\gamma),\lambda_+(b_\gamma)], $$
where the eigenvalue $1$ has multiplicity zero if $n=m$. This is a spectral
estimate for the stated scaled block preconditioner, not an iteration-count
or generic solver-speed claim.

Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$ and an integer resolution $N\ge2$, where
$N\in\mathbb N$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), and put $h=1/N$. Real scalar and
array operations use the field $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-reals-field]]). Let
$J_N=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}^d$; each coordinate index addition below is reduced
to the unique element of $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ congruent modulo $N$. The unit
torus $\mathbb T^d$ means the unit cube with opposite faces identified, so
fields and arrays are periodic across those faces. Write
$\mathbf 1=(1,\ldots,1)$ and let $e_i$ be the $i$th standard coordinate vector.
Cell $j$ has centre $x_j=h(j+\tfrac12\mathbf 1)$. The pressure value $q_j$ is
stored at that centre. Velocity component $i$ is stored at the right face of
cell $j$, with centre $x_j+\tfrac h2e_i$.

Let $\widetilde Q_h$ be all real scalar cell arrays and let
$Q_h=\{q\in\widetilde Q_h:h^d\sum_jq_j=0\}$. Let $V_h$ be the real vector
face arrays $v=(v_{i,j})_{1\le i\le d,\,j\in J_N}$. Give them the mass inner products
$$ (q,r)_{Q_h}=h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}q_jr_j,\qquad (v,w)_{M_h}=h^d\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N}v_{i,j}w_{i,j}. $$
Define the pressure gradient $G_h:\widetilde Q_h\to V_h$ and velocity
divergence $D_h:V_h\to Q_h$ by
$$ (G_hq)_{i,j}=\frac{q_{j+e_i}-q_j}{h},\qquad (D_hv)_j=\sum_{i=1}^d\frac{v_{i,j}-v_{i,j-e_i}}{h}. $$
The compatible pressure Laplacian is $\Delta_h=D_hG_h$; its restriction to
$Q_h$ is negative semidefinite, and $G_h$ annihilates constants. Define the
componentwise vector Laplacian by
$$ (\Delta_h^Vv)_{i,j}=h^{-2}\sum_{\ell=1}^d (v_{i,j+e_\ell}-2v_{i,j}+v_{i,j-e_\ell}),\qquad A_h=-\Delta_h^V, $$
and the discrete velocity-gradient seminorm by
$$ \|\mathcal G_hv\|_{M_h}^2=h^{d-2}\sum_{i=1}^d\sum_{\ell=1}^d\sum_{j\in J_N} |v_{i,j+e_\ell}-v_{i,j}|^2. $$
The fixed cell/face placement is part of the definition; collocated central
differences are a different discretization.

Fix $d\ge1$, $N\ge2$, $h=1/N$, viscosity $\nu>0$, and time step $k>0$.
Given $u^n\in V_h$ with $D_hu^n=0$, a mean-zero
pressure $p^n\in Q_h$, and a force $f^{n+1}\in V_h$ whose components each
have zero discrete mean,
$$h^d\sum_{j\in J_N}f_{i,j}^{n+1}=0\qquad(1\le i\le d),$$
define the next step by the following two solves and update:

1. Find $\widetilde u^{n+1}\in V_h$ satisfying
$$ \frac{\widetilde u^{n+1}-u^n}{k}+\nu A_h\widetilde u^{n+1}+G_hp^n=f^{n+1}. $$

2. Find the unique $\phi^{n+1}\in Q_h$ satisfying
$$ \Delta_h\phi^{n+1}=k^{-1}D_h\widetilde u^{n+1}. $$

3. Set
$$ u^{n+1}=\widetilde u^{n+1}-kG_h\phi^{n+1},\qquad p^{n+1}=p^n+\phi^{n+1}. $$

The pressure is kept in $Q_h$ after every solve; the constant pressure mode
is set to zero. The procedure is only asserted for the periodic staggered
grid and the admissible data stated here. The separate well-definedness
theorem [[thm-na-periodic-pressure-correction-solves-well-defined]] verifies
both solves and the preserved constraints.

On the periodic staggered grid of
[[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]], every admissible backward-
Euler step of [[alg-na-periodic-incremental-pressure-correction]] and every
admissible BDF2 step of
[[alg-na-bdf2-incremental-and-rotational-pressure-correction]] has a unique
predictor, a unique mean-zero pressure increment, and a unique updated pair.
Both algorithms preserve the zero-mean pressure gauge and exact discrete
incompressibility.

On the grid of [[def-na-periodic-staggered-grid-stokes-operators]], let
$\Delta_h^{-1}:Q_h\to Q_h$ be the inverse from
[[lem-na-periodic-grid-pressure-laplacian-zero-mode-and-poincare]]. Define
$$ P_h:=I-G_h\Delta_h^{-1}D_h:V_h\to V_h. $$
Then $P_h$ is the mass-orthogonal projector onto
$Z_h=\ker D_h$. In the backward-Euler algorithm
[[alg-na-periodic-incremental-pressure-correction]], the velocity correction
satisfies $u^{n+1}=P_h\widetilde u^{n+1}$ and
$D_hu^{n+1}=0$ exactly.

derivations.claim: Since $N$ is even, $q$ has zero mean. The staggered gradient is not zero: $(G_hq)_{1,j}=-2q_j/h$. Also $\Delta_hq=-4q/h^2$, so [F1] gives $D_hG_hq=\Delta_hq$. Periodic summation shows both $G_hq$ and $A_hG_hq$ have zero component means, hence the force is admissible.

Substituting $\widetilde u^{n+1}=G_hq$ and $u^n=p^n=0$ into the predictor equation [F2] gives $k^{-1}G_hq+\nu A_hG_hq=f^{n+1}$, so uniqueness [F3] identifies it as the predictor. For the pressure equation, $$ \Delta_h(k^{-1}q)=k^{-1}D_hG_hq=k^{-1}D_h\widetilde u^{n+1}; $$ both sides have mean zero and [F3] gives $\phi^{n+1}=k^{-1}q$.
The velocity update [F2] now gives $u^{n+1}=G_hq-kG_h(k^{-1}q)=0$, while the pressure update gives $p^{n+1}=k^{-1}q$. This is exact one-step removal of the selected mode.

derivations.claim: If $V=\{0\}$, the identity $LT=I_U$ forces $U=\{0\}$ and $G$ has no eigenvalues, so the assertion holds with the stated zero-space norm convention. Assume henceforth $V\ne\{0\}$. Put $D=T^TAT$, which is SPD because $T$ is injective (if $Tu=0$, then $u=LT u=0$), and $C=LA^{-1}L^T$, which is SPD because $L$ is onto (it has right inverse $T$). Hence $G=CD$ is similar to the symmetric positive definite matrix $D^{1/2}CD^{1/2}$ and has positive real eigenvalues. For an eigenvector $u\ne0$ with eigenvalue $\lambda$, let $w=A^{-1}L^TDu$, so $Lw=Gu=\lambda u$ and $\|w\|_A^2=\langle Du,Gu\rangle=\lambda\langle Du,u\rangle$.

By [A1], $\langle Du,u\rangle=\langle Du,LTu\rangle=\langle Aw,Tu\rangle$. Cauchy–Schwarz in the $A$ inner product gives $\langle Du,u\rangle^2\le\|w\|_A^2\|Tu\|_A^2=\lambda\langle Du,u\rangle^2$. Dividing by the positive square gives $\lambda\ge1$.

Also $\|Gu\|_D^2=\|TLw\|_A^2\le\|TL\|_A^2\|w\|_A^2$. For the eigenvector, the left side is $\lambda^2\langle Du,u\rangle$ and step 1.1 makes the right side $\|TL\|_A^2\lambda\langle Du,u\rangle$. Divide by the positive factor to obtain $\lambda\le\|TL\|_A^2$.

Fix a bounded, connected polygonal open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^2$ with a nonempty Dirichlet boundary segment. A finite **subdomain partition** is a family of connected polygonal open sets $Ω_i$, $1\le i\le N$, whose closures cover $\overline\Omega$, whose interiors are disjoint, and for which $\overline\Omega_i\cap\overline\Omega_j$ ($i\ne j$) is a whole common side, a common vertex, or empty. The outer Dirichlet segment is a union of mesh boundary sides. The edge-adjacency graph of each triangulated subdomain is connected, and the subdomain adjacency graph is connected to the Dirichlet boundary. Each subdomain has a matching affine simplicial triangulation; the triangulations match on every shared side. The family has a fixed shape-regularity bound, quasiuniform mesh size $h_i$, uniformly bounded polygon side count, corner angles bounded below, inradius comparable to $H_i$, and a uniform interior-cone parameter. Write $H_i=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega_i)$ and $H/h=\max_i H_i/h_i$.

Use continuous piecewise-affine ($P_1$) scalar functions on each triangulation. The reference-element and face-matching conventions are those of [[def-reference-finite-element-and-unisolvent-dofs]], [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], and [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]: local polynomials are affine, their nodal values determine them, and conforming functions have equal traces across a shared side. For each subdomain choose a coefficient $\rho_i>0$, constant on $\Omega_i$ but allowed to jump across interfaces. Its local energy is

$$a_i(v,w)=\rho_i\sum_{K\subset\Omega_i}\int_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx.$$

The global finite-element space consists of the continuous piecewise-affine functions on the subdomain meshes that vanish on the outer Dirichlet boundary, with energy $a(v,w)=\sum_i a_i(v|_{\Omega_i},w|_{\Omega_i})$. Local interior degrees of freedom are the mesh vertices strictly inside $\Omega_i$; local boundary degrees of freedom are its remaining vertices, with outer Dirichlet values fixed to zero. A **floating local block** means the same local energy before any outer-boundary values are fixed. A **subdomain corner** is a vertex of its polygonal boundary.

For uniform estimates, the fixed polygon-shape parameters include the scaled Lipschitz character: after rescaling each subdomain to diameter one, its boundary has a graph-chart cover with uniformly bounded chart count and Lipschitz constants and a uniformly positive neighborhood radius. The scaled mean-zero Poincaré constants are also included among these fixed shape parameters. A pointwise interior-cone bound alone is not a substitute for this uniform boundary-chart data. All constants in later two-dimensional estimates may depend on these polygon-shape, side-count, and mesh shape-regularity bounds, but not on $h$, $H$, the number of subdomains, or the positive numbers $\rho_i$.

The assembled global Dirichlet stiffness matrix is positive definite.

For each $i$, let $W_i$ be the vector space of local boundary nodal traces compatible with the fixed outer Dirichlet values, and set $W=\prod_i W_i$ (all interface copies independent). Let $\widehat W\subset W$ be the subspace whose nodal traces agree at every shared interface node; let $R:\widehat W\to W$ be the inclusion. Choose a set of **primal constraints**, meaning finitely many linear functionals on local traces whose values are required to agree across their incident subdomains. Vertex values and normalized edge averages are examples. The **partially assembled space** $\widetilde W$ is the subspace of $W$ satisfying those primal equalities, so $\widehat W\subset\widetilde W\subset W$.

The remaining continuity equations are collected in a jump map $B:\widetilde W\to\mathbb R^m$ with $\ker B=\widehat W$. It may contain redundant rows. Fix the **redundant-multiplier convention** $\Lambda:=\operatorname{range}B$ with its inherited Euclidean inner product: multiplier vectors are elements of this range, not arbitrary row-coordinate vectors modulo an unstated choice. Then $B^T$ is injective on $\Lambda$. For the PE26 two-dimensional estimate, all subdomain vertices are primal and the only remaining jump rows are nodal differences on open interface edges, each shared by exactly two subdomains.

An interface corner is primal whenever its value is among the selected primal functionals. An **edge average** on a side $E$ is $|E|^{-1}\int_E v_h\,ds$, which is a finite sum of nodal values for a $P_1$ trace. The two-dimensional bound below uses corner constraints; no edge-average bound is claimed there.

Use the interior/interface ordering of [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]]. The boundary-trace spaces $W_i$, $W=\prod_iW_i$, the conforming space $\widehat W$, the partially assembled space $\widetilde W$, and the inclusion $R:\widehat W\to W$ are those of [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]]. $$K_i=\begin{pmatrix}K_{II}^{(i)}&K_{I\Gamma}^{(i)}\\K_{\Gamma I}^{(i)}&K_{\Gamma\Gamma}^{(i)}\end{pmatrix}.$$

By [[thm-pe26-local-energy-kernel-and-interior-spd]], $K_{II}^{(i)}$ is positive definite when nonempty; on the zero-dimensional interior space its unique endomorphism is invertible. For admissible boundary trace $g_i$, the **discrete harmonic extension** is

$$H_i g_i:=\begin{pmatrix}-(K_{II}^{(i)})^{-1}K_{I\Gamma}^{(i)}g_i\\g_i\end{pmatrix}.$$

The local **interface Schur complement** is

$$S_i:=K_{\Gamma\Gamma}^{(i)}-K_{\Gamma I}^{(i)}(K_{II}^{(i)})^{-1}K_{I\Gamma}^{(i)}.$$

This is the Schur complement in [[def-block-lu-factorisation]]. The local Schur form on a trace is $g_i^TS_i g_i$. The block identity and the associated block LU factorization use [[thm-block-lu-factorisation-via-an-invertible-leading-block]] with leading block $K_{II}^{(i)}$. Thus a zero local Schur energy is precisely zero energy of its harmonic lift. In a local dual subproblem the primal values are prescribed, so a zero-energy local vector, or the harmonic lift of a zero-energy dual trace, is constant by [F1]. A primal corner value is among its prescribed values; because the dual correction has zero primal values, that constant is zero. The local dual quadratic form therefore has trivial kernel and, being symmetric positive semidefinite, is positive definite.

For $g=(g_i)\in\widetilde W$, [F3] and step 1.1 give $g^T\widetilde Sg=\sum_i g_i^TS_i g_i=\sum_i(H_i g_i)^TK_i(H_i g_i)$. Each summand is a nonnegative local energy. derivations.claim: Let $f_i=(f_I^{(i)},f_\Gamma^{(i)})^T$ be local load contributions whose assembly is the chosen global Galerkin load vector, as specified above. The global interior rows are local to each subdomain and give $$u_I^{(i)}=(K_{II}^{(i)})^{-1}(f_I^{(i)}-K_{I\Gamma}^{(i)}u_\Gamma^{(i)}).$$ The local interface residual contribution is $K_{\Gamma I}^{(i)}u_I^{(i)}+K_{\Gamma\Gamma}^{(i)}u_\Gamma^{(i)}-f_\Gamma^{(i)}$. Substituting the interior formula makes it $S_i u_\Gamma^{(i)}-(f_\Gamma^{(i)}-K_{\Gamma I}^{(i)}(K_{II}^{(i)})^{-1}f_I^{(i)})$, precisely the local Schur contribution in [F3]. The global interface rows are the assembled sum of these contributions, not separate local interface equations.

Sum the reduced equations from step 1.1 over subdomains and identify copies of each shared nodal value as in [F1]. Because both the stiffness and the local load vectors assemble by summing their shared interface components, this gives the assembled interface Schur system with the correspondingly reduced global right-hand side. Any solution of the original global system yields this trace. Conversely, a solution of the assembled interface system and the uniquely defined interior values from step 1.1 satisfy every local interior equation and the assembled sum of interface equations, hence the assembled global system.

The global stiffness is positive definite by [F4], so the original solution is unique. Once the interface trace is solved, each local interior vector is exactly the reconstruction formula in step 1.1, which is unique because $K_{II}^{(i)}$ is invertible. Its trace-dependent homogeneous part is $H_i u_\Gamma^{(i)}$ from [F2]. Therefore static condensation is exact in both directions.

citations.quote:
Fix a bounded, connected polygonal open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^2$ with a nonempty Dirichlet boundary segment. A finite **subdomain partition** is a family of connected polygonal open sets $Ω_i$, $1\le i\le N$, whose closures cover $\overline\Omega$, whose interiors are disjoint, and for which $\overline\Omega_i\cap\overline\Omega_j$ ($i\ne j$) is a whole common side, a common vertex, or empty. The outer Dirichlet segment is a union of mesh boundary sides. The edge-adjacency graph of each triangulated subdomain is connected, and the subdomain adjacency graph is connected to the Dirichlet boundary. Each subdomain has a matching affine simplicial triangulation; the triangulations match on every shared side. The family has a fixed shape-regularity bound, quasiuniform mesh size $h_i$, uniformly bounded polygon side count, corner angles bounded below, inradius comparable to $H_i$, and a uniform interior-cone parameter. Write $H_i=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega_i)$ and $H/h=\max_i H_i/h_i$.

Use continuous piecewise-affine ($P_1$) scalar functions on each triangulation. The reference-element and face-matching conventions are those of [[def-reference-finite-element-and-unisolvent-dofs]], [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], and [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]: local polynomials are affine, their nodal values determine them, and conforming functions have equal traces across a shared side. For each subdomain choose a coefficient $\rho_i>0$, constant on $\Omega_i$ but allowed to jump across interfaces. Its local energy is

$$a_i(v,w)=\rho_i\sum_{K\subset\Omega_i}\int_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx.$$

The global finite-element space consists of the continuous piecewise-affine functions on the subdomain meshes that vanish on the outer Dirichlet boundary, with energy $a(v,w)=\sum_i a_i(v|_{\Omega_i},w|_{\Omega_i})$. Local interior degrees of freedom are the mesh vertices strictly inside $\Omega_i$; local boundary degrees of freedom are its remaining vertices, with outer Dirichlet values fixed to zero. A **floating local block** means the same local energy before any outer-boundary values are fixed. A **subdomain corner** is a vertex of its polygonal boundary.

For uniform estimates, the fixed polygon-shape parameters include the scaled Lipschitz character: after rescaling each subdomain to diameter one, its boundary has a graph-chart cover with uniformly bounded chart count and Lipschitz constants and a uniformly positive neighborhood radius. The scaled mean-zero Poincaré constants are also included among these fixed shape parameters. A pointwise interior-cone bound alone is not a substitute for this uniform boundary-chart data. All constants in later two-dimensional estimates may depend on these polygon-shape, side-count, and mesh shape-regularity bounds, but not on $h$, $H$, the number of subdomains, or the positive numbers $\rho_i$.

Use the interior/interface ordering of [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]]. The boundary-trace spaces $W_i$, $W=\prod_iW_i$, the conforming space $\widehat W$, the partially assembled space $\widetilde W$, and the inclusion $R:\widehat W\to W$ are those of [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]]. In particular, $R$ identifies the copies of a conforming interface trace. In subdomain $i$, write its stiffness matrix as

$$K_i=\begin{pmatrix}K_{II}^{(i)}&K_{I\Gamma}^{(i)}\\K_{\Gamma I}^{(i)}&K_{\Gamma\Gamma}^{(i)}\end{pmatrix}.$$

By [[thm-pe26-local-energy-kernel-and-interior-spd]], $K_{II}^{(i)}$ is positive definite when nonempty; on the zero-dimensional interior space its unique endomorphism is invertible. For admissible boundary trace $g_i$, the **discrete harmonic extension** is

$$H_i g_i:=\begin{pmatrix}-(K_{II}^{(i)})^{-1}K_{I\Gamma}^{(i)}g_i\\g_i\end{pmatrix}.$$

The local **interface Schur complement** is

$$S_i:=K_{\Gamma\Gamma}^{(i)}-K_{\Gamma I}^{(i)}(K_{II}^{(i)})^{-1}K_{I\Gamma}^{(i)}.$$

This is the Schur complement in [[def-block-lu-factorisation]]. The local Schur form on a trace is $g_i^TS_i g_i$. The block identity and the associated block LU factorization use [[thm-block-lu-factorisation-via-an-invertible-leading-block]] with leading block $K_{II}^{(i)}$. Assembling local Schur forms on $\widehat W$ gives $\widehat S=R^T(\operatorname{diag}_i S_i)R$; restricting the same block-diagonal form to $\widetilde W$ gives the partially assembled operator $\widetilde S$.

For every admissible local trace $g_i$, $H_i g_i$ from [[def-pe26-discrete-harmonic-extension-and-schur-complement]] is the unique finite-element function with trace $g_i$ minimizing $a_i(v,v)$. The minimum is $g_i^TS_i g_i$.

derivations.claim: On the upper half-plane, Fourier transformation in the tangential variable gives, for a smooth lift $V$ with trace $g$, $$|\xi||\widehat g(\xi)|^2\le\int_0^\infty\bigl(|\partial_t\widehat V(\xi,t)|^2+|\xi|^2|\widehat V(\xi,t)|^2\bigr)\,dt.$$ Indeed, integrate $-\partial_t|\widehat V|^2$ and apply $2ab\le a^2+b^2$. Integration in $\xi$ proves the trace seminorm bound. Conversely, $\widehat V(\xi,t)=e^{-t|\xi|}\widehat g(\xi)$ has gradient energy $\int |\xi||\widehat g(\xi)|^2\,d\xi$. In a bounded chart, multiply the half-plane extension by a fixed cutoff in the inward coordinate; the added gradient term is controlled by the localized $L^2$ boundary norm, hence by the full H1/2 norm after constants are removed. A finite collection of Lipschitz graph charts covers the polygon boundary, including its corners. Flattening each chart is bi-Lipschitz, so it changes the $H^1$ gradient and boundary Gagliardo seminorm by bounded factors. Applying a partition of unity and the half-plane trace inequality to arbitrary chart-localized lifts gives $|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}\le C\|V\|_{H^1(\Omega_i)}$. Subtract the domain mean of $V$ and use scaled Poincar\'e to replace the full $H^1$ norm by $\|\nabla V\|_{L^2}$. In the other direction, apply a partition of unity to boundary data, use the half-plane extensions, and sum to obtain a right inverse of the trace. First subtract a boundary constant; the fractional Poincaré bound on the whole boundary controls the localized full norms: for the boundary mean $c$, $\|g-c\|_{L^2(\partial\Omega_i)}^2\le H_i^2|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}^2/(2|\partial\Omega_i|)$, by integrating $|s-t|\le H_i$. Add that constant back as a constant lift, which has zero gradient. The chart count, scaled radii, Lipschitz constants and mean-zero Poincaré bounds are precisely the fixed shape parameters in [F1]; a pointwise interior-cone condition alone would not justify this uniformity.

Construct an interpolant $I_h:H^1(\Omega_i)	o V_h$ as follows. For each interior mesh vertex choose one incident triangle and set its coefficient to the average of $V$ on that triangle. For each boundary vertex choose one incident boundary edge and set its coefficient to the integral of the trace of $V$ against the $L^2$-dual function to the endpoint nodal basis on that edge. These dual functionals reproduce every affine edge trace, so the trace of $I_hV$ is exactly $g$ whenever the trace of $V$ is $g$. All coefficients reproduce constants. For a triangle $K$, the chosen elements and edges for its vertices lie in a connected patch $\omega_K$ of diameter at most $Ch$ containing a uniformly bounded number of triangles; these patches have bounded overlap. Let $c_K$ be the mean of $V$ on $\omega_K$. Scaled Poincaré gives $\|V-c_K\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}\le Ch\|
abla V\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}$, and the scaled trace inequality gives $\|V-c_K\|_{L^2(e)}\le Ch^{1/2}\|
abla V\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}$ on a selected boundary edge $e$. Thus each interior average coefficient of $V-c_K$ is bounded by $C\|
abla V\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}$. A boundary dual function has $L^2(e)$ norm at most $Ch^{-1/2}$, so its coefficient has the same bound. Since $I_hc_K=c_K$ and the affine basis functions have uniformly bounded $L^2(K)$ gradient norms in two dimensions, $\|
abla I_hV\|_{L^2(K)}\le C\|
abla V\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}$. Summing and using bounded overlap proves $\|
abla I_hV\|_{L^2(\Omega_i)}\le C\|
abla V\|_{L^2(\Omega_i)}$.

For any finite-element lift $v_h$ of $g$, step 1.1 gives $|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}^2\le C\|\nabla v_h\|_{L^2(\Omega_i)}^2$. For the floating matrix, put $H^{\rm fl}g=(-K_{II}^{-1}K_{I\Gamma}g,g)^T$. Symmetry of the local Poisson form and its zero interior row give $a_i(H^{\rm fl}g+(z,0),H^{\rm fl}g+(z,0))=g^TS_i^{\rm fl}g+z^TK_{II}z$. The positive interior block from [F2] therefore makes $g^TS_i^{\rm fl}g$ the unique fixed-trace minimum, by the same identity as [F3]. Taking that minimum gives the lower Schur bound. For the upper bound, step 1.1 supplies a continuous lift $V$ with gradient energy at most $C|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}^2$, and step 1.2 gives a boundary-preserving finite-element lift $I_hV$ with the same bound up to a uniform factor. The just-proved floating minimality bounds its energy by this lift. Multiplication by $\rho_i$ proves both inequalities. If $g$ is admissible, the fixed-trace feasible lifts already vanish on the outer Dirichlet portion; [F2]–[F3] identify the same minimum with $g^TS_i g$.

Use the spaces and partial Schur operator of [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and [[def-pe26-discrete-harmonic-extension-and-schur-complement]]. Let $E_0:\widetilde W\to\widehat W$ average every remaining interface degree of freedom and preserve every already-shared primal value. It is a scaled average if the weights for all copies of each such degree of freedom sum to one. Put $\bar E:=R E_0:\widetilde W\to\widetilde W$. Then $E_0R=I_{\widehat W}$ and $\bar E$ is a projection onto $\widehat W$.

In the PE26 two-dimensional corner-constraint branch, each non-primal node is interior to one interface edge shared by exactly two subdomains $i,j$. Set

$$ (E_0w)(x)=\frac{\rho_i}{\rho_i+\rho_j}w_i(x)+\frac{\rho_j}{\rho_i+\rho_j}w_j(x). $$

At primal nodes the copies already agree, so the average is the common value. For any finite-dimensional positive definite partial Schur operator $\widetilde S$, the **BDDC preconditioner** is

$$M_{\rm BDDC}^{-1}:=E_0\widetilde S^{-1}E_0^T:\widehat W'\to\widehat W,$$

for the assembled interface system with operator $\widehat S=R^T\widetilde S R$. Its constrained partial-energy interpretation is established in [[prop-pe26-bddc-constrained-local-minimization]].

Assume the hypotheses of [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and the energy setting of [[thm-pe26-local-energy-kernel-and-interior-spd]]. If each floating local component has at least one primal vertex value fixed in its dual subproblem, its local dual stiffness is positive definite. derivations.claim: Differentiating the finite-dimensional quadratic in a direction $z\in\widetilde W$ gives $J_f'(w)[z]=\langle\widetilde S w,z\rangle-\langle f,E_0z\rangle$. Thus its critical point solves $\widetilde S w=E_0^Tf$, whose unique solution is $w_*=\widetilde S^{-1}E_0^T f$.

For any $z\in\widetilde W$, expansion about the critical point yields $J_f(w_*+z)=J_f(w_*)+\tfrac12\langle\widetilde S z,z\rangle$. By [F2] the added term is positive unless $z=0$, so $w_*$ is the unique global minimizer. Applying $E_0$ gives the displayed BDDC correction by [F1].

This gives linear B_D^T, BB_D^T=I and B_D^TB=I-Ebar. Explicit SPD of tilde S licenses its inverse for all admissible primal choices; the all-corners theorem is only a sufficient PE26 branch. Range multipliers and the stated Euclidean identification type both transpose formulas and remove redundant rows. For zero jump space the identities remain valid; two-edge coefficients are complementary averaging weights. No arbitrary choice is used. Compared with Mandel–Sousedik §§3.1,3.3, equations (3)–(7),(22)–(23), and Widlund slides 83–90. No item edit or new mathematical acceptance is recorded.

citations.quote:
Fix a bounded, connected polygonal open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^2$ with a nonempty Dirichlet boundary segment. A finite **subdomain partition** is a family of connected polygonal open sets $Ω_i$, $1\le i\le N$, whose closures cover $\overline\Omega$, whose interiors are disjoint, and for which $\overline\Omega_i\cap\overline\Omega_j$ ($i\ne j$) is a whole common side, a common vertex, or empty. The outer Dirichlet segment is a union of mesh boundary sides. The edge-adjacency graph of each triangulated subdomain is connected, and the subdomain adjacency graph is connected to the Dirichlet boundary. Each subdomain has a matching affine simplicial triangulation; the triangulations match on every shared side. The family has a fixed shape-regularity bound, quasiuniform mesh size $h_i$, uniformly bounded polygon side count, corner angles bounded below, inradius comparable to $H_i$, and a uniform interior-cone parameter. Write $H_i=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega_i)$ and $H/h=\max_i H_i/h_i$.

Use continuous piecewise-affine ($P_1$) scalar functions on each triangulation. The reference-element and face-matching conventions are those of [[def-reference-finite-element-and-unisolvent-dofs]], [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], and [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]: local polynomials are affine, their nodal values determine them, and conforming functions have equal traces across a shared side. For each subdomain choose a coefficient $\rho_i>0$, constant on $\Omega_i$ but allowed to jump across interfaces. Its local energy is

$$a_i(v,w)=\rho_i\sum_{K\subset\Omega_i}\int_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx.$$

The global finite-element space consists of the continuous piecewise-affine functions on the subdomain meshes that vanish on the outer Dirichlet boundary, with energy $a(v,w)=\sum_i a_i(v|_{\Omega_i},w|_{\Omega_i})$. Local interior degrees of freedom are the mesh vertices strictly inside $\Omega_i$; local boundary degrees of freedom are its remaining vertices, with outer Dirichlet values fixed to zero. A **floating local block** means the same local energy before any outer-boundary values are fixed. A **subdomain corner** is a vertex of its polygonal boundary.

For uniform estimates, the fixed polygon-shape parameters include the scaled Lipschitz character: after rescaling each subdomain to diameter one, its boundary has a graph-chart cover with uniformly bounded chart count and Lipschitz constants and a uniformly positive neighborhood radius. The scaled mean-zero Poincaré constants are also included among these fixed shape parameters. A pointwise interior-cone bound alone is not a substitute for this uniform boundary-chart data. All constants in later two-dimensional estimates may depend on these polygon-shape, side-count, and mesh shape-regularity bounds, but not on $h$, $H$, the number of subdomains, or the positive numbers $\rho_i$.

Let $\Omega_i$ be one of the shape-regular polygonal subdomains in [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]], with a matching quasiuniform $P_1$ mesh. For any continuous piecewise-linear boundary trace $g$, let $S_i^{\rm fl}$ be the Schur complement of the floating local stiffness matrix, before outer Dirichlet values are fixed, formed by the same interior elimination as in [[def-pe26-discrete-harmonic-extension-and-schur-complement]]. Define

$$|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}^2:=\int_{\partial\Omega_i}\int_{\partial\Omega_i}\frac{|g(s)-g(t)|^2}{|s-t|^2}\,ds\,dt.$$

This seminorm is taken modulo constants. The floating local Schur energy satisfies

$$c\rho_i|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}^2\le g^TS_i^{\rm fl} g\le C\rho_i|g|_{1/2,\partial\Omega_i}^2,$$

where $c,C>0$ depend only on the fixed scaled polygon-shape parameters (including boundary-chart and mean-zero Poincaré bounds), mesh shape-regularity and quasiuniformity. The upper bound is realized by a boundary-preserving finite-element lifting; the minimum-energy lifting is the floating discrete harmonic extension. For an admissible trace $g$, whose outer Dirichlet values are zero, $g^TS_i^{\rm fl}g=g^TS_i g$ for the Dirichlet-restricted Schur matrix of [[def-pe26-discrete-harmonic-extension-and-schur-complement]], so the same inequalities hold for that matrix on its domain.

derivations.claim: If $E$ has no interior boundary node, then $\theta_E=0$. If $|E|/h\le4$, scaling $E$ to unit length gives a uniform bound on both terms of $\|\theta_E\|_{00,E}^2$. Otherwise the first and last mesh intervals have length comparable to $h$, $\theta_E$ is linear from $0$ to $1$ and from $1$ to $0$ there, and it equals $1$ between them. The weighted integral on either endpoint interval is bounded by $\int_0^h(s/h)^2\,ds/s\le C$; the plateau contributes at most $C+\log(|E|/h)\le C+\log(H/h)$. In the double integral, pairs in the plateau contribute zero. Pairs within one endpoint interval have integrand at most $Ch^{-2}$ and hence contribute at most a constant. For one point $s$ in an endpoint interval and one outside it, integrating $(1-s/h)^2/(t-s)^2$ in the outside variable and then in $s$ gives a constant; the two endpoint intervals are treated in the same way. Therefore $\|\theta_E\|_{00,E}^2\le C(1+\log(H/h))$.

Put $v_h=u_h-\overline u_{\Omega_i}$, $H=H_i$, $h=h_i$ and $G=\|
abla v_h\|_{L^2(\Omega_i)}$. Choose a triangle $K$ containing a point where $|v_h|$ is maximal, and let $x_0$ be its centroid. Affine scaling gives $\|v_h\|_\infty\le |v_h(x_0)|+CG$. The uniform interior-cone condition in [F1] supplies at $x_0$ a cone of radius $R=cH$ and angular interval $J$ of fixed positive length, contained in $\Omega_i$. Quasiuniformity and affine scaling give the global inverse bound $\|
abla v_h\|_\infty\le Ch^{-1}G$. If $H/h$ is bounded, the inverse bound $\|v_h\|_\infty\le Ch^{-1}\|v_h\|_{L^2}$ and mean-zero scaled Poincaré prove the claim directly. Otherwise choose $\varepsilon=c'h<R/2$. Along each cone ray, the integral of $|
abla v_h|$ from $0$ to $\varepsilon$ is at most $CG$, while weighted Cauchy–Schwarz gives $$\left|\int_\varepsilon^r\partial_s v_h(x_0+s e_	heta)\,dsight|^2\le\log(R/\varepsilon)\int_\varepsilon^R|
abla v_h(x_0+s e_	heta)|^2s\,ds.$$ Express $v_h(x_0)$ by its value at $x_0+r e_	heta$ minus these two radial integrals, square, and average with measure $r\,dr\,d	heta$ over $R/2<r<R$, $	heta\in J$. The annulus has area comparable to $H^2$; the ray-energy term is independent of $r$ and integrates in $	heta$ to at most $G^2$. Hence $$|v_h(x_0)|^2\le C H^{-2}\|v_h\|_{L^2}^2+C(1+\log(H/h))G^2.$$ Mean-zero scaled Poincaré bounds the first term by $CG^2$, and the centroid comparison proves the asserted $L^\infty$ estimate. This is the radial argument underlying Widlund's estimate (5), with the centroid-to-maximum comparison included explicitly.

Put $z=u_h-\overline u_E$. In the first Gagliardo term use $$\theta(s)z(s)-\theta(t)z(t)=\theta(s)(z(s)-z(t))+z(t)(\theta(s)-\theta(t)).$$ The weighted term is bounded by $\|z\|_\infty^2\int_E\theta_E^2/\operatorname{dist}(s,\partial E)\,ds$. Together these give $$\|\theta_Ez\|_{00,E}^2\le C\left(|z|_{H^{1/2}(E)}^2+(1+\log(H/h))\|z\|_\infty^2\right).$$ On the two endpoint mesh intervals, $I_h(\theta_Ez)-\theta_Ez$ is a quadratic interpolation error vanishing at both endpoints; scaling the interval to unit length bounds its $00,E$ norm by $C\|z\|_\infty^2$. The same estimate therefore holds for $I_h(\theta_Ez)$. The floating local Schur energy of the trace of $u_h$ is at most $\rho_i\|\nabla u_h\|_{L^2(\Omega_i)}^2$ because it is the minimum over finite-element lifts; the lower trace-Schur bound in [F2] therefore gives $|z|_{H^{1/2}(E)}^2\le C\|\nabla u_h\|_{L^2(\Omega_i)}^2$. Also $|\overline u_E-\overline u_{\Omega_i}|\le\|u_h-\overline u_{\Omega_i}\|_{L^\infty(\Omega_i)}$, so $\|z\|_\infty\le2\|u_h-\overline u_{\Omega_i}\|_{L^\infty(\Omega_i)}$. Combining this with steps 1.1 and 1.2 proves the claimed squared-logarithmic multiplier estimate.

Use $\widetilde W$, $\widehat W$, $E_0$, $R$, $B$ and $\Lambda=\operatorname{range}B$ as defined in [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and [[def-pe26-scaled-averaging-and-bddc-preconditioner]]. Assume that $\widetilde S:\widetilde W\to\widetilde W'$ is symmetric positive definite. In the PE26 corner branch this follows from [[thm-pe26-primal-constraints-remove-floating-kernels]] when all subdomain vertices are primal and the global Dirichlet boundary is nonempty; for other primal choices it is a separate admissibility requirement. Use the inherited Euclidean inner product to identify $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda'$ in the transpose and coordinate formulas below. Regard $\bar E=R E_0$ as a projection on $\widetilde W$. Since $\ker B=\operatorname{range}\bar E=\widehat W$, each class of traces with the same jump has a unique representative in $\ker\bar E$. Define $B_D^T:\Lambda\to\widetilde W$ by assigning to $\lambda\in\Lambda$ that unique representative $w$ with $Bw=\lambda$ and $\bar Ew=0$. This is the scaled right inverse; it obeys $BB_D^T=I_\Lambda$ and $B_D^TB=I_{\widetilde W}-\bar E$. The latter identity makes the primal and dual projections complementary. In the two-subdomain edge case, its two entries are the coefficient-scaled jump weights complementary to those in $E_0$.

The **FETI-DP dual operator** and its preconditioner are

$$F:=B\widetilde S^{-1}B^T:\Lambda\to\Lambda',\qquad M_{\rm FETI-DP}^{-1}:=B_D\widetilde S B_D^T:\Lambda'\to\Lambda.$$

The multiplier convention removes dependent row coordinates: $\lambda$ is in $\operatorname{range}B$, so no arbitrary multiplier component in $\ker B^T$ is retained. Elimination of the partially assembled displacement and the resulting exact dual system are proved in [[prop-pe26-feti-dp-is-dual-schur-complement]].

For each $i$, let $W_i$ be the vector space of local boundary nodal traces compatible with the fixed outer Dirichlet values, and set $W=\prod_i W_i$ (all interface copies independent). Let $\widehat W\subset W$ be the subspace whose nodal traces agree at every shared interface node; let $R:\widehat W\to W$ be the inclusion. Choose a set of **primal constraints**, meaning finitely many linear functionals on local traces whose values are required to agree across their incident subdomains. Vertex values and normalized edge averages are examples. The **partially assembled space** $\widetilde W$ is the subspace of $W$ satisfying those primal equalities, so $\widehat W\subset\widetilde W\subset W$.

The remaining continuity equations are collected in a jump map $B:\widetilde W\to\mathbb R^m$ with $\ker B=\widehat W$. It may contain redundant rows. Fix the **redundant-multiplier convention** $\Lambda:=\operatorname{range}B$ with its inherited Euclidean inner product: multiplier vectors are elements of this range, not arbitrary row-coordinate vectors modulo an unstated choice. Then $B^T$ is injective on $\Lambda$. For the PE26 two-dimensional estimate, all subdomain vertices are primal and the only remaining jump rows are nodal differences on open interface edges, each shared by exactly two subdomains.

An interface corner is primal whenever its value is among the selected primal functionals. An **edge average** on a side $E$ is $|E|^{-1}\int_E v_h\,ds$, which is a finite sum of nodal values for a $P_1$ trace. The two-dimensional bound below uses corner constraints; no edge-average bound is claimed there.

Assume the hypotheses of [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and the energy setting of [[thm-pe26-local-energy-kernel-and-interior-spd]]. If each floating local component has at least one primal vertex value fixed in its dual subproblem, its local dual stiffness is positive definite. If all subdomain vertices are primal and the global Dirichlet boundary is nonempty, the partially assembled interface energy is positive definite; hence the BDDC and FETI-DP exact local and coarse solves are well-defined.

derivations.claim: The Lagrangian is $L(w,\lambda)=\tfrac12\langle\widetilde S w,w\rangle-\langle E_0^Tf,w\rangle+\langle\lambda,Bw\rangle$. Its derivative in arbitrary $z\in\widetilde W$ is $\langle\widetilde S w+B^T\lambda-E_0^Tf,z\rangle$, and its multiplier derivative is $Bw$. Setting both derivatives to zero gives the displayed saddle equations.
By the assumed positive definiteness of $\widetilde S$, the first equation has the unique solution $w=\widetilde S^{-1}(E_0^Tf-B^T\lambda)$. Substitution into $Bw=0$ gives the displayed dual system.

If $\lambda\in\Lambda$ and $B^T\lambda=0$, write $\lambda=Bv$ using [F2]. Then $\langle\lambda,\lambda\rangle=\langle Bv,\lambda\rangle=\langle v,B^T\lambda\rangle=0$, hence $\lambda=0$. Thus $B^T$ is injective on $\Lambda$, and $\langle F\lambda,\lambda\rangle=\langle\widetilde S^{-1}B^T\lambda,B^T\lambda\rangle>0$ for every nonzero $\lambda$. The exact solution satisfies $Bw=0$, so by [F2] it lies in $\widehat W$ and solves the assembled variational problem.

derivations.claim: The products $G_1$ and $G_2$ act on $U_1$ and $U_2'$, respectively. Set $X=L_1A^{-1}L_2^T:U_2'\to U_1$ and $Y=T_2^TAT_1:U_1\to U_2'$. By the given hypotheses, $L_1T_1=I$, $L_2T_2=I$, and $T_1L_1+T_2L_2=I$. Expanding the products gives $G_1-I=-XY$ and $G_2-I=-YX$. In detail, $G_1-I=L_1A^{-1}((T_1L_1)^T-I)AT_1=-L_1A^{-1}L_2^TT_2^TAT_1$; also $YX=T_2^T A(I-T_2L_2)A^{-1}L_2^T=I-G_2$.

If $u\in U_1$ satisfies $G_1u=\lambda u$ with $\lambda\ne1$, then $XYu=(1-\lambda)u$, so $Yu\ne0$. The identity $G_2-I=-YX$ gives $(G_2-I)Yu=-YXYu=(\lambda-1)Yu$, hence $G_2(Yu)=\lambda Yu$. For $v\in U_2'$, the reverse map is $v\mapsto-Xv/(\lambda-1)$; the same identities show it is the inverse on the $\lambda$-eigenspaces. Thus these eigenspaces are isomorphic.

Choose bases of the finite-dimensional spaces and their dual bases. Both operators are diagonalizable: $T_1^TAT_1$ and $L_1A^{-1}L_1^T$ are positive definite, so, writing $D_1=T_1^TAT_1$, $G_1$ is similar to the symmetric positive definite product $D_1^{1/2}(L_1A^{-1}L_1^T)D_1^{1/2}$; likewise $G_2$ is similar to $D_2^{1/2}(L_2A^{-1}L_2^T)D_2^{1/2}$, where $D_2=T_2^TAT_2$. The left-inverse identities make $T_i$ injective and $L_i$ surjective, proving each factor is positive definite. Therefore equal eigenspace dimensions from step 2.1 give equal algebraic multiplicities for every $\lambda\ne1$.

$$M_{\rm BDDC}^{-1}:=E_0\widetilde S^{-1}E_0^T:\widehat W'\to\widehat W,$$

Use $\widetilde W$, $\widehat W$, $E_0$, $R$, $B$ and $\Lambda=\operatorname{range}B$ as defined in [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and [[def-pe26-scaled-averaging-and-bddc-preconditioner]]. Fix a bounded, connected polygonal open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^2$ with a nonempty Dirichlet boundary segment. A finite **subdomain partition** is a family of connected polygonal open sets $Ω_i$, $1\le i\le N$, whose closures cover $\overline\Omega$, whose interiors are disjoint, and for which $\overline\Omega_i\cap\overline\Omega_j$ ($i\ne j$) is a whole common side, a common vertex, or empty. The outer Dirichlet segment is a union of mesh boundary sides. The edge-adjacency graph of each triangulated subdomain is connected, and the subdomain adjacency graph is connected to the Dirichlet boundary. Each subdomain has a matching affine simplicial triangulation; the triangulations match on every shared side. The family has a fixed shape-regularity bound, quasiuniform mesh size $h_i$, uniformly bounded polygon side count, corner angles bounded below, inradius comparable to $H_i$, and a uniform interior-cone parameter. Write $H_i=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega_i)$ and $H/h=\max_i H_i/h_i$.

Use continuous piecewise-affine ($P_1$) scalar functions on each triangulation. The reference-element and face-matching conventions are those of [[def-reference-finite-element-and-unisolvent-dofs]], [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], and [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]: local polynomials are affine, their nodal values determine them, and conforming functions have equal traces across a shared side. For each subdomain choose a coefficient $\rho_i>0$, constant on $\Omega_i$ but allowed to jump across interfaces. Its local energy is

$$a_i(v,w)=\rho_i\sum_{K\subset\Omega_i}\int_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx.$$

The global finite-element space consists of the continuous piecewise-affine functions on the subdomain meshes that vanish on the outer Dirichlet boundary, with energy $a(v,w)=\sum_i a_i(v|_{\Omega_i},w|_{\Omega_i})$. Local interior degrees of freedom are the mesh vertices strictly inside $\Omega_i$; local boundary degrees of freedom are its remaining vertices, with outer Dirichlet values fixed to zero. A **floating local block** means the same local energy before any outer-boundary values are fixed. A **subdomain corner** is a vertex of its polygonal boundary.

For uniform estimates, the fixed polygon-shape parameters include the scaled Lipschitz character: after rescaling each subdomain to diameter one, its boundary has a graph-chart cover with uniformly bounded chart count and Lipschitz constants and a uniformly positive neighborhood radius. The scaled mean-zero Poincaré constants are also included among these fixed shape parameters. A pointwise interior-cone bound alone is not a substitute for this uniform boundary-chart data. All constants in later two-dimensional estimates may depend on these polygon-shape, side-count, and mesh shape-regularity bounds, but not on $h$, $H$, the number of subdomains, or the positive numbers $\rho_i$.

In the setting of [[def-pe26-scalar-substructuring-model]], the nullspace of the floating local energy matrix on a connected $\Omega_i$ is exactly the one-dimensional space of constants. The principal stiffness block $K_{II}^{(i)}$ on interior nodal values with zero boundary trace is positive definite (including the empty $0$-dimensional block convention). The assembled global Dirichlet stiffness matrix is positive definite.

Assume the hypotheses of [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and the energy setting of [[thm-pe26-local-energy-kernel-and-interior-spd]]. If each floating local component has at least one primal vertex value fixed in its dual subproblem, its local dual stiffness is positive definite. If all subdomain vertices are primal and the global Dirichlet boundary is nonempty, the partially assembled interface energy is positive definite; hence the BDDC and FETI-DP exact local and coarse solves are well-defined.

Use the spaces and partial Schur operator of [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and [[def-pe26-discrete-harmonic-extension-and-schur-complement]]. Let $E_0:\widetilde W\to\widehat W$ average every remaining interface degree of freedom and preserve every already-shared primal value. It is a scaled average if the weights for all copies of each such degree of freedom sum to one. Put $\bar E:=R E_0:\widetilde W\to\widetilde W$. Then $E_0R=I_{\widehat W}$ and $\bar E$ is a projection onto $\widehat W$.

In the PE26 two-dimensional corner-constraint branch, each non-primal node is interior to one interface edge shared by exactly two subdomains $i,j$. Set

$$ (E_0w)(x)=\frac{\rho_i}{\rho_i+\rho_j}w_i(x)+\frac{\rho_j}{\rho_i+\rho_j}w_j(x). $$

At primal nodes the copies already agree, so the average is the common value. For any finite-dimensional positive definite partial Schur operator $\widetilde S$, the **BDDC preconditioner** is

$$M_{\rm BDDC}^{-1}:=E_0\widetilde S^{-1}E_0^T:\widehat W'\to\widehat W,$$

for the assembled interface system with operator $\widehat S=R^T\widetilde S R$. Its constrained partial-energy interpretation is established in [[prop-pe26-bddc-constrained-local-minimization]].

Use $\widetilde W$, $\widehat W$, $E_0$, $R$, $B$ and $\Lambda=\operatorname{range}B$ as defined in [[def-pe26-primal-interface-spaces-and-jumps]] and [[def-pe26-scaled-averaging-and-bddc-preconditioner]]. Assume that $\widetilde S:\widetilde W\to\widetilde W'$ is symmetric positive definite. In the PE26 corner branch this follows from [[thm-pe26-primal-constraints-remove-floating-kernels]] when all subdomain vertices are primal and the global Dirichlet boundary is nonempty; for other primal choices it is a separate admissibility requirement. Use the inherited Euclidean inner product to identify $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda'$ in the transpose and coordinate formulas below. Regard $\bar E=R E_0$ as a projection on $\widetilde W$. Since $\ker B=\operatorname{range}\bar E=\widehat W$, each class of traces with the same jump has a unique representative in $\ker\bar E$. Define $B_D^T:\Lambda\to\widetilde W$ by assigning to $\lambda\in\Lambda$ that unique representative $w$ with $Bw=\lambda$ and $\bar Ew=0$. This is the scaled right inverse; it obeys $BB_D^T=I_\Lambda$ and $B_D^TB=I_{\widetilde W}-\bar E$. The latter identity makes the primal and dual projections complementary. In the two-subdomain edge case, its two entries are the coefficient-scaled jump weights complementary to those in $E_0$.

The **FETI-DP dual operator** and its preconditioner are

$$F:=B\widetilde S^{-1}B^T:\Lambda\to\Lambda',\qquad M_{\rm FETI-DP}^{-1}:=B_D\widetilde S B_D^T:\Lambda'\to\Lambda.$$

The multiplier convention removes dependent row coordinates: $\lambda$ is in $\operatorname{range}B$, so no arbitrary multiplier component in $\ker B^T$ is retained. Elimination of the partially assembled displacement and the resulting exact dual system are proved in [[prop-pe26-feti-dp-is-dual-schur-complement]].

For BDDC and FETI-DP built from the same positive definite partially assembled Schur operator, primal constraints, and scaled averaging, all eigenvalues of the two preconditioned operators other than $1$ agree with multiplicity. With the multiplier space fixed as $\Lambda=\operatorname{range}B$, neither operator has a zero eigenvalue; retaining all redundant row coordinates instead would add only multiplier null modes that are removed by this convention. The multiplicity of $1$ is not asserted to agree.

Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $m \ge 1$ and let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$.

1. **Fundamental theorem, second part, in $\mathbb{R}^{m}$.** Let
   $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ be differentiable at every point of $[a,b]$ as
   a function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]), and
   suppose $f' : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ is integrable. Then
   $$\int_a^b f' \;=\; f(b) - f(a).$$
2. **A bounded derivative gives a Lipschitz function.** Let
   $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^{m}$ be continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable at
   every point of $(a,b)$, and let $M \ge 0$ satisfy
   $\lVert f'(t)\rVert_2 \le M$ for every $t \in (a,b)$. Then
   $$\lVert f(t) - f(s)\rVert_2 \;\le\; M\,|t-s| \qquad \text{for all } s,t \in [a,b],$$
   that is, $f$ is Lipschitz with constant $M$ as a map
   $([a,b], d_{\mathbb{R}}) \to (\mathbb{R}^{m}, d_2)$
   ([[def-lipschitz-holder-contraction]], [[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]],
   [[lem-metrics-on-rn]]).

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be
conjugate exponents, and let $f,g$ be measurable real-valued functions.

1. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $q<\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^q(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q.$$
2. If $p=1$ and $q=\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$ and
   $g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_1\|g\|_\infty.$$
3. If $p=\infty$ and $q=1$ with $f\in L^\infty(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_1.$$

In every case the right-hand side is finite, so $fg$ is integrable.

derivations.claim: First let $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ and extend it by zero to $\mathbb R^d$. Write $x=x_\perp+te$ with $x_\perp\perp e$. For fixed $x_\perp$ and $a<t<b$, the fundamental theorem [F1] gives $\varphi(x_\perp+te)=\int_a^t\partial_e\varphi(x_\perp+se)\,ds$, since the zero extension vanishes at $t=a$. Holder's inequality [F4], applied on $(a,t)$ and then enlarged to $(a,b)$, yields $|\varphi(x_\perp+te)|^2\le(b-a)\int_a^b|\partial_e\varphi(x_\perp+se)|^2\,ds$.

Integrate step 1.1 over $t\in(a,b)$ and $x_\perp\in e^\perp$. Choose an orthonormal basis of $e^\perp$ and let $Q$ have those basis vectors followed by $e$ as its columns. Then $T(y)=Qy$ sends $(y_\perp,t)$ to $x_\perp+te$; Tonelli [F2] and $Q^TQ=I$, $|\det Q|=1$ in [F3] give the coordinate integral over the slab. The zero extension of $\varphi$ and its derivative vanish off $\Omega$, so those slab integrals equal their integrals over $\Omega$. Thus $\|\varphi\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\le(b-a)^2\|\partial_e\varphi\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\le(b-a)^2\|\nabla\varphi\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2$.

Let $\delta>0$. By the closure definition of $H^1_0(\Omega)$, choose a single $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $\|v-\varphi\|_{H^1}<\delta$. The $L^2$ triangle inequality follows by expanding $\|f+g\|_2^2$ and applying [F4] to the cross term; hence [F4] and step 2.1 give $\|v\|_2\le\|\varphi\|_2+\delta\le(b-a)\|\nabla\varphi\|_2+\delta\le(b-a)\|\nabla v\|_2+(b-a+1)\delta$. This holds for every $\delta>0$, so letting $\delta\downarrow0$ proves the statement without selecting a sequence of approximants.

Let $d\ge2$ and let $K$ be a nondegenerate affine $d$-simplex with vertices
$a_0,\ldots,a_d$ and facets $F_i$ opposite $a_i$. Write
$\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$ for its barycentric coordinate functions, so
$\lambda_i(a_j)=\delta_{ij}$ and $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$. The local
Crouzeix–Raviart polynomial space is $\mathbb P_1(K)$, the real affine
functions on $K$. Its face-average functionals are
$$\sigma_{K,F_i}(p):=\frac1{|F_i|}\int_{F_i}p\,dS,\qquad p\in\mathbb P_1(K).$$
The candidate dual shape polynomial associated with $F_i$ is
$$\phi_{K,F_i}:=1-d\lambda_i.$$
The next item proves that these $d+1$ functionals are unisolvent and that the
displayed polynomials form their dual basis. No pointwise continuity across
different cells is part of this local element.

Crouzeix–Raviart polynomial space is $\mathbb P_1(K)$, the real affine
functions on $K$. Its face-average functionals are
$$\sigma_{K,F_i}(p):=\frac1{|F_i|}\int_{F_i}p\,dS,\qquad p\in\mathbb P_1(K).$$
The candidate dual shape polynomial associated with $F_i$ is
$$\phi_{K,F_i}:=1-d\lambda_i.$$
The next item proves that these $d+1$ functionals are unisolvent and that the
displayed polynomials form their dual basis. No pointwise continuity across

derivations.claim: Let $b_j$ be the barycenter of $F_j$. By [F2], the face average of an affine polynomial $p$ on $F_j$ is $p(b_j)$. At $b_j$, the barycentric coordinates of the $d$ vertices of $F_j$ are all $1/d$, while the coordinate opposite $F_j$ is zero. Therefore $\lambda_i(b_j)=0$ if $i=j$ and $\lambda_i(b_j)=1/d$ if $i\ne j$. Hence $(1-d\lambda_i)(b_j)=\delta_{ij}$, which proves the displayed duality identities.

The $d+1$ polynomials $\phi_{K,F_i}$ are linearly independent: applying $\sigma_{K,F_j}$ to $\sum_i c_i\phi_{K,F_i}=0$ gives $c_j=0$ by step 1.1. Since $\mathbb P_1(K)$ has dimension $d+1$, they form a basis. Applying the same functionals to $p-\sum_i\sigma_{K,F_i}(p)\phi_{K,F_i}$ gives zero for every face; expansion in this basis then gives zero coefficients. This proves existence and uniqueness of the stated expansion.
