Assume Countable Choice for the Sobolev notation below. Each cell $K$ is the closed simplex from [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]; in $W^{m,2}(K)$ notation, $K$ means its open interior, and its facets are the boundary faces of that interior. Write $H^m(K):=W^{m,2}(K;\mathbb R)$ for $m=1,2$. Use the mesh and jump convention of [[def-sipdg-jump-average-convention]]. Specialize [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]] to scalar real polynomials of a fixed degree $k\ge1$, so $V_h^{\rm br}=\prod_{K\in\mathcal T}\mathbb P_k(K;\mathbb R)$. On every cell $K$, let $A_K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ be a constant symmetric matrix. Assume common bounds $0<\lambda\le\Lambda<\infty$ such that
$$\lambda|\xi|^2\le \xi^TA_K\xi\le\Lambda|\xi|^2\qquad(\xi\in\mathbb R^d,\ K\in\mathcal T).$$
Write $A|_K=A_K$, let $h_F:=\operatorname{diam}(F)>0$, and fix a penalty parameter $\gamma>0$. Define $\mathcal D_h$ to consist of broken real-valued functions $v$ with $v|_K\in H^1(K)$, distributional $\operatorname{div}(A_K\nabla v|_K)\in L^2(K)$, and an $L^2(F)$ one-sided normal coefficient-flux trace $r_{K,F}(v)$ on every facet $F$ of each cell $K$. Precisely, $r_{K,F}(v)$ is the unique $L^2(F)$ function satisfying
$$\int_K A_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla\phi+\operatorname{div}(A_K\nabla v)\,\phi\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_F r_{K,F}(v)\,\gamma_F\phi\,dS\qquad(\phi\in C^\infty(\overline K)).$$
Here $\gamma_F\phi$ is the value trace from [[lem-sipdg-physical-simplex-trace-green]]; uniqueness follows by testing smooth functions supported near the relative interior of each facet, whose restrictions are dense in $L^2(F)$. If $F=K^-\cap K^+$ and $n_F$ points outward from $K^-$, set $q_F(v):=\tfrac12(r_{K^-,F}(v)-r_{K^+,F}(v))$; on a boundary facet set $q_F(v):=r_{K,F}(v)$ with the outward normal. These definitions agree with $\{A\nabla_hv\}_F\cdot n_F$ whenever the classical one-sided vector flux traces exist. Broken polynomials and cellwise $H^2$ functions belong to $\mathcal D_h$ by [[lem-sipdg-physical-simplex-trace-green]]. For $v,w\in\mathcal D_h$, define
$$a_h(v,w):=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K A_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}\int_F q_F(v)[w]_F\,dS-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}\int_F q_F(w)[v]_F\,dS+\gamma\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}h_F^{-1}\int_F[v]_F[w]_F\,dS,$$
All facet integrals and $L^2(F)$ norms use $(d-1)$-dimensional surface measure for the stated mesh dimension $d\ge2$. Counting measure is reserved for the separate one-dimensional interval examples in [[def-sipdg-jump-average-convention]]. The expression is real and symmetric.

Define the energy expression and its augmented version on $\mathcal D_h$ by
$$\|v\|_{DG}^2:=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K A_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla v\,dx+\gamma\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}h_F^{-1}\|[v]_F\|_{L^2(F)}^2,$$
$$\|v\|_{DG,*}^2:=\|v\|_{DG}^2+\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}h_F\|q_F(v)\|_{L^2(F)}^2.$$
The first expression is initially a seminorm on $V_h^{\rm br}$; its definiteness is not part of this definition. The stated Sobolev notation follows [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. Cellwise $H^2$ functions have the required value and normal coefficient-flux traces by [[lem-sipdg-physical-simplex-trace-green]], because $A_K$ is constant. The augmented expression is defined whenever $v\in\mathcal D_h$, so it applies in particular to the exact functions, dual functions and discrete polynomials used below.

For $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ define the discrete load $\ell_h(w):=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K f w\,dx$. A symmetric interior-penalty DG solution is a function $u_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$ satisfying $a_h(u_h,w_h)=\ell_h(w_h)$ for every $w_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\widehat S_d$ be the reference simplex, and let $F_K(\widehat x)=b+B\widehat x$ map $\overline{\widehat S_d}$ affinely onto a nondegenerate closed simplex $K$, with $\det B>0$. Sobolev spaces on $K$ mean spaces on its open interior. For every scalar $u\in W^{1,2}(K)$ and vector field $G\in W^{1,2}(K;\mathbb R^d)$, each physical facet has bounded $L^2$ traces $\gamma_Fu$ and $\gamma_FG$, obtained by affine transfer from the reference trace maps. These traces are independent of the chosen orientation-preserving reference map, and they satisfy
$$\int_K u\,\operatorname{div}G+\nabla u\cdot G\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_F(\gamma_Fu)(\gamma_FG)\cdot n_{K,F}\,dS,$$
where $n_{K,F}$ is the outward unit normal.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

For the zero multi-index, set $D^0u=u$. Since $\mathcal A_0=\{0\}$,
$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$
The formula is finite because each derivative class belongs to $L^p$ and
$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

For open $U\subseteq\Omega$ with $\overline U$ compact and contained in
$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

On each cell $K$, take $v=w_h|_K$ and $G=A_K

abla u\cdot
abla w_h=\int_Kfw_h+\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_F(A_K
abla u\cdot n_{K,F})w_h|_K$.

abla z$, which belongs to $W^{1,2}$ by [F4]. Symmetry of $A_K$ and the dual equation give $\int_KA_K
abla e\cdot

Assume Countable Choice for the Sobolev notation below. Each cell $K$ is the closed simplex from [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]; in $W^{m,2}(K)$ notation, $K$ means its open interior, and its facets are the boundary faces of that interior. Write $H^m(K):=W^{m,2}(K;\mathbb R)$ for $m=1,2$. Use the mesh and jump convention of [[def-sipdg-jump-average-convention]]. Specialize [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]] to scalar real polynomials of a fixed degree $k\ge1$, so $V_h^{\rm br}=\prod_{K\in\mathcal T}\mathbb P_k(K;\mathbb R)$. On every cell $K$, let $A_K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ be a constant symmetric matrix. Assume common bounds $0<\lambda\le\Lambda<\infty$ such that
$$\lambda|\xi|^2\le \xi^TA_K\xi\le\Lambda|\xi|^2\qquad(\xi\in\mathbb R^d,\ K\in\mathcal T).$$
Write $A|_K=A_K$, let $h_F:=\operatorname{diam}(F)>0$, and fix a penalty parameter $\gamma>0$. Define $\mathcal D_h$ to consist of broken real-valued functions $v$ with $v|_K\in H^1(K)$, distributional $\operatorname{div}(A_K\nabla v|_K)\in L^2(K)$, and an $L^2(F)$ one-sided normal coefficient-flux trace $r_{K,F}(v)$ on every facet $F$ of each cell $K$. Precisely, $r_{K,F}(v)$ is the unique $L^2(F)$ function satisfying
$$\int_K A_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla\phi+\operatorname{div}(A_K\nabla v)\,\phi\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_F r_{K,F}(v)\,\gamma_F\phi\,dS\qquad(\phi\in C^\infty(\overline K)).$$
Here $\gamma_F\phi$ is the value trace from [[lem-sipdg-physical-simplex-trace-green]]; uniqueness follows by testing smooth functions supported near the relative interior of each facet, whose restrictions are dense in $L^2(F)$. If $F=K^-\cap K^+$ and $n_F$ points outward from $K^-$, set $q_F(v):=\tfrac12(r_{K^-,F}(v)-r_{K^+,F}(v))$; on a boundary facet set $q_F(v):=r_{K,F}(v)$ with the outward normal. These definitions agree with $\{A\nabla_hv\}_F\cdot n_F$ whenever the classical one-sided vector flux traces exist. Broken polynomials and cellwise $H^2$ functions belong to $\mathcal D_h$ by [[lem-sipdg-physical-simplex-trace-green]]. For $v,w\in\mathcal D_h$, define
$$a_h(v,w):=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K A_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}\int_F q_F(v)[w]_F\,dS-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}\int_F q_F(w)[v]_F\,dS+\gamma\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}h_F^{-1}\int_F[v]_F[w]_F\,dS,$$
All facet integrals and $L^2(F)$ norms use $(d-1)$-dimensional surface measure for the stated mesh dimension $d\ge2$. Counting measure is reserved for the separate one-dimensional interval examples in [[def-sipdg-jump-average-convention]]. The expression is real and symmetric.

Define the energy expression and its augmented version on $\mathcal D_h$ by
$$\|v\|_{DG}^2:=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K A_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla v\,dx+\gamma\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}h_F^{-1}\|[v]_F\|_{L^2(F)}^2,$$
$$\|v\|_{DG,*}^2:=\|v\|_{DG}^2+\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}h_F\|q_F(v)\|_{L^2(F)}^2.$$
The first expression is initially a seminorm on $V_h^{\rm br}$; its definiteness is not part of this definition. The stated Sobolev notation follows [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. Cellwise $H^2$ functions have the required value and normal coefficient-flux traces by [[lem-sipdg-physical-simplex-trace-green]], because $A_K$ is constant. The augmented expression is defined whenever $v\in\mathcal D_h$, so it applies in particular to the exact functions, dual functions and discrete polynomials used below.

For $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ define the discrete load $\ell_h(w):=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K f w\,dx$. A symmetric interior-penalty DG solution is a function $u_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$ satisfying $a_h(u_h,w_h)=\ell_h(w_h)$ for every $w_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal T$, $A_K$, $k$, $\lambda$, $\Lambda$, $h_F$, and $q_F$ be as in [[def-sipdg-bilinear-form-and-energy-norm]]. There is a constant $C_{\rm flux}<\infty$, depending only on $d$, $k$, $\sigma$, $\lambda$, and $\Lambda$, such that every $v_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$ satisfies
$$\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}h_F\|q_F(v_h)\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le C_{\rm flux}\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K A_K\nabla v_h\cdot\nabla v_h\,dx.$$
The constant is uniform over the mesh family and does not depend on its cell sizes. In particular, the penalty threshold derived from this estimate is mesh-degree and shape dependent; it is not a universal numerical constant.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\|\cdot\|_{DG}$ be the energy expression from [[def-sipdg-bilinear-form-and-energy-norm]] on a finite matching simplicial mesh of a nonempty bounded polyhedral domain, with $\lambda>0$ and $\gamma>0$. Then $\|\cdot\|_{DG}$ is a norm on $V_h^{\rm br}$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be
conjugate exponents, and let $f,g$ be measurable real-valued functions.

1. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $q<\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^q(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q.$$
2. If $p=1$ and $q=\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$ and
   $g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_1\|g\|_\infty.$$
3. If $p=\infty$ and $q=1$ with $f\in L^\infty(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_1.$$

In every case the right-hand side is finite, so $fg$ is integrable.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$, with the Euclidean
inner product and the Euclidean norm as in [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Then:

1. **Cauchy-Schwarz.**
   $$\lvert\langle x,y\rangle\rvert \;\le\; \lVert x\rVert_2\,\lVert y\rVert_2 ,$$
   with equality if and only if there is a pair $(\lambda,\mu) \ne (0,0)$ of
   reals with $\lambda x_k = \mu y_k$ for every $k < n$.
2. **$\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ is a norm on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$**
   ([[def-norm-and-normed-space]]), for **every** $n \in \mathbb{N}$; the metric
   it induces is $d_2$ of [[lem-metrics-on-rn]] whenever $n \ge 1$.
3. **Parallelogram law.**
   $$\lVert x+y\rVert_2^{2} + \lVert x-y\rVert_2^{2} \;=\; 2\lVert x\rVert_2^{2} + 2\lVert y\rVert_2^{2} .$$
4. **Polarisation.**
   $$\langle x,y\rangle \;=\; \tfrac14\Bigl(\lVert x+y\rVert_2^{2} - \lVert x-y\rVert_2^{2}\Bigr),$$
   so the inner product is recovered from the norm it induces.

**Clause 1 is a citation, not a new proof.** The inequality and its equality case
are the published [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite]], stated there for two lists of
reals; all that happens below is that it is read in the vector notation of
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Re-proving it here would put two proofs of one
statement in the library.

derivations.claim: Put $X^2:=\sum_K\int_KA_K\nabla v_h\cdot\nabla v_h$ and $J^2:=\sum_Fh_F^{-1}\|[v_h]_F\|_{L^2(F)}^2$. The integral Cauchy–Schwarz inequality [F5] on each facet, followed by [F6] on the finite weighted face sum and [F2] give $|\sum_F\int_Fq_F(v_h)[v_h]_F|\le (\sum_Fh_F\|q_F(v_h)\|_F^2)^{1/2}J\le\sqrt{C_{\rm flux}}XJ$.

By [F1], $a_h(v_h,v_h)=X^2-2\sum_F\int_Fq_F(v_h)[v_h]_F+\gamma J^2$. Young's inequality gives $2\sqrt{C_{\rm flux}}XJ\le\tfrac12X^2+2C_{\rm flux}J^2$, hence $a_h(v_h,v_h)\ge\tfrac12X^2+(\gamma-2C_{\rm flux})J^2\ge\tfrac12(X^2+\gamma J^2)=\tfrac12\|v_h\|_{DG}^2$.

The coefficient matrix of $a_h$ in any basis of the finite-dimensional space $V_h^{\rm br}$ is symmetric by [F1]. If its matrix kernel contained a nonzero vector, the corresponding $v_h\ne0$ would satisfy $a_h(v_h,v_h)=0$, contradicting [F3] and step 2.1. Therefore the square matrix is injective, hence invertible in finite dimension, so every load has exactly one solution.

$$|a_h(v,w)|\le C_B\|v\|_{DG,*}\|w\|_{DG,*},\qquad C_B:=2+2\gamma^{-1/2}.$$
The energy expression $\|\cdot\|_{DG}$ is also a seminorm on $\mathcal D_h$.

Assume Countable Choice and the mesh and coefficient hypotheses of [[def-sipdg-bilinear-form-and-energy-norm]]. Let $e|_K\in H^2(K)$ on every cell, and let $z|_K\in H^2(K)$ be a dual solution with matching interior traces, zero boundary trace, matching normal coefficient fluxes, and $-\nabla\cdot(A_K\nabla z)=e$ on every cell. Then the SIPDG form, extended to these piecewise regular functions by its same formula, satisfies
$$a_h(e,z)=\|e\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2.$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

$$\int_K u\,\operatorname{div}G+\nabla u\cdot G\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_F(\gamma_Fu)(\gamma_FG)\cdot n_{K,F}\,dS,$$
where $n_{K,F}$ is the outward unit normal.

derivations.claim: The result is immediate if $\|e\|_{L^2}=0$. Otherwise choose $z_h$ from the stated approximation hypothesis. For $s=1$, [F3] gives $a_h(e,z_e)=\|e\|_{L^2}^2$ under the stated piecewise-$H^2$ and trace-matching hypotheses; for $s<1$ this identity is [A1]. Exact consistency plus the discrete equation give $a_h(e,z_h)=0$ by [F1]. Hence $\|e\|_{L^2}^2=a_h(e,z_e-z_h)$.

By [F7], $u$ is cellwise $H^2$ and $u_h,z_h$ are broken polynomials, so $e=u-u_h$ and $z_h$ belong to $\mathcal D_h$. For each cell $K$, a test in $C_c^\infty(K)$ extended by zero belongs to $V$ by [F5]; the weak dual equation then gives $\operatorname{div}(A_K\nabla z_e)|_K=-e|_K\in L^2(K)$ in distributions. Item 1 supplies the one-sided $L^2$ normal flux traces, and $z_e\in V$ supplies its cellwise $H^1$ restrictions and value traces by [F6]. Thus $z_e\in\mathcal D_h$ and [F2] gives $|a_h(e,z_e-z_h)|\le C_B\|e\|_{DG,*}\|z_e-z_h\|_{DG,*}$ with $C_B=2+2\gamma^{-1/2}$.

Apply step 1.2 to step 1.1 and then use the dual approximation and regularity assumptions. This gives $\|e\|_{L^2}^2\le C_BC_{\rm app}C_{\rm reg}h^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}\|e\|_{DG,*}\|e\|_{L^2}$. Divide by the positive $\|e\|_{L^2}$ to obtain the asserted estimate.

If $F=K^-\cap K^+$ and $n_F$ points outward from $K^-$, set $q_F(v):=\tfrac12(r_{K^-,F}(v)-r_{K^+,F}(v))$; on a boundary facet set $q_F(v):=r_{K,F}(v)$ with the outward normal. These definitions agree with $\{A\nabla_hv\}_F\cdot n_F$ whenever the classical one-sided vector flux traces exist. Broken polynomials and cellwise $H^2$ functions belong to $\mathcal D_h$ by [[lem-sipdg-physical-simplex-trace-green]]. For $v,w\in\mathcal D_h$, define
$$a_h(v,w):=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K A_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\,dx-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}\int_F q_F(v)[w]_F\,dS-\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}\int_F q_F(w)[v]_F\,dS+\gamma\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}h_F^{-1}\int_F[v]_F[w]_F\,dS,$$
All facet integrals and $L^2(F)$ norms use $(d-1)$-dimensional surface measure for the stated mesh dimension $d\ge2$. Counting measure is reserved for the separate one-dimensional interval examples in [[def-sipdg-jump-average-convention]]. The expression is real and symmetric.

Define the energy expression and its augmented version on $\mathcal D_h$ by
$$\|v\|_{DG}^2:=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K A_K\nabla v\cdot\nabla v\,dx+\gamma\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}h_F^{-1}\|[v]_F\|_{L^2(F)}^2,$$
$$\|v\|_{DG,*}^2:=\|v\|_{DG}^2+\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}h_F\|q_F(v)\|_{L^2(F)}^2.$$
The first expression is initially a seminorm on $V_h^{\rm br}$; its definiteness is not part of this definition. The stated Sobolev notation follows [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. Cellwise $H^2$ functions have the required value and normal coefficient-flux traces by [[lem-sipdg-physical-simplex-trace-green]], because $A_K$ is constant. The augmented expression is defined whenever $v\in\mathcal D_h$, so it applies in particular to the exact functions, dual functions and discrete polynomials used below.

For $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ define the discrete load $\ell_h(w):=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K f w\,dx$. A symmetric interior-penalty DG solution is a function $u_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$ satisfying $a_h(u_h,w_h)=\ell_h(w_h)$ for every $w_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$.

Assume Countable Choice. Use the mesh, coefficient field, energy norm, and form of [[def-sipdg-bilinear-form-and-energy-norm]], and let $C_{\rm flux}$ be the constant of [[lem-sipdg-discrete-flux-inverse-bound]]. If $\gamma\ge4C_{\rm flux}$, then
$$a_h(v_h,v_h)\ge\tfrac12\|v_h\|_{DG}^2\qquad(v_h\in V_h^{\rm br}).$$
Thus the discrete bilinear form is coercive with constant $1/2$ in the broken energy norm. For every $f\in L^2(\Omega)$, the finite-dimensional SIPDG system has a unique solution. The sufficient threshold depends on the polynomial degree, shape regularity, and coefficient ellipticity bounds; no universal penalty value is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal T$, $A_K$, $k$, $\lambda$, $\Lambda$, $h_F$, and $q_F$ be as in [[def-sipdg-bilinear-form-and-energy-norm]]. There is a constant $C_{\rm flux}<\infty$, depending only on $d$, $k$, $\sigma$, $\lambda$, and $\Lambda$, such that every $v_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$ satisfies
$$\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h}h_F\|q_F(v_h)\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le C_{\rm flux}\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K A_K\nabla v_h\cdot\nabla v_h\,dx.$$
The constant is uniform over the mesh family and does not depend on its cell sizes. In particular, the penalty threshold derived from this estimate is mesh-degree and shape dependent; it is not a universal numerical constant.

Assume Countable Choice and the SIPDG setting of [[def-sipdg-bilinear-form-and-energy-norm]], with $\gamma>0$. For all $v,w\in\mathcal D_h$,
$$|a_h(v,w)|\le C_B\|v\|_{DG,*}\|w\|_{DG,*},\qquad C_B:=2+2\gamma^{-1/2}.$$
The energy expression $\|\cdot\|_{DG}$ is also a seminorm on $\mathcal D_h$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: The exact solution $u$ is cellwise $H^2$ and $u_h,w_h$ are broken polynomials, so $u-w_h$ and $u_h-w_h$ belong to $\mathcal D_h$. The boundedness constant for their form pairing is $C_B=2+2\gamma^{-1/2}$ by [F5].

Fix $w_h$ and set $z_h=u_h-w_h$. If $\|z_h\|_{DG}=0$, then $\|z_h\|_{DG}\le2C_B\sqrt{1+C_{\rm flux}}\|u-w_h\|_{DG,*}$ is immediate. Otherwise, coercivity [F2], the discrete equation and exact consistency [F3] give $\tfrac12\|z_h\|_{DG}^2\le a_h(z_h,z_h)=a_h(u-w_h,z_h)$. By [F4] and $\sum_K\int_K\nabla z_h^TA_K\nabla z_h\le\|z_h\|_{DG}^2$, $\|z_h\|_{DG,*}\le\sqrt{1+C_{\rm flux}}\|z_h\|_{DG}$. Apply [F5] and step 1.1 to obtain $\tfrac12\|z_h\|_{DG}^2\le C_B\sqrt{1+C_{\rm flux}}\|u-w_h\|_{DG,*}\|z_h\|_{DG}$. Dividing by $\|z_h\|_{DG}>0$ proves $\|z_h\|_{DG}\le2C_B\sqrt{1+C_{\rm flux}}\|u-w_h\|_{DG,*}$.

Since $\|\cdot\|_{DG}$ is a seminorm on $\mathcal D_h$ by [F5], its triangle inequality and step 2.1 give $\|u-u_h\|_{DG}\le\|u-w_h\|_{DG}+\|w_h-u_h\|_{DG}\le(1+2C_B\sqrt{1+C_{\rm flux}})\|u-w_h\|_{DG,*}$. This holds for every $w_h$, so taking the infimum proves both assertions.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

For the zero multi-index, set $D^0u=u$. Since $\mathcal A_0=\{0\}$,
$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$
The formula is finite because each derivative class belongs to $L^p$ and
$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

For open $U\subseteq\Omega$ with $\overline U$ compact and contained in
$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be
conjugate exponents, and let $f,g$ be measurable real-valued functions.

1. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $q<\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^q(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q.$$
2. If $p=1$ and $q=\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$ and
   $g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_1\|g\|_\infty.$$
3. If $p=\infty$ and $q=1$ with $f\in L^\infty(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_1.$$

In every case the right-hand side is finite, so $fg$ is integrable.

Then $\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C(p)\,(b-a)\,\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$ for every $u\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, let $a$ be a bounded coercive sesquilinear form on $H$ with constants $M,\alpha$ ([[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]]), and let $F:H\to\mathbb K$ be a bounded conjugate-linear functional with norm $\|F\|=\sup_{\|v\|\le1}|F(v)|$. Then there is a unique $u\in H$ with $$a(u,v)=F(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in H,$$ and it satisfies $\alpha\|u\|\le\|F\|$, that is $\|u\|\le\|F\|/\alpha$. The real bilinear case is the same statement with $a$ symmetric or not, $F$ a bounded linear functional, and the conjugation read as the identity.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. On $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]]) define $$(u,v)_{H^1}:=(u,v)_{L^2}+\sum_{i=1}^n(D_iu,D_iv)_{L^2},$$ with the $L^2$ inner product of [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. Then $(\cdot,\cdot)_{H^1}$ is an inner product on the Sobolev classes whose induced norm is the $W^{1,2}$ norm of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], and $H^1(\Omega)$ is a Hilbert space for it. The zero-boundary space $H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a closed subspace of $H^1(\Omega)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]) and hence a Hilbert space for the restricted inner product. The pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, in the convention of [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]].

A **real Hilbert space** is a real inner-product space $H$ ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]) whose induced-length metric is complete in the sense of [[def-complete-metric-space]]: every Cauchy sequence in $H$ for the norm $\|v\|=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$ ([[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]) converges to a point of $H$. A **complex Hilbert space** is a complex inner-product space with the same completeness property, so that a Hilbert space is exactly a real or complex inner-product space that is a Banach space for its induced norm ([[def-banach-space]]).

**The completion convention is the Cauchy-sequence one.**
[[def-banach-space]] defines completeness by convergence of Cauchy sequences, and this page keeps that convention throughout. It is weaker than $\sigma$-completeness — the assertion that every decreasing sequence of nonempty closed subsets with diameters tending to zero has a nonempty intersection. The two agree in ZFC, but Blackadar, Farah and Karagila note that the closest-point theorem on a $\sigma$-complete inner-product space is provable in ZF, whereas the Cauchy-complete form used below consumes the Axiom of Countable Choice; nothing here silently imports the stronger notion.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. For every $1\le p<\infty$ there is
$C_{d,p}<\infty$ such that for all
$u\in W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)$,
$$\|u-u_{\widehat S_d}\|_{L^p(\widehat S_d)} \le C_{d,p}|u|_{W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d)},\qquad u_{\widehat S_d}:=|\widehat S_d|^{-1}\int_{\widehat S_d}u\,dx.$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $1<p<\infty$ and $p'=p/(p-1)$. For each facet $F$ of
$\widehat S_d$, restriction of smooth functions extends uniquely to a
bounded linear trace map
$$\gamma_F:W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)\to L^p(F;\mathbb R).$$
For real-valued $u\in W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d)$ and
$G\in W^{1,p'}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R^d)$, the facet traces satisfy
$$\int_{\widehat S_d}u\,\operatorname{div}G+\nabla u\cdot G\,dx =\sum_{F\subset\partial\widehat S_d}\int_F\gamma_Fu\,\gamma_FG\cdot\widehat n_F\,dS.$$
Here $\gamma_FG$ is the componentwise trace and $\widehat n_F$ is the
outward unit normal. The bounded C1-domain trace and Green theorems are not
used for the simplex.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants

regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to

derivations.claim:
Scaling [F1] to each triangle $K$ gives $\|v-v_K\|_{L^2(K)}\le C h_K\|
abla v\|_{L^2(K)}$ and $\|v-v_K\|_{L^2(E)}\le C h_K^{1/2}\|
abla v\|_{L^2(K)}$ for every edge $E\subset\partial K$. Shape regularity makes $h_E$ comparable to $h_K$. If $K,L$ share $E$, their traces of $v$ agree, so $|v_K-v_L|\,|E|^{1/2}\le\|v-v_K\|_{L^2(E)}+\|v-v_L\|_{L^2(E)}\le C h_z^{1/2} ig(\|
abla v\|_{L^2(K)}+\|
abla v\|_{L^2(L)} ig).$ Using $|E|^{1/2}\ge c h_z^{1/2}$ for cells in one shape-regular vertex star bounds the difference of neighboring means by the two gradient norms.

The star has at most $N_\Gamma$ cells, and its dual edge graph is connected. Join each cell to a fixed cell by a graph path of length at most $N_\Gamma-1$ and apply step 1.1 along that path. The cell Poincaré bound from step 1.1 then gives $\|v-v_K\|_{L^2(\omega_z)}\le C h_z\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\omega_z)}$. Since $|v_{\omega_z}-v_K|\le|\omega_z|^{-1/2}\|v-v_K\|_{L^2(\omega_z)}$, replacing $v_K$ by the patch mean proves the interior estimate.

For a boundary vertex patch choose one boundary edge $E_0\subset\partial\omega_z$. By the definition of $H_0^1$ as the $H^1$-closure of compactly supported smooth functions, and the continuous local trace bound in [F1], the trace of $v$ is zero on $E_0$. The trace inequality in step 1.1 therefore gives $|v_K|\,|E_0|^{1/2}=\|v-v_K\|_{L^2(E_0)}\le C h_z^{1/2}\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(K)}$ for the incident cell $K$. The same bounded-path comparison of cell means from step 2.1 controls every cell mean in the star by $C\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\omega_z)}$. Summing the cell Poincaré bounds proves the boundary estimate.

For a cell patch $\omega_K$, the three vertex stars are edge-connected because they all contain $K$, and the number of cells is at most three times the valence bound from [F2]. Along each edge-adjacency path, neighboring cell diameters are comparable by shape regularity, so all diameters in the patch are comparable to $h_K$. The mean-zero estimate follows by applying the cell-mean comparison of step 2.1 over this connected finite graph. If $K$ meets the boundary, $\omega_K$ contains a boundary edge; apply the zero-trace argument of step 3.1 there and the same path comparison to all cells in the union. These two estimates are the asserted cell-patch inequalities.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $V$ be a vector space over $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let
$V_h\subseteq V$ be a subspace, let $a$ be linear in its first argument and
conjugate-linear in its second, and let $F:V\to\mathbb K$ be conjugate-linear.
If $u\in V$ and $u_h\in V_h$ satisfy
$$a(u,v)=F(v)\quad(v\in V),\qquad a(u_h,v_h)=F(v_h)\quad(v_h\in V_h),$$
then
$$a(u-u_h,v_h)=0\qquad\text{for every }v_h\in V_h.$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

For the zero multi-index, set $D^0u=u$. Since $\mathcal A_0=\{0\}$,
$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$
The formula is finite because each derivative class belongs to $L^p$ and
$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

For open $U\subseteq\Omega$ with $\overline U$ compact and contained in
$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

A compatible labeled initial mesh is a finite matching affine simplicial triangulation $\mathcal T_0$ of a polygon in $\mathbb R^2$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], equipped with labels on its edges such that each triangle has one edge labeled $0$ and two labeled $1$, and every shared edge has the same label from both incident triangles. Matching means that distinct cell interiors are disjoint and any nonempty cell intersection is a whole common face: in two dimensions it may be a vertex or an edge. For a descendant triangle of generation $g(K)$, its three edge labels, in any order, are $(g(K)+1,g(K)+1,g(K))$. The unique edge labeled $g(K)$ is its reference edge.

To bisect $K$, join the midpoint of its reference edge to the opposite vertex. The two resulting triangles have generation $g(K)+1$. In each child, the two new half-edges and the bisector receive label $g(K)+2$; the one inherited nonreference edge retains label $g(K)+1$ and is the child's reference edge. A finite bisection forest is the collection of the initial triangles and all descendants reached by finitely many such bisections; its leaves form a triangulation when all shared-edge subdivisions agree. The admissible family $\mathbb T(\mathcal T_0)$ consists of the matching conforming leaf triangulations generated by these compatible bisections. A refinement $\mathcal T\le\mathcal T_*$ means every cell of $\mathcal T_*$ lies in a cell of $\mathcal T$.

For deterministic operational ordering, fix a finite starting mesh in this family and a total order of its cells. Enumerate those operational roots as $K_1,\ldots,K_N$ in that order; this starting mesh may already be a geometric descendant of $\mathcal T_0$, and operational numbering does not reset its generations or edge labels. Give root $K_r$ identifier $(r,\varnothing)$ and order its three vertices lexicographically by their two real coordinates. If a parent has identifier $(r,w)$, with $w$ a finite binary word, let $A$ be the earlier endpoint of its labeled reference edge in its stored vertex list, let $B$ be the other endpoint, let $C$ be the opposite vertex, and let $M=(A+B)/2$. Its children with vertex sets $\{A,M,C\}$ and $\{B,M,C\}$ receive identifiers $(r,w0)$ and $(r,w1)$, respectively. Each child's stored vertex list is the parent list restricted to its two retained vertices, in their previous order, followed by $M$. These lists are bookkeeping orders, independent of the orientation convention for affine reference maps. Compare identifiers first by root rank, then lexicographically by binary word, with $0<1$ and a proper prefix before its extensions. This is a total order, so every finite nonempty pending set has a unique least identifier. Distinct roots or distinct binary paths have distinct identifiers, and a retained cell keeps its identifier and vertex list through all subsequent calls. This operational decoration changes no geometric bisection, reference edge, admissible triangulation or finite-element space.

The compatible initial labeling is a hypothesis, not a consequence of an arbitrary initial triangulation. This definition is two-dimensional and makes no claim about three-dimensional closure or complexity.

derivations.claim: Write the parent vertices as $A,B,C$, with reference edge $AB$, midpoint $M$, and squared side lengths $X=|AC|^2$, $Y=|BC|^2$, $Z=|AB|^2$. The two first children have edge-length squares $\{X,Z/4,W\}$ and $\{Y,Z/4,W\}$, where $W=|(A+B)/2-C|^2=(2X+2Y-Z)/4$ by expanding the squared norm. The four labeled types have squared edge lists $\{X,Y,Z\}$, $\{Z/4,X,W\}$, $\{Z/4,Y,W\}$, and $\{X/4,Y/4,W\}$. In type 1 the reference side has square $X$, and the new median square is $(2(Z/4)+2W-X)/4=Y/4$; its children therefore have side lists $\{X/4,Z/4,Y/4\}$ and $\{X/4,W,Y/4\}$, which are a quarter-scale type 0 and type 3. The type 2 calculation interchanges $X,Y$. In type 3 the reference side has square $W$, and its median square is $(2(X/4)+2(Y/4)-W)/4=Z/16$; its children are quarter-scale types 1 and 2. Type 0 gives types 1 and 2 by the first bisection. Hence this finite list is closed under every labeled bisection and no other normalized shape occurs.

Each of the finitely many normalized triangles in step 1.1 is nondegenerate: its area is half the parent area at each bisection and its side lengths are the explicit midpoint lengths, so its three angles are positive. The minimum of these finitely many angles and the initial minimum angle is positive. Hence all descendants have a common positive minimum angle and a common shape-regularity bound. The angle minimum over this finite list is positive; the maximum shape-regularity constant over it and the initial cells is therefore finite.

After the first generation the midpoint $M$ of $AB$ is present. The second generation bisects $AC$ and $BC$, adding their midpoints $N$ and $P$. The four second-generation triangles have reference edges on the segments $AM, BM, CM$; the third generation bisects those segments, in particular $CM$, adding its midpoint $S$ in the interior of $ABC$. The eight leaves have vertex triples $(A,N,Q),(Q,M,N),(N,M,S),(N,S,C),(P,M,R),(P,R,B),(P,C,S),(P,S,M)$, where $Q=(A+M)/2$ and $R=(B+M)/2$. Subtracting these vertex coordinates shows that each leaf side is an original side divided by $2$, the median $|C-M|$ divided by $2$, or the reference side divided by $4$. Since $M$ lies on $AB$, convexity of the norm gives $|C-M|\le\max\{|C-A|,|C-B|\}\le\operatorname{diam}(ABC)$. Thus every leaf side, and hence every leaf diameter, is at most half the parent diameter.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $1<p<\infty$ and $p'=p/(p-1)$. For each facet $F$ of
$\widehat S_d$, restriction of smooth functions extends uniquely to a
bounded linear trace map
$$\gamma_F:W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)\to L^p(F;\mathbb R).$$
For real-valued $u\in W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d)$ and
$G\in W^{1,p'}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R^d)$, the facet traces satisfy
$$\int_{\widehat S_d}u\,\operatorname{div}G+\nabla u\cdot G\,dx =\sum_{F\subset\partial\widehat S_d}\int_F\gamma_Fu\,\gamma_FG\cdot\widehat n_F\,dS.$$
Here $\gamma_FG$ is the componentwise trace and $\widehat n_F$ is the
outward unit normal. The bounded C1-domain trace and Green theorems are not
used for the simplex.

Orient every top-dimensional cell of a matching simplicial mesh by the
ambient orientation of $\mathbb R^d$, and orient each facet by the induced
boundary convention of [[def-oriented-simplicial-cell-chains]]. In the sum
of the oriented boundaries of all top-dimensional cells, every interior
facet occurs twice with opposite signs; every boundary facet occurs once.

by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

For smooth compactly supported $v$, integrate $\int_K
abla U\cdot
abla v=-\int_K\Delta U\,v+\int_{\partial K}(
abla U\cdot n_K)v$ on every cell using [F1]. Since $U|_K$ is affine, $\Delta U=0$. The sum of boundary integrals on each interior edge is $\int_EJ_E(U)v$, and boundary-edge terms vanish because $v$ is compactly supported.

The weak residual is $(f,v)-\int
abla U\cdot
abla v-\int(b\cdot
abla U)v$. Substituting step 1.1 gives cell integrands $f-b\cdot
abla U=R_K(U)$ and the negative of the summed outward flux jumps. This is the displayed formula for smooth compactly supported $v$.

Every term in the identity is continuous in the $H^1$ norm: volume terms use $f,\nabla U\in L^2$, and edge terms use the trace inequality from [F1] on the finite mesh. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice for the $H_0^1$ convention of [[def-countable-choice]].

Fix a finite conforming triangular mesh $\mathcal T$. For each interior vertex $z$, choose the incident triangle with least fixed mesh index and denote it $K_z$. On the reference triangle $\widehat K$, let $\widehat\lambda_1,\widehat\lambda_2,\widehat\lambda_3$ be its barycentric coordinates. The Gram matrix $G_{ij}=\int_{\widehat K}\widehat\lambda_i\widehat\lambda_j$ is positive definite because $\int_{\widehat K}p^2>0$ for every nonzero $p\in P_1(\widehat K)$. Thus there are unique dual affine polynomials $\widehat\psi_i\in P_1(\widehat K)$ with $\int_{\widehat K}\widehat\lambda_j\widehat\psi_i=\delta_{ij}$. Pull them to $K_z$ by the affine map using the normalized measure so $\int_{K_z}\varphi_y\psi_{z,K_z}=\delta_{zy}$ for its three local nodal hats.

For $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ set $c_z(v)=\int_{K_z}v\psi_{z,K_z}$ at interior vertices and $c_z(v)=0$ at boundary vertices. Define
$$I_{\mathcal T}v=\sum_{z\ {\rm interior}}c_z(v)\varphi_z,$$
where $\varphi_z$ is the continuous piecewise-affine nodal hat. The sum is finite and belongs to the conforming zero-boundary P1 space. This is a moment quasi-interpolant; it is not a point-evaluation operator on arbitrary Sobolev classes.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$,
$\widehat S_d$ be the reference simplex, let $\widehat P$ be a finite
dimensional $\mathbb K$-space of polynomial functions on it, let
$\widehat F$ be any facet, and let integer $m\ge0$. For $1\le p,q\le\infty$ there is a finite
constant $C$ such that
$$|v|_{W^{m,p}(\widehat S_d)}+\|v\|_{L^p(\widehat F)}\le C\|v\|_{L^q(\widehat S_d)}\qquad(v\in\widehat P).$$
For every pair of integers $0\le m\le\ell$, there is also a finite
constant $C$ such that
$$|v|_{W^{\ell,p}(\widehat S_d)} \le C|v|_{W^{m,q}(\widehat S_d)}\qquad(v\in\widehat P).$$
For finitely many facets, one constant works for all of them. In particular,
every linear degree-of-freedom functional on $\widehat P$ is bounded with
respect to the $L^q(\widehat S_d)$ norm.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

Assume Countable Choice, as in the reference-simplex trace and Poincare suppliers.

Let $\mathcal T$ be a conforming shape-regular triangular mesh. For an interior vertex $z$, let $\omega_z$ be the union of its incident triangles; for a boundary vertex use the same patch. There is a constant $C$ depending only on the shape-regularity bound such that, at an interior vertex, every $v\in H^1(\omega_z)$ satisfies
$$\|v-v_{\omega_z}\|_{L^2(\omega_z)}\le C h_z\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\omega_z)},$$
where $v_{\omega_z}$ is the patch mean and $h_z=\max_{K\subset\omega_z}h_K$. On a boundary vertex patch, every $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ satisfies
$$\|v\|_{L^2(\omega_z)}\le C h_z\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\omega_z)}.$$
For a cell $K$, define $\omega_K=\bigcup_{z\in\mathcal V(K)}\omega_z$, where $\mathcal V(K)$ is its set of three vertices. If $K$ does not meet $\partial\Omega$, the corresponding mean-zero estimate holds on $\omega_K$ with scale $h_K$; if $K$ meets $\partial\Omega$ and $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$, then
$$\|v\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}\le Ch_K\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}.$$

derivations.claim: The definition gives finitely many coefficients, each an integral against a bounded affine polynomial, hence a linear functional on $L^2(K_z)$; the resulting finite sum is continuous piecewise affine. Its boundary nodal coefficients are zero, so [F2] places it in $V(\mathcal T)$. If $v\in V(\mathcal T)$, then on the selected cell $K_z$ its affine restriction is a linear combination of the three local hats. The dual moment identities recover its nodal coefficient at $z$, so $c_z(v)=v(z)$ at every interior vertex; at boundary vertices both the coefficient and the P1 trace value are zero. Therefore $I_{\mathcal T}v=v$.

For a cell $K$ not meeting the boundary, set $c=v_{\omega_K}$; for a boundary cell set $c=0$. The patch Poincaré estimate gives $\|v-c\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}\le Ch_K\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}$. For each interior vertex $z$ of $K$, put $a_z=c_z(v)-c=\int_{K_z}(v-c)\psi_{z,K_z}$; this equality follows from the dual identities, which give $\int_{K_z}\psi_{z,K_z}=1$. These are local integrals of an $L^2(K_z)$ function, with no application of $I_{\mathcal T}$ to $v-c$. The scaled dual bound gives $|a_z|\le Ch_K^{-1}\|v-c\|_{L^2(K_z)}$, since $K_z\subset\omega_K$ and its diameter is comparable to $h_K$. At a boundary vertex of $K$, necessarily $c=0$ and the corresponding coefficient difference is zero. The three barycentric hats on $K$ sum to one, so $(I_{\mathcal T}v-c)|_K=\sum_{z\in\mathcal V(K),\ z\ {\rm interior}}a_z\varphi_z|_K$. Each hat has $L^2(K)$ norm at most $Ch_K$ and gradient norm at most $C$. Thus $\|I_{\mathcal T}v-c\|_{L^2(K)}\le C\|v-c\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}$ and $\|\nabla I_{\mathcal T}v\|_{L^2(K)}\le Ch_K^{-1}\|v-c\|_{L^2(\omega_K)}$. The patch inequality and $v-I_{\mathcal T}v=(v-c)-(I_{\mathcal T}v-c)$ prove the first two bounds. This argument uses only that each selected $K_z$ is incident to $z$, so its constants are uniform over all such selections.

Apply the scaled trace inequality to $v-I_{\mathcal T}v$ on $K$. The first two bounds from step 1.2 control the cell $L^2$ term and its gradient; the neighboring patch gives the same estimates on $K'$. Since $h_E$ and $h_K$ are comparable by shape regularity, this yields the asserted edge bound.

A compatible labeled initial mesh is a finite matching affine simplicial triangulation $\mathcal T_0$ of a polygon in $\mathbb R^2$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], equipped with labels on its edges such that each triangle has one edge labeled $0$ and two labeled $1$, and every shared edge has the same label from both incident triangles. Matching means that distinct cell interiors are disjoint and any nonempty cell intersection is a whole common face: in two dimensions it may be a vertex or an edge. For a descendant triangle of generation $g(K)$, its three edge labels, in any order, are $(g(K)+1,g(K)+1,g(K))$. The unique edge labeled $g(K)$ is its reference edge.

To bisect $K$, join the midpoint of its reference edge to the opposite vertex. The two resulting triangles have generation $g(K)+1$. In each child, the two new half-edges and the bisector receive label $g(K)+2$; the one inherited nonreference edge retains label $g(K)+1$ and is the child's reference edge. A finite bisection forest is the collection of the initial triangles and all descendants reached by finitely many such bisections; its leaves form a triangulation when all shared-edge subdivisions agree. The admissible family $\mathbb T(\mathcal T_0)$ consists of the matching conforming leaf triangulations generated by these compatible bisections. A refinement $\mathcal T\le\mathcal T_*$ means every cell of $\mathcal T_*$ lies in a cell of $\mathcal T$.

For deterministic operational ordering, fix a finite starting mesh in this family and a total order of its cells. Enumerate those operational roots as $K_1,\ldots,K_N$ in that order; this starting mesh may already be a geometric descendant of $\mathcal T_0$, and operational numbering does not reset its generations or edge labels. Give root $K_r$ identifier $(r,\varnothing)$ and order its three vertices lexicographically by their two real coordinates. If a parent has identifier $(r,w)$, with $w$ a finite binary word, let $A$ be the earlier endpoint of its labeled reference edge in its stored vertex list, let $B$ be the other endpoint, let $C$ be the opposite vertex, and let $M=(A+B)/2$. Its children with vertex sets $\{A,M,C\}$ and $\{B,M,C\}$ receive identifiers $(r,w0)$ and $(r,w1)$, respectively. Each child's stored vertex list is the parent list restricted to its two retained vertices, in their previous order, followed by $M$. These lists are bookkeeping orders, independent of the orientation convention for affine reference maps. Compare identifiers first by root rank, then lexicographically by binary word, with $0<1$ and a proper prefix before its extensions. This is a total order, so every finite nonempty pending set has a unique least identifier. Distinct roots or distinct binary paths have distinct identifiers, and a retained cell keeps its identifier and vertex list through all subsequent calls. This operational decoration changes no geometric bisection, reference edge, admissible triangulation or finite-element space.

The compatible initial labeling is a hypothesis, not a consequence of an arbitrary initial triangulation. This definition is two-dimensional and makes no claim about three-dimensional closure or complexity.

For any compatible 2D initial labeling from [[def-afem-nvb-labelled-triangulation-family]], every conforming NVB descendant has shape regularity bounded by a constant depending only on the initial mesh. Three complete generations of uniform bisection of a triangle split each original edge at its midpoint, create a new interior midpoint on the median from the opposite vertex, and give child diameters at most half the parent diameter.

derivations.claim: Let $F_i$ be the finite binary forest for $\mathcal T_i$. Their node union $F=F_1\cup F_2$ is a forest: every nonroot node keeps its parent, and a node is either a leaf in both forests or has its same two children in at least one; if it has children in either forest, the union contains both. The common initial edges have equal labels. Induct on the bisection depth of any shared edge: its midpoint is uniquely determined by the segment, and its two half-edge labels are determined by the same generation rule [F1]; therefore both incident forests prescribe the same descendants on that edge. The leaves of $F$ consequently form a matching conforming triangulation refining both $\mathcal T_1$ and $\mathcal T_2$. Any common refinement must contain every node split in either forest, so it contains $F$ and refines its leaf partition. Thus this is the smallest common conforming overlay.

For each initial root, a finite full binary tree with $i$ internal nodes has $i+1$ leaves; induction on $i$ proves this because splitting one leaf increases the leaf count by one. The internal nodes of $F$ are the union of the internal nodes of $F_1,F_2$, so $\#\operatorname{Int}(F)\le\#\operatorname{Int}(F_1)+\#\operatorname{Int}(F_2).$ Summing the leaf identity over the $\#\mathcal T_0$ roots gives $\#\mathcal T_i=\#\mathcal T_0+\#\operatorname{Int}(F_i)$ and the same identity for the overlay. Substitution proves the inequality.

Input: a finite labeled conforming mesh $\mathcal T$, exact nonnegative arrays $(\eta_K^2)_{K\in\mathcal T}$ and $(o_K^2)_{K\in\mathcal T}$, where $\eta_K^2$ is the cell estimator contribution and $o_K^2$ the cell data-oscillation contribution, bulk-fraction parameters $\theta_E,\theta_O\in(0,1]$, a per-call total bisection budget $B\in\mathbb N_0$, and a stable total order of mesh identifiers. On the first call on a mesh not yet carrying operational forest identifiers, rank its cells by the supplied order and initialize the operational roots and vertex lists of [[def-afem-nvb-labelled-triangulation-family]]. This initialization preserves the supplied order on those cells and does not change their geometric generations or labels. On subsequent calls retain that forest decoration and use its identifier order. Thus each current input leaf, including every generated descendant, has a specified identifier. For an array $q_K\ge0$ and $\theta\in(0,1]$, sort by decreasing $q_K$ and then increasing identifier. If $\sum_Kq_K=0$, return the empty set. Otherwise return the shortest initial segment whose sum is at least $\theta\sum_Kq_K$. Thus these parameters are fractions of the squared contributions (the square-root convention for the usual estimator-norm parameter). Call the resulting sets $M_E,M_O$ and set $M=M_E\cup M_O$.

Before modifying the mesh, form the original edge-neighbor request set
$$Q=\{L\in\mathcal T:L=K\text{ or }L\text{ shares an edge with some }K\in M\}.$$
Thus $M_E,M_O$ and their union $M$ remain the bulk marks; $Q$ is the larger refinement request, with $M\subseteq Q$ and $\#Q\le4\#M$ because a triangle has at most three edge neighbors. A compatible labeled initial mesh is a finite matching affine simplicial triangulation $\mathcal T_0$ of a polygon in $\mathbb R^2$ as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], equipped with labels on its edges such that each triangle has one edge labeled $0$ and two labeled $1$, and every shared edge has the same label from both incident triangles. Matching means that distinct cell interiors are disjoint and any nonempty cell intersection is a whole common face: in two dimensions it may be a vertex or an edge. For a descendant triangle of generation $g(K)$, its three edge labels, in any order, are $(g(K)+1,g(K)+1,g(K))$. The unique edge labeled $g(K)$ is its reference edge.

To bisect $K$, join the midpoint of its reference edge to the opposite vertex. The two resulting triangles have generation $g(K)+1$. In each child, the two new half-edges and the bisector receive label $g(K)+2$; the one inherited nonreference edge retains label $g(K)+1$ and is the child's reference edge. A finite bisection forest is the collection of the initial triangles and all descendants reached by finitely many such bisections; its leaves form a triangulation when all shared-edge subdivisions agree. The admissible family $\mathbb T(\mathcal T_0)$ consists of the matching conforming leaf triangulations generated by these compatible bisections. A refinement $\mathcal T\le\mathcal T_*$ means every cell of $\mathcal T_*$ lies in a cell of $\mathcal T$.

For deterministic operational ordering, fix a finite starting mesh in this family and a total order of its cells. Enumerate those operational roots as $K_1,\ldots,K_N$ in that order; this starting mesh may already be a geometric descendant of $\mathcal T_0$, and operational numbering does not reset its generations or edge labels. Give root $K_r$ identifier $(r,\varnothing)$ and order its three vertices lexicographically by their two real coordinates. If a parent has identifier $(r,w)$, with $w$ a finite binary word, let $A$ be the earlier endpoint of its labeled reference edge in its stored vertex list, let $B$ be the other endpoint, let $C$ be the opposite vertex, and let $M=(A+B)/2$. Its children with vertex sets $\{A,M,C\}$ and $\{B,M,C\}$ receive identifiers $(r,w0)$ and $(r,w1)$, respectively. Each child's stored vertex list is the parent list restricted to its two retained vertices, in their previous order, followed by $M$. These lists are bookkeeping orders, independent of the orientation convention for affine reference maps. Compare identifiers first by root rank, then lexicographically by binary word, with $0<1$ and a proper prefix before its extensions. This is a total order, so every finite nonempty pending set has a unique least identifier. Distinct roots or distinct binary paths have distinct identifiers, and a retained cell keeps its identifier and vertex list through all subsequent calls. This operational decoration changes no geometric bisection, reference edge, admissible triangulation or finite-element space.

The compatible initial labeling is a hypothesis, not a consequence of an arbitrary initial triangulation. This definition is two-dimensional and makes no claim about three-dimensional closure or complexity.

For any compatible 2D initial labeling from [[def-afem-nvb-labelled-triangulation-family]], every conforming NVB descendant has shape regularity bounded by a constant depending only on the initial mesh. Three complete generations of uniform bisection of a triangle split each original edge at its midpoint, create a new interior midpoint on the median from the opposite vertex, and give child diameters at most half the parent diameter.

derivations.claim: For a current cell $K$, follow its interior reference-edge neighbor. The common label is $g(K)$; by [F1] the neighbor either has the same generation, giving a compatibly divisible pair, or has generation $g(K)-1$. Continue in the latter case. Strict generation drops terminate at a boundary reference edge or compatible pair. Refine from that terminal end and re-inspect each earlier pending leaf, as the algorithm prescribes. A coarser neighbor may need two bisections: after its reference-edge split, the child containing the pending common edge has that inherited edge as reference and is bisected before returning to $K$. These are children or grandchildren of a chain cell $L$; for a coarser chain cell $g(L)\le g(K)-1$, so their generations are at most $g(K)+1$. The terminal partner and $K$ itself need one split. Each processed common edge is split on both sides, so the resulting mesh is conforming. The finite chain and this finite reinspection give termination for one request, and the finitely many requested descendant generations give termination of a complete call.

Let $g(K)$ denote generation. Each bisection halves area, and [F2] gives constants $c_0,C_0>0$ depending only on the finitely many initial shapes such that $c_0\,2^{-g(K)}\le |K|\le C_0\,2^{-g(K)}$ and $\operatorname{diam}K\le C_0\,2^{-g(K)/2}$. In the backward chain of step 1.1 there is at most one cell at each generation, plus at most one terminal compatible partner. Hence the sum of diameters from generation $g_{\min}$ upward is at most $D_0 2^{-g_{\min}/2}$ with $D_0=2C_0/(1-2^{-1/2})$. Every created cell is a child of $K$ or its terminal same-generation partner, or a child or grandchild of a strictly coarser chain cell. Step 1.1 therefore gives $g(T)\le g(K)+1$. For a created cell $T$ within an original chain cell $L$, the portion of the chain between $K$ and $L$ has its lowest generation $g(L)$; summing its diameters gives $\operatorname{dist}(K,T)\le D_1 2^{-g(T)/2}$ with $D_1=4D_0$. The chain is finite by the integer generation drop, and these estimates supply the geometric radius used below.

First consider one-generation requests in a finite sequence and let $\mathcal M$ be the union of all requested cells. For a final cell $T$ and marked cell $T^*$ define a nonnegative allocation $\lambda(T,T^*)=\begin{cases}a(g(T^*)-g(T)),& \operatorname{dist}(T,T^*)<D\,B\,2^{-g(T)/2}\ \text{and }g(T)\le g(T^*)+1,\\0,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}$ where $a(\ell)=(\ell+2)^{-2}$ for $\ell\ge-1$, $b(\ell)=2^{\ell/3}$ for $\ell\ge0$, $A=\sum_{\ell\ge-1}a(\ell)<\infty$, $B=\sum_{\ell\ge0}2^{-\ell/2}b(\ell)<\infty$, and $D=2D_1+2C_0$, with $D_1$ from step 2.1. The series for $B$ is geometric with ratio $2^{-1/6}<1$, and $c_*=\inf_{\ell\ge1}a(\ell)b(\ell)>0$ because $2^{\ell/3}/(\ell+2)^2$ tends to infinity.

Fix $T^*\in\mathcal M$ with generation $g^*$. At a fixed generation $g\le g^*+1$, cells with nonzero allocation lie in a ball of radius $D B2^{-g/2}$ about $T^*$. Each has area at least $c_0 2^{-g}$ by step 2.1, while that ball enlarged by one cell diameter has area at most $C_D2^{-g}$. Since cell interiors are disjoint, their number is at most a constant $N_D$ independent of $g,T^*$, and the final level. Summing weights over generations therefore gives $\sum_{T\in\mathcal T_n\setminus\mathcal T_0}\lambda(T,T^*)\le N_D\sum_{\ell\ge-1}a(\ell)=N_DA=:C_1.$

Fix a new cell $T_0$ in the final forest. Trace its unique parent backward through the finite refinement history. If the parent was created during closure, take the least-ID requested cell whose recursive chain created it; repeat this at each earlier creation time. This gives a finite sequence of requested cells $T_1,\ldots,T_J$ ending at an initial cell. Step 2.1 gives $g(T_{j+1})\ge g(T_j)-1$ and, for each consecutive pair in the sequence, $\operatorname{dist}(T_{j-1},T_j)\le D_1 2^{-g(T_{j-1})/2}$. Let $s$ be the first index with $g(T_s)=g(T_0)-1$. The prefix whose links join $T_0$ to $T_s$ is $T_0,\ldots,T_{s-1}$; each of its generations is $g(T_0)+\ell$ for some $\ell\ge0$. The triangle inequality for set distances includes the diameters of the intervening cells. Steps 2.1 and the diameter bound control the sum by $(D_1+C_0)$ times the corresponding generation sum; $D=2(D_1+C_0)$ leaves strict slack. Consequently, if this prefix has at most $b(\ell)$ cells at every generation $g(T_0)+\ell$, then $\operatorname{dist}(T_0,T_s)<D B\,2^{-g(T_0)/2}.$ Thus the terminal requested cell $T_s$ lies in the allocation radius and contributes $a(-1)>0$. Otherwise let $j_*$ be the first prefix with more than $b(\ell_*)$ cells at some generation $g(T_0)+\ell_*$. Every earlier link prefix satisfies the displayed distance bound. If $\ell_*=0$, since $T_0$ is new and $b(0)=1$, at least one other cell of that generation is a marked cell and contributes $a(0)$. If $\ell_*>0$, all cells of that generation in the prefix are marked; each lies within the allocation radius and contributes $a(\ell_*)$. In this case their total is greater than $a(\ell_*)b(\ell_*)\ge c_*$. Hence every new cell receives at least $C_2=\min\{a(-1),a(0),c_*\}>0$ allocation.

Sum the lower bound from step 3.3 over new cells and interchange the two finite sums. The upper bound from step 3.2 gives $C_2(\#\mathcal T_n-\#\mathcal T_0)\le\sum_{T^*\in\mathcal M}\sum_{T\notin\mathcal T_0}\lambda(T,T^*)\le C_1\#\mathcal M.$ For three requested generations, view each parent in $Q_k$ as successive one-generation requests. There are at most $2^{j-1}\#Q_k$ virtual requests at stage $j=1,2,3$, even if closure performs some requested splits before their scheduled turn. The total is at most $7\#Q_k$, giving $C_{\rm gen}=7C_1/C_2$. For the algorithm, every original triangle has at most three edge neighbors, so $\#Q_k\le4\#M_k$; hence $C_{\rm cl}=28C_1/C_2$ proves the displayed estimate in terms of the unchanged bulk marks. Empty marks give no requests or splits, and all bisections, including those needed for patch expansion and conformity, are counted.

Let $\mathcal T$ be a shape-regular conforming triangular mesh and let $I_{\mathcal T}$ be the moment interpolant from [[def-afem-local-moment-interpolant]]. For each cell $K$, let $\omega_K$ be the union of vertex stars of its vertices. There is a constant $C$ depending only on shape regularity such that for every $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$,
$$\|v-I_{\mathcal T}v\|_{L^2(K)}\le Ch_K\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\omega_K)},\quad \|\nabla I_{\mathcal T}v\|_{L^2(K)}\le C\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\omega_K)},$$

where $K'$ is the other incident cell. The operator maps into $V(\mathcal T)$ and reproduces every member of $V(\mathcal T)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix polynomial degree $k\ge0$, $1\le p,q\le\infty$, and integers
$0\le m\le\ell\le k$. Let the shape-regular affine simplex family be as in
[[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. For every cell $K$ in that family,
there is a constant independent of cell size such that, for every
$v\in\mathbb P_k(K)$ and every facet $F\subset\partial K$,
$$|v|_{W^{\ell,p}(K)} \le C h_K^{m-\ell+d(1/p-1/q)}|v|_{W^{m,q}(K)},$$
$$\|v\|_{L^p(F)} \le C h_K^{(d-1)/p-d/q}\|v\|_{L^q(K)}.$$

regularity bound, but not on $K$ or $h_K$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex

$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants

$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of a bounded

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded polyhedral open set with a finite matching

abla v_K\|_{L^2(K)}\le Ch_K^{-1}\| ar R_K\|_{L^2(K)}$. The residual identity has no edge term for this test, so $ ar R_K\int_K v_K=a(e,v_K)+\int_K( ar R_K-R_K(U))v_K$. The left side is at least $c\| ar R_K\|_{L^2(K)}^2$, while the two terms on the right are bounded by $C(1+|b|h_K)h_K^{-1}\|
