For $U\in\mathcal G$, let $Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_d)$ and $W=(W_1,\ldots,W_d)$ be arrays of entropy-variable gradients, with $Z_k,W_k\in\mathbb R^{d+2}$. Write $Z_{k,m_\ell}$ for the momentum-variable component and $Z_{k,E}$ for the energy-variable component. Define

$$G_{k\ell}(Z)=Z_{k,m_\ell}+u_\ell Z_{k,E},\qquad c_k(Z)=Z_{k,E},$$

and $G^0(Z)=\operatorname{sym}G(Z)-(\operatorname{tr}G(Z)/d)I$. Define the linear map

$$\mathcal R_U Z=\bigl(\sqrt{2\mu T}\,G^0(Z),\ \sqrt{\zeta T}\,\operatorname{tr}G(Z),\ \sqrt{\kappa}\,T c(Z)\bigr).$$

The bilinear form

$$\mathcal B_U(Z,W)=2\mu T\,G^0(Z):G^0(W)+\zeta T\,\operatorname{tr}G(Z)\operatorname{tr}G(W)+\kappa T^2\sum_{k=1}^d c_k(Z)c_k(W)$$

has the factorization $\mathcal B_U(Z,W)=(\mathcal R_UZ)\cdot(\mathcal R_UW)=\sum_{j,k}Z_j^TK_{jk}(U)W_k$, so $K(U)=\mathcal R_U^*\mathcal R_U$ is a symmetric positive-semidefinite block matrix. For $Z_k=\partial_kv(U)$, its blocks give exactly the model viscous flux $F_j^{\mathrm{visc}}=\sum_kK_{jk}(U)\partial_kv$, and

$$\sum_{j,k}(\partial_jv)^TK_{jk}(U)(\partial_kv)=\frac{\tau:\nabla u}{T}+\frac{\kappa|\nabla T|^2}{T^2}\ge0.$$

For the ideal-gas model in [[def-compressible-navier-stokes-fourier-model]], the mathematical entropy $\eta=-\rho s$ has positive-definite Hessian on $\mathcal G$. Its entropy variables are

$$v(U)=\nabla_U\eta(U)=\left(c_v\gamma-s-\frac{\beta|u|^2}{2},\ \beta u,\ -\beta\right),\qquad \beta=\frac{c_v\rho}{\varepsilon}=\frac1T.$$

The Euler entropy flux $q_j(U)=\eta(U)u_j$ is compatible with $F_j$, meaning $\nabla_Uq_j=(\nabla_U\eta)^TDF_j$, and its entropy potential is $\psi_j(U)=v(U)^TF_j(U)-q_j(U)=\rho R u_j$. Consequently $U\mapsto v(U)$ is a local diffeomorphism at every $U\in\mathcal G$ and $\eta$ is strictly convex on $\mathcal G$.

derivations.claim: Fix an interior face $x_f=x_{i+1/2}$ and put $U_f=U(x_f)$. Taylor's theorem at $x_f$ gives $U(x_f\pm h/2)=U_f\pm(h/2)U'(x_f)+(h^2/8)U''(x_f)+O(h^3)$, uniformly in the face index because $U'''$ is bounded. Averaging the two expansions and using [F1] yields $U_{i+1/2}=U_f+O(h^2)$.

In [F3], $u=m/\rho$, $\varepsilon=E-|m|^2/(2\rho)$, and $s=c_v\log((\gamma-1)\varepsilon/\rho^\gamma)+s_0$. These functions and $\beta$ are smooth on $\mathcal G$, where $\rho,\varepsilon>0$, so $v\circ U$ is $C^3$ on $[0,L]$ with bounded third derivative. Its centered Taylor expansion gives $(v(U(x_f+h/2))-v(U(x_f-h/2)))/h=\partial_xv(U_f)+O(h^2)$ uniformly in $i$.

The block $K_{11}(U)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$ by its explicit finite-dimensional factorization [F2], hence has bounded first derivatives on a compact neighborhood of the image of $U$. Step 1.1 gives $K_{11}(U_{i+1/2})=K_{11}(U_f)+O(h^2)$. Multiplying this by the bounded difference quotient in step 1.2 and using [F1] proves the stated $O(h^2)$ face-flux estimate.

derivations.claim: For the total conservative state, substitute [F1] and telescope the finite sum: $\frac{d}{dt}\sum_{i=1}^NhU_i=\sum_{i=1}^N(G_{i+1/2}-G_{i-1/2})=G_{N+1/2}-G_{1/2}=0$.

Since $v_i=\nabla_U\eta(U_i)$ by [F3], the chain rule gives $\frac{d}{dt}\sum_i h\eta(U_i)=\sum_i h v_i^T\dot U_i$. Substituting [F1] cancels the factors $h$ and gives $\sum_i v_i^T(G_{i+1/2}-G_{i-1/2})$.

At each interior face $i+1/2$, the two adjacent cells contribute $v_i^TG_{i+1/2}-v_{i+1}^TG_{i+1/2}=-(v_{i+1}-v_i)^TG_{i+1/2}$. The boundary terms vanish by [F1]. Substituting the face flux gives the exact negative sum in the Statement.

Each midpoint state is admissible by the convexity built into [F1], and its matrix block is positive semidefinite by [F2]. Thus every face term $(v_{i+1}-v_i)^TK_{i+1/2}(v_{i+1}-v_i)/h$ is nonnegative because $h>0$. This proves the entropy inequality, including the case $N=1$ when the face sum is empty.

Fix the periodic SBP data and semidiscrete vector field $L_h$ of [[def-periodic-sbp-compressible-viscous-scheme]]. Let $\mathcal C\subset\mathcal G$ be a specified compact set, let the initial nodal vector $U^0=(U_i^0)_{i\in\mathcal I}$ satisfy $U_i^0\in\mathcal C$ for every node, let $\Delta t>0$, and let $N\in\mathbb N\cup\{0\}$ be a finite step budget. The algorithm returns a nodal vector, a status, and an accepted-step count.

1. For $n=0,\ldots,N-1$, compute the candidate
   $$U^{n+1,*}=U^n+\Delta t\,L_h(U^n).$$

2. If $U_i^{n+1,*}\in\mathcal C$ for every node $i$, accept it by setting $U^{n+1}=U^{n+1,*}$ and continue.

3. If any candidate node lies outside $\mathcal C$, return $(U^n,\texttt{left\_positive\_tube},n)$ immediately. Here $U^n$ is the last accepted vector and $n$ is the number of accepted steps; the rejected candidate is the one-based stage $n+1$.

4. If all $N$ candidates are accepted, return $(U^N,\texttt{completed},N)$. For $N=0$, return $(U^0,\texttt{completed},0)$.

The membership test is applied nodewise to the compact positive-state tube. A returned `left_positive_tube` status records a failed candidate and makes no claim that the prescribed step budget was completed.

derivations.claim: If $N=0$, branch 4 of [F1] returns the input immediately, with zero evaluations and zero accepted stages.

Suppose $N>0$. At each visited stage $n<N$, branch 3 returns immediately if the candidate fails, so no rejected stage repeats; the algorithm reports $n$ accepted steps because $U^n$ follows exactly $n$ earlier acceptances. Otherwise branch 2 accepts one candidate, so the next stored iterate follows one more acceptance. If all $N$ candidates are accepted, branch 4 returns `completed` with count $N$. Thus the loop has at most $N$ evaluations and the accepted count lies in $[0,N]$.

The initial nodal vector is in $\mathcal C$ by the algorithm input. Each later vector becomes the stored state only after every node passes membership in $\mathcal C$; branch 3 returns the preceding stored vector. Therefore every returned nodal state lies in $\mathcal C$.

$$HD_j+D_j^TH=0,\qquad D_j\mathbf1=0.$$

$$\dot U_i+2\sum_{j=1}^d\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal I}(D_j)_{i\ell}F_j^{\mathrm{ec}}(U_i,U_\ell) =\sum_{j,k=1}^d\left[D_j\left(\bigl(K_{jk}(U_i)(D_kv)_i\bigr)_{i\in\mathcal I}\right)\right]_i, \qquad i\in\mathcal I,$$

This definition specifies a periodic semidiscrete operator on $\mathcal G^M$; it does not include a time discretization or a positivity limiter.

The flux in [[def-ideal-gas-entropy-conservative-pair-flux]] is well-defined for every pair in $\mathcal G\times\mathcal G$, symmetric in its two states, and consistent in the sense that $F_j^{\mathrm{ec}}(U,U)=F_j(U)$. It satisfies

$$(v(U_R)-v(U_L))^TF_j^{\mathrm{ec}}(U_L,U_R)=\psi_j(U_R)-\psi_j(U_L).$$

derivations.claim: The formula [F6] is smooth on $\mathcal G$: $u=m/\rho$, $\varepsilon=E-|m|^2/(2\rho)$, $s=c_v\log((\gamma-1)\varepsilon/\rho^\gamma)+s_0$, and $\beta=c_v\rho/\varepsilon$ have positive denominators and logarithm arguments there. Thus $v$ is locally Lipschitz. Together with [F2] and [F3], this makes every term in the finite sum [F1] locally Lipschitz on the open finite-dimensional domain $\mathcal G^{|\mathcal I|}$, so $L_h$ is locally Lipschitz and continuous there. Compactness of $\mathcal C^{|\mathcal I|}$ gives a bound $M_h=\sup_{Y\in\mathcal C^{|\mathcal I|}}\|L_h(Y)\|<\infty$. Cover this compact set by finitely many smaller balls whose doubled balls lie in local Lipschitz neighborhoods, and let $\delta_0>0$ be the smallest smaller-ball radius. Any pair at distance less than $\delta_0$ lies together in one of those larger balls, so its Lipschitz quotient is bounded by the largest local constant. For pairs at distance at least $\delta_0$, boundedness gives quotient at most $2M_h/\delta_0$. Thus a finite Lipschitz constant $L_h^*$ holds on $\mathcal C^{|\mathcal I|}$.

For an exact time $t_n=n\Delta t$ and $t_{n+1}\le T$, the integral equation and the bound in step 1.1 give the one-step defect $r_n=\bar U(t_{n+1})-\bar U(t_n)-\Delta tL_h(\bar U(t_n))$, with $\|r_n\|\le\frac12L_h^*M_h(\Delta t)^2$. Indeed, $r_n=\int_0^{\Delta t}(L_h(\bar U(t_n+s))-L_h(\bar U(t_n)))\,ds$, while $\|\bar U(t_n+s)-\bar U(t_n)\|\le M_hs$.

The unguarded Euler recurrence, as long as each preceding candidate has been accepted, therefore satisfies $e_{n+1}\le(1+L_h^*\Delta t)e_n+\frac12L_h^*M_h(\Delta t)^2$, where $e_n=\|U^n-\bar U(t_n)\|$ and $e_0=0$. Summing the geometric bound and using $(1+L_h^*\Delta t)^n\le e^{L_h^*T}$ yields $e_n\le C_{h,T}\Delta t$ with, for example, $C_{h,T}=\frac12M_h(e^{L_h^*T}-1)$ when $L_h^*>0$ and $C_{h,T}=0$ when $L_h^*=0$.

The continuous exact trajectory is compactly contained in $\operatorname{int}\mathcal C$ over the compact time interval, so there is a positive minimum distance $\delta$ from every nodal exact state to $\mathbb R^{d+2}\setminus\mathcal C$. Choose $\Delta t$ so small that $C_{h,T}\Delta t<\delta$. Inductively, after an accepted stage the recurrence in step 3.1 bounds the next candidate's distance from the exact next state by less than $\delta$, so every candidate node remains in $\mathcal C$ and [F4] accepts it. This proves all $N$ steps are accepted; [F5] confirms finite return within the stated budget. The estimate in step 3.1 then holds for every returned stage.

Fix an integer $d\ge1$, a gas constant $R>0$, an adiabatic exponent $\gamma>1$, a constant reference entropy $s_0\in\mathbb R$, shear viscosity $\mu>0$, bulk viscosity $\zeta\ge0$, and heat conductivity $\kappa>0$. Put $c_v=R/(\gamma-1)$. A conservative state is $U=(\rho,m,E)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R$. Its **admissible state set** is

$$\mathcal G=\left\{(\rho,m,E):\rho>0,\ E>\frac{|m|^2}{2\rho}\right\}.$$

For $U\in\mathcal G$, define the velocity $u=m/\rho$, internal-energy density $\varepsilon=E-|m|^2/(2\rho)$, pressure $p=(\gamma-1)\varepsilon$, temperature $T=p/(R\rho)$, specific entropy $s(U)=c_v\log(p/\rho^\gamma)+s_0$, and mathematical entropy $\eta(U)=-\rho s(U)$. The Euler flux in coordinate direction $j$ is

$$F_j(U)=\bigl(\rho u_j,\ m u_j+p e_j,\ (E+p)u_j\bigr),\qquad j=1,\ldots,d,$$

where $e_j$ is the $j$th standard basis vector of $\mathbb R^d$. The mathematical entropy flux is $q_j(U)=\eta(U)u_j$.

For a differentiable velocity field, write $D=\operatorname{sym}\nabla u$ with $D_{ab}=(\partial_bu_a+\partial_au_b)/2$, and $D^0=D-(\operatorname{tr}D/d)I$. The Newtonian stress and Fourier viscous flux are

$$\tau=2\mu D^0+\zeta(\operatorname{tr}D)I, \qquad F_j^{\mathrm{visc}}=\bigl(0,\tau_{j1},\ldots,\tau_{jd},\ u\cdot\tau_{j\cdot}+\kappa\partial_jT\bigr).$$

The **compressible Navier–Stokes–Fourier balance law** is the conservative system

$$\partial_tU+\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_jF_j(U) =\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_jF_j^{\mathrm{visc}}(U,\nabla u,\nabla T).$$

Unless a boundary is specified separately, a periodic solution means that all fields and fluxes are periodic in each spatial coordinate. The positive parameters and the inequalities defining $\mathcal G$ imply $p>0$ and $T>0$.

For the ideal-gas model in [[def-compressible-navier-stokes-fourier-model]], the mathematical entropy $\eta=-\rho s$ has positive-definite Hessian on $\mathcal G$. Its entropy variables are

$$v(U)=\nabla_U\eta(U)=\left(c_v\gamma-s-\frac{\beta|u|^2}{2},\ \beta u,\ -\beta\right),\qquad \beta=\frac{c_v\rho}{\varepsilon}=\frac1T.$$

The Euler entropy flux $q_j(U)=\eta(U)u_j$ is compatible with $F_j$, meaning $\nabla_Uq_j=(\nabla_U\eta)^TDF_j$, and its entropy potential is $\psi_j(U)=v(U)^TF_j(U)-q_j(U)=\rho R u_j$. Consequently $U\mapsto v(U)$ is a local diffeomorphism at every $U\in\mathcal G$ and $\eta$ is strictly convex on $\mathcal G$.

derivations.claim: For $U_n$, $\rho_n>0$, $\varepsilon_n=E_n=1/n>|0|^2/(2\rho_n)$, so $U_n\in\mathcal G$. The formulas [F1] give $p_n=1/n$, $T_n=1$, and $s_n=\log((1/n)/(1/n)^2)=\log n$.
Here $u_n=0$ and $\beta_n=1$. Substitution into [F2] gives $v_{\rho,n}=2-\log n$ and $v_{E,n}=-1$, hence $|v_{\rho,n}|\to\infty$.

The states satisfy $U_n\to(0,0,0)$, which is outside $\mathcal G$ because its density is zero. Every compact subset of Euclidean state space is closed, so a compact $\mathcal C\Subset\mathcal G$ containing every $U_n$ would also contain their limit, a contradiction.

Let $U$ be a smooth solution with values in $\mathcal G$ of the unforced balance law in [[def-compressible-navier-stokes-fourier-model]]. Then

$$\partial_t\eta(U)+\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_j\left(\eta(U)u_j+\kappa\frac{\partial_jT}{T}\right) =-\sum_{j,k=1}^d(\partial_jv)^TK_{jk}(U)(\partial_kv) =-\left(\frac{\tau:\nabla u}{T}+\frac{\kappa|\nabla T|^2}{T^2}\right)\le0.$$

derivations.claim: Since $T(x)\ge1$, $\rho=1$, $u=0$, $m=0$, and $E=c_vT>0$, the state lies in $\mathcal G$. The equation of state gives $p=(\gamma-1)c_vT=RT$. The stress is zero because $u_x=0$, so $F_1=(0,RT,0)$ and $F_1^{\mathrm{visc}}=(0,0,\kappa\cos x)$.

The state is stationary, so $\partial_tU=0$. Direct differentiation gives $\partial_xF_1=(0,R\cos x,0)$ and $\partial_xF_1^{\mathrm{visc}}=(0,0,-\kappa\sin x)$. Therefore $\partial_xF_1^{\mathrm{visc}}+S=\partial_xF_1$, proving the forced balance componentwise.

The physical production is $\tau u_x/T+\kappa T_x^2/T^2=\kappa\cos^2x/T^2$. For a source $S$, multiplying the conservative equation by $v$ adds $v^TS$ to the right side of the mathematical-entropy identity [F2]; here $v^TS=-\kappa\sin x/T$. The left-side entropy flux derivative is $\partial_x(\kappa\cos x/T)= -\kappa\sin x/T-\kappa\cos^2x/T^2$, which equals minus the production plus $v^TS$. Periodicity removes endpoint contributions.

derivations.claim: The profile has $T(y)\ge T_w>0$, so $\rho>0$. Its internal-energy density is $E-|m|^2/(2\rho)=p_0/(\gamma-1)$, hence [F1] gives $p=p_0$. The velocity gradient has only $\partial_yu_1=a$, so $\nabla\cdot u=0$, $\tau_{12}=\tau_{21}=\mu a$, and all entries of $\tau$ are constant.

The stress production is $\tau:\nabla u=\mu a^2$. The physical entropy law [F2], no normal velocity at either wall, and periodicity in $x$ give the boundary-flux identity after integration in $y$. Directly, $(\kappa T'/T)'=\kappa T''/T-\kappa(T')^2/T^2=-\mu a^2/T-\kappa(T')^2/T^2$, so integrating its negative proves the equality. The integrand is strictly positive because $a\ne0$, $\mu>0$, and $T>0$.

Let $\mathcal I=\{1,\ldots,M\}$ be a nonempty finite periodic node set. Let $H\in\mathbb R^{M\times M}$ be diagonal with strictly positive entries, and for each direction $j=1,\ldots,d$ let $D_j\in\mathbb R^{M\times M}$ satisfy the periodic diagonal-norm SBP identities

$$HD_j+D_j^TH=0,\qquad D_j\mathbf1=0.$$

For a nodal array $w=(w_i)_{i\in\mathcal I}$, $D_jw$ means componentwise matrix multiplication, $(D_jw)_i=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal I}(D_j)_{i\ell}w_\ell$. Given admissible nodal states $U_i\in\mathcal G$, write $v_i=v(U_i)$. Define the semidiscrete system

$$\dot U_i+2\sum_{j=1}^d\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal I}(D_j)_{i\ell}F_j^{\mathrm{ec}}(U_i,U_\ell) =\sum_{j,k=1}^d\left[D_j\left(\bigl(K_{jk}(U_i)(D_kv)_i\bigr)_{i\in\mathcal I}\right)\right]_i, \qquad i\in\mathcal I,$$

where $F_j^{\mathrm{ec}}$ is the two-point flux in [[def-ideal-gas-entropy-conservative-pair-flux]] and $K_{jk}$ is the viscous block matrix in [[lem-compressible-viscous-flux-entropy-variable-factorization]]. This definition specifies a periodic semidiscrete operator on $\mathcal G^M$; it does not include a time discretization or a positivity limiter.

The flux in [[def-ideal-gas-entropy-conservative-pair-flux]] is well-defined for every pair in $\mathcal G\times\mathcal G$, symmetric in its two states, and consistent in the sense that $F_j^{\mathrm{ec}}(U,U)=F_j(U)$. It satisfies

$$(v(U_R)-v(U_L))^TF_j^{\mathrm{ec}}(U_L,U_R)=\psi_j(U_R)-\psi_j(U_L).$$

The flux is locally Lipschitz on $\mathcal G\times\mathcal G$.

For $U\in\mathcal G$, let $Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_d)$ and $W=(W_1,\ldots,W_d)$ be arrays of entropy-variable gradients, with $Z_k,W_k\in\mathbb R^{d+2}$. Write $Z_{k,m_\ell}$ for the momentum-variable component and $Z_{k,E}$ for the energy-variable component. Define

$$G_{k\ell}(Z)=Z_{k,m_\ell}+u_\ell Z_{k,E},\qquad c_k(Z)=Z_{k,E},$$

and $G^0(Z)=\operatorname{sym}G(Z)-(\operatorname{tr}G(Z)/d)I$. Define the linear map

$$\mathcal R_U Z=\bigl(\sqrt{2\mu T}\,G^0(Z),\ \sqrt{\zeta T}\,\operatorname{tr}G(Z),\ \sqrt{\kappa}\,T c(Z)\bigr).$$

The bilinear form

$$\mathcal B_U(Z,W)=2\mu T\,G^0(Z):G^0(W)+\zeta T\,\operatorname{tr}G(Z)\operatorname{tr}G(W)+\kappa T^2\sum_{k=1}^d c_k(Z)c_k(W)$$

has the factorization $\mathcal B_U(Z,W)=(\mathcal R_UZ)\cdot(\mathcal R_UW)=\sum_{j,k}Z_j^TK_{jk}(U)W_k$, so $K(U)=\mathcal R_U^*\mathcal R_U$ is a symmetric positive-semidefinite block matrix. For $Z_k=\partial_kv(U)$, its blocks give exactly the model viscous flux $F_j^{\mathrm{visc}}=\sum_kK_{jk}(U)\partial_kv$, and

$$\sum_{j,k}(\partial_jv)^TK_{jk}(U)(\partial_kv)=\frac{\tau:\nabla u}{T}+\frac{\kappa|\nabla T|^2}{T^2}\ge0.$$

For the ideal-gas model in [[def-compressible-navier-stokes-fourier-model]], the mathematical entropy $\eta=-\rho s$ has positive-definite Hessian on $\mathcal G$. Its entropy variables are

$$v(U)=\nabla_U\eta(U)=\left(c_v\gamma-s-\frac{\beta|u|^2}{2},\ \beta u,\ -\beta\right),\qquad \beta=\frac{c_v\rho}{\varepsilon}=\frac1T.$$

The Euler entropy flux $q_j(U)=\eta(U)u_j$ is compatible with $F_j$, meaning $\nabla_Uq_j=(\nabla_U\eta)^TDF_j$, and its entropy potential is $\psi_j(U)=v(U)^TF_j(U)-q_j(U)=\rho R u_j$. Consequently $U\mapsto v(U)$ is a local diffeomorphism at every $U\in\mathcal G$ and $\eta$ is strictly convex on $\mathcal G$.

Formula [F4] gives $v_{E}=(-1,-1/2,-1)$ and $v_m=(0,0,0)$. Multiplication by $D$ gives $Dv_E=(1/4,0,-1/4)$ and $Dv_m=0$. Since $u_i=0$, the strain array $G$ in [F3] vanishes at every node.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice for the published Sobolev interfaces cited below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and use real scalars. $L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$ means the $d$-tuple of real $L^2$ equivalence classes, with norm $\|v\|_2^2=\sum_{j=1}^d\|v_j\|_2^2$. The test space $C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R)$ consists of real smooth functions compactly supported in $D$.

For $v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$, say that $g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$ is its distributional divergence when
$$
\int_D v\cdot\nabla\phi\,dx=-\int_D g\phi\,dx\qquad\text{for every }\phi\in C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R).
$$
The $L^2$ class $g$ is unique when it exists. Indeed, if $g_1,g_2$ both satisfy the identity, put $h=g_1-g_2\in L^2(D)$. Every compact $C\subset D$ has finite Lebesgue measure by [[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]], and [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]] gives $\int_C|h|\le |C|^{1/2}\|h\|_{L^2(D)}<\infty$. Thus $h\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$. Subtracting the two divergence identities gives $\int_Dh\phi=0$ for every real test $\phi$; splitting a complex test into real and imaginary parts gives the same identity for complex tests. Injectivity of the regular-distribution map in [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] therefore yields $h=0$ almost everywhere, hence $g_1=g_2$ as $L^2$ classes. Define
$$
H(\operatorname{div};D):=\{v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d):\text{there is }g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)\text{ with }g=\operatorname{div}v\text{ distributionally}\},
$$
and equip it with the graph norm
$$
\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div};D)}:=\bigl(\|v\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}v\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}.
$$
The Sobolev notation $H^1(D)=W^{1,2}(D)$ and $H^1_0(D)=W^{1,2}_0(D)$ uses the norm and zero-boundary closure conventions of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]. No pointwise boundary value is part of this definition.

Assume Countable Choice for the Sobolev-space interfaces below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and $v\in H(\operatorname{div};D)$. Define the trace quotient
$$T_D:=H^1(D)/H^1_0(D),\qquad \|[w]\|_{T_D}:=\inf_{z\in H^1_0(D)}\|w+z\|_{H^1(D)}.$$
Then the formula
$$
\langle\gamma_n v,[w]\rangle:=\int_D\bigl(v\cdot\nabla w+(\operatorname{div}v)w\bigr)\,dx
$$
is independent of the representative $w$, defines a bounded real linear functional $\gamma_n v\in T_D'$, and satisfies $\|\gamma_n v\|_{T_D'}\le\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div};D)}$. This functional is the weak normal trace; no pointwise boundary value is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of

hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative

$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$

[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes

metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$

$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by

derivations.claim:
Approximate $\delta u$ by compactly supported smooth functions. The distributional divergence identity and $L^{2}$ continuity give $(\delta\sigma,
abla\delta u)=-(div\delta\sigma,\delta u)$. Substitute $\delta\sigma=R_1z-
abla\delta u$ to get $g^2=(R_1z,
abla\delta u)+(R_2z,\delta u)$.

Cauchy–Schwarz and [F3] imply $g^2\le ag+C_Pbg$. If $g>0$, divide by $g$; if $g=0$, the bound is immediate. Poincare and $\delta\sigma=R_1z-\nabla\delta u$ give the stated component estimates, controlling the product graph norm.

The first residual square is at most $2\|\delta\sigma\|_2^2+2\|\nabla\delta u\|_2^2$ and the second is the divergence component. If $Rz=0$, step 2.1 and Poincare give $\delta u=0$, then $\delta\sigma=0$. This proves reverse boundedness and injectivity.

$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by

for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$

axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

$$f(x)=\langle x,y\rangle\qquad\text{for every }x\in H,$$

Under the first-variable-linear convention the representing vector depends conjugate-linearly and isometrically on $f$: if $f_i$ is represented by $y_i$ and $a,b$ are scalars, then $af_1+bf_2$ is represented by $\overline a\,y_1+\overline b\,y_2$.

$$T_D:=H^1(D)/H^1_0(D),\qquad \|[w]\|_{T_D}:=\inf_{z\in H^1_0(D)}\|w+z\|_{H^1(D)}.$$

$$

The test space $C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R)$ consists of real smooth functions compactly supported in $D$.

For $v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$, say that $g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$ is its distributional divergence when
$$
\int_D v\cdot\nabla\phi\,dx=-\int_D g\phi\,dx\qquad\text{for every }\phi\in C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R).
$$
The $L^2$ class $g$ is unique when it exists. Indeed, if $g_1,g_2$ both satisfy the identity, put $h=g_1-g_2\in L^2(D)$. Every compact $C\subset D$ has finite Lebesgue measure by [[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]], and [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]] gives $\int_C|h|\le |C|^{1/2}\|h\|_{L^2(D)}<\infty$. Thus $h\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$. Subtracting the two divergence identities gives $\int_Dh\phi=0$ for every real test $\phi$; splitting a complex test into real and imaginary parts gives the same identity for complex tests. Injectivity of the regular-distribution map in [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] therefore yields $h=0$ almost everywhere, hence $g_1=g_2$ as $L^2$ classes. Define
$$
H(\operatorname{div};D):=\{v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d):\text{there is }g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)\text{ with }g=\operatorname{div}v\text{ distributionally}\},
$$

$$
\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div};D)}:=\bigl(\|v\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}v\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. For every open $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, the real space $H(\operatorname{div};D)$ with the graph inner product
$$
(v,w)_{H(\operatorname{div})}:=(v,w)_{L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)}+(\operatorname{div}v,\operatorname{div}w)_{L^2(D)}
$$
is a Hilbert space. Its subspace $H_0(\operatorname{div};D)$ of [[def-na-h0div-space]] is closed, hence is Hilbert with the restricted inner product.

Assume Countable Choice for the Sobolev-space interfaces below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and $v\in H(\operatorname{div};D)$. Define the trace quotient
$$T_D:=H^1(D)/H^1_0(D),\qquad \|[w]\|_{T_D}:=\inf_{z\in H^1_0(D)}\|w+z\|_{H^1(D)}.$$
Then the formula
$$
\langle\gamma_n v,[w]\rangle:=\int_D\bigl(v\cdot\nabla w+(\operatorname{div}v)w\bigr)\,dx
$$
is independent of the representative $w$, defines a bounded real linear functional $\gamma_n v\in T_D'$, and satisfies $\|\gamma_n v\|_{T_D'}\le\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div};D)}$. This functional is the weak normal trace; no pointwise boundary value is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. For a nondegenerate affine simplex $K$ with diameter $h_K$ and shape bound $h_K/r_K\le\gamma$, and any facet $F$, every $u\in H^1(K)$ has a well-defined trace $\gamma_Fu\in L^2(F)$ and
$$
\|\gamma_Fu\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le C(d,\gamma)\bigl(h_K^{-1}\|u\|_{L^2(K)}^2+h_K\|\nabla u\|_{L^2(K)}^2\bigr).
$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a polyhedral open set with a conforming affine simplicial mesh, let $K_+$ and $K_-$ share an interior facet $F$, and let $w\in H^1(D)$. The elementwise $L^2(F)$ traces of $w|_{K_+}$ and $w|_{K_-}$ agree almost everywhere on $F$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d=2$ or $3$, $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral and $\mathcal T_h$ a finite conforming shape-regular simplicial partition; all fields are real. For a load $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, put $H(div,\mathcal T_h)=\prod_KH(div;K)$ and $H^1(\mathcal T_h)=\prod_KH^1(K)$, with squared broken graph norm $\sum_K(\|	au\|_2^2+\|div	au\|_2^2+\|v\|_2^2+\|
abla v\|_2^2)$. Let $\widehat U$ be the elementwise trace range of $H^1_0(\Omega)$ and $\widehat Q_n$ the elementwise weak normal trace range of $H(div;\Omega)$, each with global lift infimum norm; range membership is compatibility and normal traces are conservative across interior facets. $$b(x,y)=(\sigma,	au)-(u,div_h	au)+\langle\widehat u,	au\cdot nangle-(\sigma,
abla_hv)+\langle\widehat\sigma_n,vangle,\quad F_f(y)=(f,v).$$
Pairings sum over cell boundaries and use the cell-outward normal. The sign convention is $\sigma=-
abla u$, $div\sigma=f$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space and let
$L^2(\mu)$ be the quotient of $\mathcal L^2(\mu)$ by the almost-everywhere zero
functions ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]), with the quotient
norm $\|\cdot\|_2$ ([[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]).

1. On **real** $L^2(\mu)$ the formula
   $$\langle f,g\rangle:=\int fg\,d\mu$$is a well-defined inner product, linear in both variables, positive definite, with $\langle f,f\rangle=\|f\|_2^2$; with it $L^2(\mu)$ is a real Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). 2. On **complex** $L^2(\mu;\mathbb C)$ the formula$$\langle f,g\rangle:=\int f\overline g\,d\mu$$
   is a well-defined inner product, linear in the first variable and
   conjugate-linear in the second, positive definite, with
   $\langle f,f\rangle=\|f\|_2^2$; with it $L^2(\mu;\mathbb C)$ is a complex
   Hilbert space ([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]).

In both cases the inner product induces exactly the established quotient
$L^2$ norm.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

For the zero multi-index, set $D^0u=u$. Since $\mathcal A_0=\{0\}$,
$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$
The formula is finite because each derivative class belongs to $L^p$ and
$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

For open $U\subseteq\Omega$ with $\overline U$ compact and contained in
$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume Countable Choice for the published Sobolev interfaces cited below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and use real scalars. $L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$ means the $d$-tuple of real $L^2$ equivalence classes, with norm $\|v\|_2^2=\sum_{j=1}^d\|v_j\|_2^2$. The test space $C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R)$ consists of real smooth functions compactly supported in $D$.

For $v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$, say that $g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$ is its distributional divergence when
$$
\int_D v\cdot\nabla\phi\,dx=-\int_D g\phi\,dx\qquad\text{for every }\phi\in C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R).
$$
The $L^2$ class $g$ is unique when it exists. Indeed, if $g_1,g_2$ both satisfy the identity, put $h=g_1-g_2\in L^2(D)$. Every compact $C\subset D$ has finite Lebesgue measure by [[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]], and [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]] gives $\int_C|h|\le |C|^{1/2}\|h\|_{L^2(D)}<\infty$. Thus $h\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$. Subtracting the two divergence identities gives $\int_Dh\phi=0$ for every real test $\phi$; splitting a complex test into real and imaginary parts gives the same identity for complex tests. Injectivity of the regular-distribution map in [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] therefore yields $h=0$ almost everywhere, hence $g_1=g_2$ as $L^2$ classes. Define
$$
H(\operatorname{div};D):=\{v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d):\text{there is }g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)\text{ with }g=\operatorname{div}v\text{ distributionally}\},
$$
and equip it with the graph norm
$$
\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div};D)}:=\bigl(\|v\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}v\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}.
$$
The Sobolev notation $H^1(D)=W^{1,2}(D)$ and $H^1_0(D)=W^{1,2}_0(D)$ uses the norm and zero-boundary closure conventions of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]. No pointwise boundary value is part of this definition.

derivations.claim: H1 is complete: completeness of real $L^{2}$ [F6] gives limits in $L^{2}$ of a Cauchy sequence and each weak derivative satisfy distributional derivative identities by testing against compactly supported smooth functions and passing both integrals to their limits. H1_0 is closed by its closure definition. The scalar trace-quotient map is continuous because $\|[u|_K]\|_{H^1(K)/H^1_0(K)}\le\|u|_K\|_{H^1(K)}$ on each cell; the finite product preserves continuity. The normal map is continuous by [F2], again with a finite product. Thus both kernels are closed.

Let $\tau\in H(\operatorname{div};\Omega)$ and let an interior facet $F=K_+\cap K_-$ be fixed. For $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\operatorname{relint}F)$, choose a smooth function $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ supported in a small tubular neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}\psi$ meeting only $K_+$ and $K_-$ and having trace $\psi$ on $F$. The global distributional-divergence identity [F8] gives $\int_\Omega(\tau\cdot\nabla\phi+(\operatorname{div}\tau)\phi)=0$. Applying the cell Green identity [F2] to the two restrictions, with all other cell traces zero, yields $$\langle\gamma_{n_+,K_+}(\tau|_{K_+}),[\phi|_{K_+}]\rangle+\langle\gamma_{n_-,K_-}(\tau|_{K_-}),[\phi|_{K_-}]\rangle=0.$$ The two cell trace classes in this equation restrict to the same $\psi$ on $F$ and vanish on the other facets. Since this holds for every such $\psi$, the two outward weak normal traces cancel as distributions on the relative interior of each interior facet. This is the conservative facet relation for a global H(div) lift; it uses the distributional divergence identity and weak Green formula, not pointwise normal values.

For a closed subspace $M$ of a Hilbert space, a distance-minimizing sequence is Cauchy by the parallelogram identity; its limit is nearest, and variation along $M$ makes the residual orthogonal. Thus $H=M\oplus M^\perp$ and $H/M$ is isometric to $M^\perp$. Applying this to both kernels in step 1.1 proves the quotient ranges are Hilbert with their infimum norms.

Global lifts restrict to broken lifts; conversely the admissible broken extensions in the Statement are exactly those gluing to a global lift, so the two infima have the same set. Cell scalar traces are bounded by [F3] and those of a global H1 lift match across interior facets by [F4]; normal traces of a global H(div) lift satisfy the cancellation proved in step 1.2. Thus range membership is precisely the stated compatibility, with the global lift infimum norms.

**Admissible conditions:** $N\ge0$; all entries are real and exact; $\ell_w$ is defined and linear on $V_r(K)$. The Gram entries and functional values are evaluated exactly. No quadrature or rounded solve is part of this procedure.

2. Initialize $L=I_N$ and compute an unpivoted symmetric $LDL^{\mathsf T}$ factorization in the listed order. At pivot $k$, set

values $\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_n>0$. Define the spectral condition number
of the rectangular matrix $A$ by

$$\kappa_2(A):=\frac{\sigma_1}{\sigma_n};$$

for a square invertible $A$ this agrees with
$\lVert A\rVert_2\lVert A^{-1}\rVert_2$ of
[[def-condition-number-of-a-nonsingular-linear-system]]. Then:

1. The normal-equation matrix $A^{\mathsf T}A$ is invertible, with
   $\kappa_2(A^{\mathsf T}A)=\kappa_2(A)^{2}$;
2. equivalently,

[[thm-least-squares-solutions-and-normal-equation]] therefore has condition
number exactly the square of the condition number of the least-squares problem
itself.

statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d=2$ or $3$, $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral and $\mathcal T_h$ a finite conforming shape-regular simplicial partition; all fields are real. For a load $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, put $H(div,\mathcal T_h)=\prod_KH(div;K)$ and $H^1(\mathcal T_h)=\prod_KH^1(K)$, with squared broken graph norm $\sum_K(\|	au\|_2^2+\|div	au\|_2^2+\|v\|_2^2+\|
abla v\|_2^2)$. Let $\widehat U$ be the elementwise trace range of $H^1_0(\Omega)$ and $\widehat Q_n$ the elementwise weak normal trace range of $H(div;\Omega)$, each with global lift infimum norm; range membership is compatibility and normal traces are conservative across interior facets. Set $U=L^2(\Omega)^d	imes L^2(\Omega)	imes\widehat U	imes\widehat Q_n$, $V=H(div,\mathcal T_h)	imes H^1(\mathcal T_h)$. For $x=(\sigma,u,\widehat u,\widehat\sigma_n)$ and $y=(	au,v)$, define
$$b(x,y)=(\sigma,	au)-(u,div_h	au)+\langle\widehat u,	au\cdot nangle-(\sigma,
abla_hv)+\langle\widehat\sigma_n,vangle,\quad F_f(y)=(f,v).$$
Pairings sum over cell boundaries and use the cell-outward normal. The sign convention is $\sigma=-
abla u$, $div\sigma=f$.

Assume Countable Choice and [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]]. The elementwise trace map $\Gamma_0:H^1_0(\Omega)\to\prod_KH^1(K)/H^1_0(K)$ and normal-trace map $\Gamma_n:H(div;\Omega)\to\prod_K(H^1(K)/H^1_0(K))'$ have real Hilbert quotient ranges with global lift infimum norms. These equal the infima over broken extensions whose gluing belongs to the respective global space. Compatibility means membership in these ranges, so normal traces are conservative on each interior facet in the weak distributional sense.

Assume Countable Choice for the Sobolev-space interfaces below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and $v\in H(\operatorname{div};D)$. Define the trace quotient
$$T_D:=H^1(D)/H^1_0(D),\qquad \|[w]\|_{T_D}:=\inf_{z\in H^1_0(D)}\|w+z\|_{H^1(D)}.$$

Assume Countable Choice for the published Sobolev interfaces cited below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and use real scalars. $L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$ means the $d$-tuple of real $L^2$ equivalence classes, with norm $\|v\|_2^2=\sum_{j=1}^d\|v_j\|_2^2$. The test space $C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R)$ consists of real smooth functions compactly supported in $D$.

For $v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$, say that $g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$ is its distributional divergence when
$$
\int_D v\cdot\nabla\phi\,dx=-\int_D g\phi\,dx\qquad\text{for every }\phi\in C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R).
$$
The $L^2$ class $g$ is unique when it exists. Indeed, if $g_1,g_2$ both satisfy the identity, put $h=g_1-g_2\in L^2(D)$. Every compact $C\subset D$ has finite Lebesgue measure by [[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]], and [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]] gives $\int_C|h|\le |C|^{1/2}\|h\|_{L^2(D)}<\infty$. Thus $h\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$. Subtracting the two divergence identities gives $\int_Dh\phi=0$ for every real test $\phi$; splitting a complex test into real and imaginary parts gives the same identity for complex tests. Injectivity of the regular-distribution map in [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] therefore yields $h=0$ almost everywhere, hence $g_1=g_2$ as $L^2$ classes. Define
$$
H(\operatorname{div};D):=\{v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d):\text{there is }g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)\text{ with }g=\operatorname{div}v\text{ distributionally}\},
$$
and equip it with the graph norm
$$
\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div};D)}:=\bigl(\|v\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}v\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}.
$$
The Sobolev notation $H^1(D)=W^{1,2}(D)$ and $H^1_0(D)=W^{1,2}_0(D)$ uses the norm and zero-boundary closure conventions of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]. No pointwise boundary value is part of this definition.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

For the zero multi-index, set $D^0u=u$. Since $\mathcal A_0=\{0\}$,
$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$
The formula is finite because each derivative class belongs to $L^p$ and
$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

For open $U\subseteq\Omega$ with $\overline U$ compact and contained in
$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, and suppose its first coordinate projection is contained in an interval $(a,b)$ of width $L=b-a$. For every real $v\in H^1_0(D)$,
$$\|v\|_{L^2(D)}\le L\|\partial_1v\|_{L^2(D)}\le L\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(D)}.$$

derivations.claim: Compactly supported vector tests on each cell give $\sigma+\nabla u=0$ distributionally; compactly supported scalar tests give $div\sigma=0$. Thus $u|_K\in H^1(K)$, $\sigma|_K\in H(div;K)$, and both identities hold cellwise.

With $\sigma=-\nabla u$, the first local equation and [F3] give $\langle\widehat u-u|_{\partial K},\gamma_n\tau\rangle=0$ for every $\tau\in H(div;K)$. Surjectivity [F4] makes the scalar trace classes equal. The second local equation gives $\langle\widehat\sigma_n-\gamma_n\sigma,v\rangle=0$ for every $v\in H^1(K)$, so those normal-trace functionals are equal as well.

Take a global H1_0 lift $u_0$ of $\widehat u$. On each cell, $u-u_0$ has zero scalar trace, hence belongs to $H^1_0(K)$; zero-extending compactly supported approximants and summing over the finite mesh shows $u-u_0\in H^1_0(\Omega)$, so $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$. Take a global H(div) lift $\sigma_0$ of $\widehat\sigma_n$. The cell field $\sigma-\sigma_0$ has zero weak normal trace on every cell. Summing its local Green identities against restrictions of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ shows its piecewise $L^{2}$ divergence is its global distributional divergence; thus it glues to H(div), and $\sigma\in H(div;\Omega)$. Now $\sigma=-\nabla u$ and $div\sigma=0$; the weak Green identity tested with $u\in H^1_0$ gives $\|\nabla u\|_2^2=0$. By [F6], $u=0$, then $\sigma$ and both trace components vanish.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be bounded connected Lipschitz and $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. Solve $-\Delta u=f$, $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$; set $\sigma=-\nabla u$, so $\operatorname{div}\sigma=f$. For a finite conforming shape-regular triangular mesh, define $X_h=RT_0(\mathcal T_h)\times(P_1(\mathcal T_h)\cap H^1_0(\Omega))$ and $J_h(\sigma_h,u_h)=\|\sigma_h+\nabla u_h\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}\sigma_h-f\|_2^2$. Here $RT_0(K)=P_0(K)^2+xP_0(K)$ and $P_1$ is continuous piecewise affine. The real Sobolev-space and zero-boundary conventions are [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]; H(div), mesh, and RT conventions are [[def-na-hdiv-space]] and [[def-na-simplicial-mesh-rt-bdm-spaces]]. This is the plan-spec PE30 sign convention; negating the design flux converts its residuals to these and preserves the squared objective. Integrals are exact; geometry, quadrature and roundoff errors are excluded.

Assume Countable Choice and the mesh conventions of [[def-na-simplicial-mesh-rt-bdm-spaces]]. On each $d$-simplex $K$, $\operatorname{RT}_0(K)=\{a+cx:a\in\mathbb R^d,c\in\mathbb R\}$ has dimension $d+1$, and the $d+1$ integrated outward facet-normal fluxes determine its element uniquely. A piecewise RT0 field belongs to $H(\operatorname{div};D)$ exactly when its oriented integrated fluxes match across every shared facet; such a field belongs to $H_0(\operatorname{div};D)$ exactly when its normal component (equivalently its integrated outward flux) also vanishes on every boundary facet.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D$ be a polyhedral open set with a conforming affine simplicial mesh, let $K_+$ and $K_-$ share an interior facet $F$, and let $w\in H^1(D)$. The elementwise $L^2(F)$ traces of $w|_{K_+}$ and $w|_{K_-}$ agree almost everywhere on $F$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d=2$ or $3$, $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral and $\mathcal T_h$ a finite conforming shape-regular simplicial partition; all fields are real. For a load $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, put $H(div,\mathcal T_h)=\prod_KH(div;K)$ and $H^1(\mathcal T_h)=\prod_KH^1(K)$, with squared broken graph norm $\sum_K(\|	au\|_2^2+\|div	au\|_2^2+\|v\|_2^2+\|
abla v\|_2^2)$. Let $\widehat U$ be the elementwise trace range of $H^1_0(\Omega)$ and $\widehat Q_n$ the elementwise weak normal trace range of $H(div;\Omega)$, each with global lift infimum norm; range membership is compatibility and normal traces are conservative across interior facets. Set $U=L^2(\Omega)^d	imes L^2(\Omega)	imes\widehat U	imes\widehat Q_n$, $V=H(div,\mathcal T_h)	imes H^1(\mathcal T_h)$. For $x=(\sigma,u,\widehat u,\widehat\sigma_n)$ and $y=(	au,v)$, define
$$b(x,y)=(\sigma,	au)-(u,div_h	au)+\langle\widehat u,	au\cdot nangle-(\sigma,
abla_hv)+\langle\widehat\sigma_n,vangle,\quad F_f(y)=(f,v).$$
Pairings sum over cell boundaries and use the cell-outward normal. The sign convention is $\sigma=-
abla u$, $div\sigma=f$.

Assume Countable Choice and [[def-na-ultraweak-poisson-dpg-formulation]]. The elementwise trace map $\Gamma_0:H^1_0(\Omega)\to\prod_KH^1(K)/H^1_0(K)$ and normal-trace map $\Gamma_n:H(div;\Omega)\to\prod_K(H^1(K)/H^1_0(K))'$ have real Hilbert quotient ranges with global lift infimum norms. These equal the infima over broken extensions whose gluing belongs to the respective global space. Compatibility means membership in these ranges, so normal traces are conservative on each interior facet in the weak distributional sense.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded, connected polyhedral Lipschitz domain. A matching affine simplicial mesh and its shape regularity have the exact meaning of [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]; additionally, call the mesh facet-connected when its dual graph (one vertex per cell and one edge per shared $(d-1)$-facet) is connected. Write $h=\max_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\operatorname{diam}K$.

For $k\ge0$, $\mathbb P_k(K)$ is the real scalar polynomial space of total degree at most $k$, and $\widetilde{\mathbb P}_k$ is the real homogeneous scalar polynomial space of degree exactly $k$ (for $k=0$, the constants). Define
$$\operatorname{RT}_k(K)=\mathbb P_k(K;\mathbb R^d)+x\widetilde{\mathbb P}_k(K),\qquad \operatorname{BDM}_k(K)=\mathbb P_k(K;\mathbb R^d)\quad(k\ge1).$$
For either local family $X_k$, its global H(div)-conforming space is
$$X_k(\mathcal T_h)=\{v\in H(\operatorname{div};D):v|_K\in X_k(K)\text{ for every }K\in\mathcal T_h\}.
$$
The zero-normal RT0 flux space and mean-zero P0 pressure space are
$$V_h:=\operatorname{RT}_0(\mathcal T_h)\cap H_0(\operatorname{div};D),\qquad Q_h:=\{q\in L^2(D):q|_K\text{ is constant for every }K,\ \int_Dq=0\}.$$
For each mesh facet $F$, fix one unit normal $n_F$; on a cell boundary use the outward unit normal $n_K$, which equals either $n_F$ or $-n_F$. The notation $\mathbb P_0(\mathcal T_h)$ means cellwise constants. No existence of a mesh for every $D$ is asserted by this definition.

Assume Countable Choice for the Sobolev-space interfaces below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and $v\in H(\operatorname{div};D)$. Define the trace quotient
$$T_D:=H^1(D)/H^1_0(D),\qquad \|[w]\|_{T_D}:=\inf_{z\in H^1_0(D)}\|w+z\|_{H^1(D)}.$$
Then the formula
$$
\langle\gamma_n v,[w]\rangle:=\int_D\bigl(v\cdot\nabla w+(\operatorname{div}v)w\bigr)\,dx
$$
is independent of the representative $w$, defines a bounded real linear functional $\gamma_n v\in T_D'$, and satisfies $\|\gamma_n v\|_{T_D'}\le\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div};D)}$. This functional is the weak normal trace; no pointwise boundary value is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. For a nondegenerate affine simplex $K$ with diameter $h_K$ and shape bound $h_K/r_K\le\gamma$, and any facet $F$, every $u\in H^1(K)$ has a well-defined trace $\gamma_Fu\in L^2(F)$ and
$$
\|\gamma_Fu\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le C(d,\gamma)\bigl(h_K^{-1}\|u\|_{L^2(K)}^2+h_K\|\nabla u\|_{L^2(K)}^2\bigr).
$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

Assume Countable Choice. For every $1\le p<\infty$ there is
$C_{d,p}<\infty$ such that for all
$u\in W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)$,
$$\|u-u_{\widehat S_d}\|_{L^p(\widehat S_d)} \le C_{d,p}|u|_{W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d)},\qquad u_{\widehat S_d}:=|\widehat S_d|^{-1}\int_{\widehat S_d}u\,dx.$$

Let $\widehat K,K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nondegenerate open simplices and let $F_K:\widehat K\to K$ be the orientation-preserving affine bijection $F_K(\widehat x)=A_K\widehat x+b_K$, where $J_K:=\det A_K>0$. For a measurable vector field $\widehat v$ on $\widehat K$, define its contravariant Piola push-forward by
$$
(\mathcal P_K\widehat v)(x):=J_K^{-1}A_K\widehat v(F_K^{-1}(x)),\qquad x\in K.
$$
The inverse pull-back is $\widehat v(\widehat x)=J_KA_K^{-1}v(F_K(\widehat x))$. Facet normals are oriented consistently with the chosen orientation of $F_K$; the associated oriented surface vector transforms by $n\,ds=J_KA_K^{-T}\widehat n\,d\widehat s$.

Let $F(\widehat x)=A\widehat x+b$ be an orientation-preserving affine bijection between nondegenerate $d$-simplices, with $J=\det A>0$, and use the contravariant Piola map of [[def-na-contravariant-piola-map]]. For every $k\ge0$, it maps $\operatorname{RT}_k(\widehat K)$ bijectively onto $\operatorname{RT}_k(K)$, and for every $k\ge1$ it maps $\operatorname{BDM}_k(\widehat K)$ bijectively onto $\operatorname{BDM}_k(K)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d=2$ or $3$ and let $F(\widehat x)=A\widehat x+b$ map a reference
simplex to an affine cell with $\det A>0$. The contravariant Piola map
$\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{div}}\widehat v=(\det A)^{-1}A\widehat v\circ F^{-1}$
maps $H(\operatorname{div},\widehat S_d)$ into $H(\operatorname{div},K)$ and
$$\operatorname{div}(\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{div}}\widehat v) =(\det A)^{-1}(\widehat{\operatorname{div}}\widehat v)\circ F^{-1}.$$
The covariant Piola map
$\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{curl}}\widehat v=A^{-T}\widehat v\circ F^{-1}$
maps $H(\operatorname{curl},\widehat S_d)$ into $H(\operatorname{curl},K)$;
in $d=2$ its scalar curl is
$(\det A)^{-1}(\widehat{\operatorname{curl}}\widehat v)\circ F^{-1}$,
and in $d=3$ its vector curl is
$(\det A)^{-1}A(\widehat{\operatorname{curl}}\widehat v)\circ F^{-1}$.
For every $\widehat u\in W^{1,2}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)$, the scalar
pullback $u=\widehat u\circ F^{-1}$ belongs to $W^{1,2}(K;\mathbb R)$ and
its gradient satisfies
$$\nabla u=\mathcal P_F^{\mathrm{curl}}(\widehat\nabla\widehat u).$$
For smooth fields, contravariant normal fluxes satisfy
$v\cdot n\,dS=\widehat v\cdot\widehat n\,d\widehat S$; covariant tangential
pullbacks satisfy $v(F(\widehat x))\cdot A\widehat\tau=
\widehat v(\widehat x)\cdot\widehat\tau$ for every reference tangent
$\widehat\tau$. Thus edge line integrals and normal-flux moments are
preserved, and face tangential moments transform with this pullback and
the induced facet surface Jacobian. These formulas record the chosen
orientation; reversing a facet orientation reverses its signed moment.

Assume Countable Choice for the Sobolev-space interfaces below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and $v\in H(\operatorname{div};D)$. Define the trace quotient
$$T_D:=H^1(D)/H^1_0(D),\qquad \|[w]\|_{T_D}:=\inf_{z\in H^1_0(D)}\|w+z\|_{H^1(D)}.$$
Then the formula
$$
\langle\gamma_n v,[w]\rangle:=\int_D\bigl(v\cdot\nabla w+(\operatorname{div}v)w\bigr)\,dx
$$
is independent of the representative $w$, defines a bounded real linear functional $\gamma_n v\in T_D'$, and satisfies $\|\gamma_n v\|_{T_D'}\le\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div};D)}$. This functional is the weak normal trace; no pointwise boundary value is asserted.

derivations.claim: On the reference triangle $B^{grad}_3=\{p\in P_3:p(a_i)=0\}$ has dimension $7$. Define $\Pi^0_3w\in B^{grad}_3$ by matching one cell mean and two edge $P_1$ moments on each edge. In the homogeneous system an edge restriction is $t(1-t)(a+bt)$; testing against $a+bt$ forces its weighted square integral to vanish. Each edge restriction is zero, leaving $c\lambda_0\lambda_1\lambda_2$, whose mean forces $c=0$. Hence the seven scalar moments are unisolvent.

On the reference triangle $RT_2=P_2^2+x\widetilde P_2$ has dimension $15$. Its normal trace map is onto broken P2: for an edge $F$ opposite vertex $a_i$, extend any $q\in P_2(F)$ polynomially in the other two barycentric coordinates and set $	au=(x-a_i)q(x)/H_i$, where $H_i$ is the altitude to $F$. This vector is tangent to the other two edges and has normal trace $q$ on $F$; it lies in $RT_2$ because its cubic part is $x$ times a homogeneous degree-two polynomial and its remaining terms lie in $P_2^2$. Thus the broken normal trace image has dimension $9$. Let $B^{div}_3$ be its inverse image of continuous P2 boundary traces, a $12$-dimensional subspace. Define $\Pi^{div}_3	au\in B^{div}_3$ by matching six volume moments against $P_1^2$ and six continuous boundary P2 normal moments. In the homogeneous system the normal trace is continuous P2 and orthogonal to itself, hence zero. Green’s identity and $
abla P_2\subset P_1^2$ then give $div	au=0$; its homogeneous cubic part $xq_2$ has divergence $4q_2$, so $	au\in P_2^2$. Write $	au=R
abla\phi$: explicitly, for polynomial $	au=(	au_1,	au_2)$ use $\phi(x,y)=\int_0^x	au_2(s,0)\,ds-\int_0^y	au_1(x,t)\,dt$. The identity $\partial_x	au_1+\partial_y	au_2=0$ gives $\partial_x\phi=	au_2$ and $\partial_y\phi=-	au_1$, and $\deg\phi\le3$. Zero normal trace makes $\phi$ constant on each edge; vertex continuity makes these constants equal. After subtracting the common constant, $\phi=c\lambda_0\lambda_1\lambda_2$. The volume moment against $Rx$ is $\int_K
abla\phi\cdot x=-2c\int_K\lambda_0\lambda_1\lambda_2$ by Green’s identity and $\phi|_{\partial K}=0$, so $c=0$. Thus the 12 moments are unisolvent.

On the reference triangle set $\widehat\Pi^{grad}_3\widehat v=\bar{\widehat v}+\Pi^0_3(\widehat v-\bar{\widehat v})$; for a physical cell let $F_K(\widehat x)=A_K\widehat x+b_K$ be its orientation-preserving affine map and define $\Pi^{grad}_{3,K}v=(\widehat\Pi^{grad}_3(v\circ F_K))\circ F_K^{-1}$. Affine change of variables preserves the cell mean and, since each edge Jacobian is constant, the edge $P_1$ moments. The bounded inverse reference moment matrix, [F5], mean-zero Poincare–Wirtinger [F7], and shape scaling [F6] yield $\|\Pi^{grad}_{3,K}v\|_{H^1(K)}\le C\|v\|_{H^1(K)}$ and $\|v-\Pi^{grad}_{3,K}v\|_2\le Ch_K\|\nabla v\|_2$.

Let $F_K(\widehat x)=A_K\widehat x+b_K$, $J_K=\det A_K>0$, and $\widehat\tau=J_KA_K^{-1}(\tau\circ F_K)$. Applying [F8] to the affine inverse shows $\widehat\tau\in H(\operatorname{div};\widehat K)$ with the transformed divergence. Define the physical projection by $\Pi^{div}_{3,K}\tau:=\mathcal P_K(\widehat\Pi^{div}_3\widehat\tau)$. For every $w\in H^1(K)$, $w\circ F_K\in H^1(\widehat K)$ by [F8], and the weak Green functional, affine weak-derivative/divergence transformations, and change of variables give $$\langle\gamma_{n,K}\tau,[w]\rangle=\int_{\widehat K}\bigl(\widehat\tau\cdot\widehat\nabla(w\circ F_K)+(\widehat{\operatorname{div}}\widehat\tau)(w\circ F_K)\bigr) =\langle\gamma_{\widehat n,\widehat K}\widehat\tau,[w\circ F_K]\rangle.$$ The volume moments also transport: for $p\in P_1(K)^2$, affine change of variables gives $$(\Pi^{div}_3\tau,p)_K=(\widehat\Pi^{div}_3\widehat\tau,A_K^{\mathsf T}(p\circ F_K))_{\widehat K},\qquad A_K^{\mathsf T}(p\circ F_K)\in P_1(\widehat K)^2,$$ and the same identity with $\widehat\Pi^{div}_3\widehat\tau$ replaced by $\widehat\tau$; hence every physical $P_1(K)^2$ volume moment is matched. This derives the weak normal-trace transport for arbitrary $H(\operatorname{div})$ inputs; it does not infer it from the smooth-field flux identity. Each continuous boundary $P_2$ function on a triangle is the trace of a polynomial in $P_2(K)$ (the six vertex and edge-midpoint values determine that polynomial), so the identity transports exactly the six boundary moments used in step 1.2. By [F8], the Piola-conjugated reference projection lands in $\operatorname{RT}_2(K)\subset P_3(K)^2$. Its reference moment vector is bounded by $C\|\widehat\tau\|_{H(\operatorname{div};\widehat K)}$: volume moments are controlled by $L^2$, and boundary moments by [F9] and the fixed polynomial trace norms. The unisolvent reference moment matrix therefore gives $\|\widehat\Pi^{div}_3\widehat\tau\|_{L^2(\widehat K)}\le C\|\widehat\tau\|_{H(\operatorname{div};\widehat K)}$. In dimension two, [F6] implies $J_K^{1/2}\|A_K^{-1}\|\le C$ and $\|A_K\|J_K^{-1/2}\le C$, while $\|\widehat\tau\|_{L^2}\le C\|\tau\|_{L^2(K)}$ and $\|\widehat{\operatorname{div}}\widehat\tau\|_{L^2}\le C h_K\|\operatorname{div}\tau\|_{L^2(K)}$. Since $h_K\le\operatorname{diam}\Omega$ on the fixed bounded domain, Piola scaling gives $\|\Pi^{div}_3\tau\|_{L^2(K)}\le C_\Omega\|\tau\|_{H(\operatorname{div};K)}$. Finally, for every $q\in P_2(K)$, Green’s formula, the matched volume moments against $\nabla q\in P_1(K)^2$, and the matched continuous boundary moments imply $(\operatorname{div}\Pi^{div}_3\tau,q)_K=(\operatorname{div}\tau,q)_K$. Thus $\operatorname{div}\Pi^{div}_3\tau=P_2(\operatorname{div}\tau)$ and its $L^2$ norm is at most $\|\operatorname{div}\tau\|_{L^2(K)}$. This proves the uniform broken H(div) graph bound.

Vector moments match $\sigma_h\in P_1^2$, and the divergence projection from step 2.2 matches $u_h\in P_1$. The continuous boundary $P_2$ moments match $\widehat u_h$, while the scalar edge $P_1$ moments match $\widehat\sigma_{n,h}$. For the remaining volume term, put $q=v-\Pi^{grad}_3v$ and integrate $-(\sigma_h,\nabla q)_K$ by parts: $\operatorname{div}\sigma_h\in P_0(K)$ pairs to zero with $q$ by cell-mean preservation, and $\sigma_h\cdot n\in P_1(F)$ pairs to zero with $q$ on each edge by the scalar edge moments. Hence every term of [F1] vanishes locally, and summing gives $b(w_h,y-\Pi y)=0$. The cell bounds add in broken graph norms.

risk_review.notes: Checked every step. Scalar dimension 7 and edge weighted-square argument leave only the cubic bubble, killed by its mean. RT2 dimension 15, onto nine broken P2 edge traces, and continuous boundary subspace dimension 6 give dimension 12. Homogeneous moments force zero normal trace, zero divergence, and a rotated polynomial gradient; zero edge potentials leave a bubble killed by the Rx volume moment. Weak boundary pairings use continuous P2 traces of cell P2 functions. Piola inverse/pushforward transport volume moments via A^T and weak Green traces without requiring rough pointwise traces. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. The finite-mesh family $RT_0(\mathcal T_h)\times(P_1(\mathcal T_h)\cap H^1_0(\Omega))$ from [[def-na-least-squares-poisson-first-order]] is a finite-dimensional subspace of $H(div;\Omega)\times H^1_0(\Omega)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be bounded connected Lipschitz and $C_P$ satisfy $\|w\|_2\le C_P\|
abla w\|_2$ on $H^1_0$. For $z=(\delta\sigma,\delta u)\in H(div)	imes H^1_0$, put $Rz=(\delta\sigma+
abla\delta u,div\delta\sigma)$. This is injective and its norm is equivalent to the product graph norm. If $a=\|R_1z\|_2$, $b=\|R_2z\|_2$, $g=\|
abla\delta u\|_2$, then $g\le a+C_Pb$, $\|\delta u\|_2\le C_P(a+C_Pb)$, $\|\delta\sigma\|_2\le2a+C_Pb$, and $\|Rz\|^2\le2\|z\|^2_{H(div)	imes H^1}$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be bounded connected Lipschitz and $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. Solve $-\Delta u=f$, $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$; set $\sigma=-\nabla u$, so $\operatorname{div}\sigma=f$. For a finite conforming shape-regular triangular mesh, define $X_h=RT_0(\mathcal T_h)\times(P_1(\mathcal T_h)\cap H^1_0(\Omega))$ and $J_h(\sigma_h,u_h)=\|\sigma_h+\nabla u_h\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}\sigma_h-f\|_2^2$. Here $RT_0(K)=P_0(K)^2+xP_0(K)$ and $P_1$ is continuous piecewise affine. The real Sobolev-space and zero-boundary conventions are [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]; H(div), mesh, and RT conventions are [[def-na-hdiv-space]] and [[def-na-simplicial-mesh-rt-bdm-spaces]]. derivations.claim: The weak solution supplier in [A1] applies because a bounded polygon is open and bounded in one direction, and $v\mapsto(f,v)$ is bounded on $H^1_0$ by Cauchy–Schwarz and Poincare. It gives $u\in H^1_0$; the distributional equation gives $\sigma=-\nabla u\in H(div)$ and $div\sigma=f$.

For any $(\sigma_h,u_h)$ in the trial family, the residual of its difference from $(\sigma,u)$ equals $(\sigma_h+\nabla u_h,div\sigma_h-f)$ by [F3]. Thus $J_h=\|R((\sigma_h,u_h)- (\sigma,u))\|^2$. By [F2], $(z,w)_R=(Rz,Rw)_{L^2\times L^2}$ is an inner product on the ambient error space.

By Gram–Schmidt choose an orthonormal basis $e_1,\ldots,e_N$ of $R(X_h)$, and define $Pq=\sum_{j=1}^N(q,e_j)e_j$. $$f(x)=\langle x,y\rangle\qquad\text{for every }x\in H,$$

Under the first-variable-linear convention the representing vector depends conjugate-linearly and isometrically on $f$: if $f_i$ is represented by $y_i$ and $a,b$ are scalars, then $af_1+bf_2$ is represented by $\overline a\,y_1+\overline b\,y_2$.

Let $H$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, let $a$ be a bounded coercive sesquilinear form on $H$ with constants $M,\alpha$ ([[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]]), and let $F:H\to\mathbb K$ be a bounded conjugate-linear functional with norm $\|F\|=\sup_{\|v\|\le1}|F(v)|$. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded polyhedral open set with a finite matching
affine simplicial mesh, let $1\le p<\infty$, and let $v$ be a real-valued
conforming piecewise polynomial whose polynomial trace vanishes on every boundary
facet. Then
$$v\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega),\qquad \|v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}.$$
Here $W^{1,p}_0$ is the norm closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$; no C1
trace characterization is used.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume Countable Choice for the published Sobolev interfaces cited below. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and use real scalars. $L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$ means the $d$-tuple of real $L^2$ equivalence classes, with norm $\|v\|_2^2=\sum_{j=1}^d\|v_j\|_2^2$. The test space $C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R)$ consists of real smooth functions compactly supported in $D$.

For $v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d)$, say that $g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)$ is its distributional divergence when
$$
\int_D v\cdot\nabla\phi\,dx=-\int_D g\phi\,dx\qquad\text{for every }\phi\in C_c^\infty(D;\mathbb R).
$$
The $L^2$ class $g$ is unique when it exists. Indeed, if $g_1,g_2$ both satisfy the identity, put $h=g_1-g_2\in L^2(D)$. Every compact $C\subset D$ has finite Lebesgue measure by [[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]], and [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]] gives $\int_C|h|\le |C|^{1/2}\|h\|_{L^2(D)}<\infty$. Thus $h\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$. Subtracting the two divergence identities gives $\int_Dh\phi=0$ for every real test $\phi$; splitting a complex test into real and imaginary parts gives the same identity for complex tests. Injectivity of the regular-distribution map in [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] therefore yields $h=0$ almost everywhere, hence $g_1=g_2$ as $L^2$ classes. Define
$$
H(\operatorname{div};D):=\{v\in L^2(D;\mathbb R^d):\text{there is }g\in L^2(D;\mathbb R)\text{ with }g=\operatorname{div}v\text{ distributionally}\},
$$
and equip it with the graph norm
$$
\|v\|_{H(\operatorname{div};D)}:=\bigl(\|v\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}v\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}.
$$
The Sobolev notation $H^1(D)=W^{1,2}(D)$ and $H^1_0(D)=W^{1,2}_0(D)$ uses the norm and zero-boundary closure conventions of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]. No pointwise boundary value is part of this definition.

The factor $x(1-x)y(1-y)$ vanishes on all four edges. Differentiating gives $\Delta u=-2x(1-x)-2y(1-y)$, so $f=2x(1-x)+2y(1-y)$ is polynomial and [F2] gives $u\in H^1_0$. For every $v\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, integration by parts gives $(
abla u,
abla v)=(f,v)$; both sides are continuous in the H1 norm, so [F3] extends the identity to every $v\in H^1_0$. Thus $u$ is the weak Dirichlet solution. Also $\sigma=-
abla u$ and $\operatorname{div}\sigma=f$ are polynomials in $L^2$, so [F4] gives $\sigma\in H(\operatorname{div};\Omega)$.

By definition $\sigma+\nabla u=0$ and $div\sigma=-\Delta u=f$, so both components in [F1] vanish pointwise. The objective is nonnegative and therefore this exact zero residual is a global least-squares minimum.
