citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice for the $k\ge1$ branch. Let $P_n$ be the real Legendre polynomial normalized by $P_n(1)=1$, and let $\Pi_N$ be the $L^2(-1,1;\mathbb R)$ orthogonal projection onto $\mathbb P_N(-1,1)$. For every integer $k\ge1$, every integer $N\ge k-1$, and every real-valued $f\in H^k(-1,1)$,

$$
\|f-\Pi_Nf\|_{L^2(-1,1)}\le\left(\frac{(N+1-k)!}{(N+1+k)!}\right)^{1/2}\|f^{(k)}\|_{L^2(-1,1)}.
$$

For $k=0$, every integer $N\ge0$, and $f\in L^2(-1,1)$, $\|f-\Pi_Nf\|_2\le\|f\|_2$. For $n,m\ge k$ the repeated derivative orthogonality identity is

$$
\int_{-1}^1(1-x^2)^kP_n^{(k)}(x)P_m^{(k)}(x)\,dx=\frac{2}{2n+1}\frac{(n+k)!}{(n-k)!}\,\delta_{nm}.
$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge2$. For every integer $k\ge0$ and
$1\le p\le\infty$, there is a bounded linear operator
$$E_{k,p}:W^{k,p}(\widehat S_d)\longrightarrow W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^d)$$
whose restriction to $\widehat S_d$ is the input class. Consequently
$\widehat S_d$ is a $W^{k,p}$-extension domain in the sense of
[[def-sobolev-extension-domain-and-extension-operator]]. The operator may
be chosen with support in one fixed bounded set.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $1\le p<\infty$, integer $r\ge1$,
integer $s\ge0$, and real-valued $v\in W^{\max(r,s),p}(\widehat S_d)$.
There is a polynomial $q\in\mathbb P_{r-1}(\widehat S_d)$, chosen by
matching all means $\int_{\widehat S_d}D^\alpha q=
\int_{\widehat S_d}D^\alpha v$ for $|\alpha|\le r-1$, such that:

- if $0\le s\le r$, then
  $\|v-q\|_{W^{s,p}(\widehat S_d)}\le C|v|_{W^{r,p}(\widehat S_d)}$;
- if $s>r$, then
  $\|v-q\|_{W^{s,p}(\widehat S_d)}\le
  C\sum_{j=r}^{s}|v|_{W^{j,p}(\widehat S_d)}$.

The second clause assumes $v\in W^{s,p}$; constants depend only on
$d,p,r,s$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p<\infty$ and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then the compactly supported smooth
functions $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ are dense in
$W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$: for every
$u\in W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ and every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ with
$$\|\varphi-u\|_{W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n)}<\delta.$$
No such norm-density assertion is made for $p=\infty$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice for the ACL and absolutely-continuous
fundamental-theorem interfaces. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open
interval, let $1\le p\le\infty$, let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$,
and let $u\in W^{1,p}(I;\mathbb K)$, with weak derivative class $Du$. Then
there is exactly one continuous representative $u^*$ of the class of $u$ on
$I$ that is locally absolutely continuous, that is, absolutely continuous on
every compact interval contained in $I$, and satisfies
$$u^*(x)-u^*(y)=\int_y^xDu(t)\,dt\qquad\text{for every }x,y\in I,$$
where for $x<y$ the right-hand side denotes $-\int_x^yDu$, equivalently
$u^*(y)-u^*(x)=\int_x^yDu$ whenever $x\le y$.

If $I=(a,b)$ has finite endpoints, then $Du\in L^1(a,b)$, the representative
$u^*$ extends uniquely to an absolutely continuous function on $[a,b]$, and
the extension satisfies
$$u^*(x)=u^*(a)+\int_a^xDu(t)\,dt\qquad\text{for every }x\in[a,b].$$

The scalar field is arbitrary, $p=1$ and $p=\infty$ are included, and the
one-dimensional interval may be bounded or unbounded. The Axiom of Choice is
used only through the Countable-Choice and Dependent-Choice hypotheses of the
cited characterisation, fundamental-theorem and completeness interfaces.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to \mathbb C$ belong to
$L^1(\mu \times \nu)$. Then:

1. for $\mu$-almost every $x$, the section $f_x$ belongs to $L^1(\nu)$;
2. for $\nu$-almost every $y$, the section $f^y$ belongs to $L^1(\mu)$;
3. after assigning the value $0$ on the exceptional parameter sets, the
   section-integral functions are integrable; and
4. the three integrals agree:
$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

Let $V$ be a normed space over $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and let
$W\subseteq V$ be a normed subspace over that same field: use [[def-normed-subspace]] for $\mathbb R$ and [[def-complex-normed-subspace]] for $\mathbb C$. If $W$ admits an ordered basis of finite
length, including length zero, then $W$ is closed in $V$. This holds in ZF,
without a choice axiom; the ambient space need not be complete.

derivations.claim: On $I=(-1,1)$ define $S_nf(x)=f(-1)+(x+1)f'(-1)+\int_{-1}^x(x-t)\Pi_{n-2}f''(t)\,dt,$ where $\Pi_{n-2}$ is the ordinary Legendre $L^2$ projection. Here $p\ge2r-4$ implies $n\ge r-2\ge3$. For $f\in H^2(I)$, the endpoint values are those of its absolutely continuous representatives from [F4]. The polynomial $S_nf$ has degree at most $n$ and matches $f,f'$ at $-1$. Its second derivative is an $L^2$ contraction; integrating twice and using the one-dimensional endpoint estimate gives $\|S_nf\|_{H^2(I)}\le C\|f\|_{H^2(I)}$ with absolute $C$. For every integer $s\ge3$ with $n\ge s-1$, the error $e=f-S_nf$ has $e(-1)=e'(-1)=0$ and $e''=f''-\Pi_{n-2}f''$. Apply the Legendre tail estimate to $f''$ with derivative order $s-2$ and projection degree $n-2$; the factorial ratio is $\rho_{n,s}=\left(\frac{(n-s+1)!}{(n+s-3)!}\right)^{1/2}.$ Two integrations of $e''$, with Cauchy–Schwarz [F5], give $\|e\|_{H^2(I)}\le C\rho_{n,s}\|f^{(s)}\|_2$. The same inequality holds for each derivative of order at most two.

Put $\mathbb Q_n=\operatorname{span}\{x^iy^j:0\le i,j\le n\}$, apply $S_n$ in each coordinate on $I^2$, and write $S_n^x,S_n^y$. For smooth $U$, $U-S_n^xS_n^yU=(1-S_n^x)U+S_n^x(1-S_n^y)U.$ Let $a+b\le2$. For the first term choose $s_b=r-\max(1,b)$, so $s_b\in\{r-1,r-2\}$, $s_b\ge3$, $n\ge s_b-1$, and $s_b+b\le r$. Step 1.1 on the $x$ sections of $D_y^bU$ bounds $\|D_x^aD_y^b(1-S_n^x)U\|_2$ by $C\rho_{n,s_b}\|D_x^{s_b}D_y^bU\|_2$. For the second term, the uniform $H^2_x$ bound in step 1.1 bounds its $D_x^aD_y^b$ norm by $C\sum_{j=0}^2\|D_x^jD_y^b(1-S_n^y)U\|_2$. For each such $j$, choose $t_j=r-\max(1,j)\in\{r-1,r-2\}$; then $t_j\ge3$, $n\ge t_j-1$, and $j+t_j\le r$. Apply the $H^2_y$ error estimate of step 1.1 to $D_x^jU$; it bounds every $y$ derivative of order $b\le2$ in this sum by $C\rho_{n,t_j}\|D_x^jD_y^{t_j}U\|_2$. Because $\rho_{n,r-1}\le\rho_{n,r-2}=\eta_{n,r}$, all terms are bounded by $C\eta_{n,r}\|U\|_{H^r(I^2)}$. Fubini [F5] and addition over $a+b\le2$ give $\|U-S_n^xS_n^yU\|_{H^2(I^2)}\le C\eta_{n,r}\|U\|_{H^r(I^2)}.$ For the inputs used below, namely restrictions of $H^r(\mathbb R^2)$ extensions, choose smooth whole-space approximants by [F4]. The estimate on their differences makes $S_n^xS_n^yU$ a well-defined $H^2$ limit. Every smooth approximant has image in $\mathbb Q_n$, so closedness [F7] gives $S_n^xS_n^yU\in\mathbb Q_n$ and the same bound for the limit.

Let $b=B_{r-1}u$ and $w=u-b$. By [F3], $\|w\|_{H^r(T)}\le B_r|u|_{H^r(T)}$. Set $U=(E_rw)|_{I^2}$ and define $A_{p,r}u=b+(S_n^xS_n^yU)|_T.$ This map is linear. The first summand has degree at most $r-1\le p$; the second lies in $\mathbb Q_n\subseteq\mathbb P_{2n}\subseteq\mathbb P_p$. Since $E_rw=w$ on $T$, step 2.1 and [F2]–[F3] yield $\|u-A_{p,r}u\|_{H^2(T)}\le C M_rB_r\eta_{n,r}|u|_{H^r(T)}.$ This identifies the constant as the absolute tensor constant times the fixed extension and moment bounds; no growth in $r$ is asserted.

Transport step 3.1 to a shape-regular affine triangle $K$. For $e=u-A_{K,p,r}u$ and $\widehat e=e\circ F_K$, two-dimensional affine pullback gives $|\widehat e|_{H^j(T)}\asymp_{j,\gamma}h_K^{j-1}|e|_{H^j(K)}$ for $j=0,1,2$, and $|\widehat u|_{H^r(T)}\le C_{r,\gamma}h_K^{r-1}|u|_{H^r(K)}$ by [F6]. This proves the displayed full scaled estimate. Finally, $\eta_{n,r}^{-2}$ is a product of $2(r-4)$ consecutive integers beginning with $n-r+4$. If $p\ge4(r-2)$ and $n=\lfloor p/2\rfloor$, then $n-r+4\ge p/4$; taking square roots yields $\eta_{n,r}\le(4/p)^{r-4}$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

For $p\ge1$ and $g\in L^2(-1,1)$, define the degree-$(p-1)$ Legendre orthogonal projection
$$
\Pi_{p-1}g:=\sum_{n=0}^{p-1}\frac{2n+1}{2}\left(\int_{-1}^1g(t)P_n(t)\,dt\right)P_n.
$$
For $c\in\mathbb R$, define the endpoint-anchored integrated projector
$$
\mathcal I_p(c,g)(x):=c+\int_{-1}^x\Pi_{p-1}g(t)\,dt,\qquad -1\le x\le1.
$$
If an absolutely continuous function $f$ is represented as $f(x)=f(-1)+\int_{-1}^xf'(t)\,dt$ with $f'\in L^2$, write $I_pf:=\mathcal I_p(f(-1),f')$. The finite sum and integral are defined for every such input; no choice axiom is used in this definition.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $p\in\mathbb N_0$, let $T=\{(x,y):x>0,\ y>0,\ x+y<1\}$, and let $q$ be a real polynomial of degree at most $p$ satisfying $q(0)=q(1)=0$. Define the polynomial $R(t)=q(t)/t$ by cancellation at $t=0$, and put

$$
Lq(x,y)=q(x)-xR(1-y).
$$

Then $Lq\in\mathbb P_p(T)$, it equals $q$ on $y=0$, and it vanishes on $x=0$ and $x+y=1$. Moreover,

$$
\|Lq\|_{H^1(T)}\le4\|q'\|_{L^2(0,1)},
$$

independently of $p$. Permuting the three vertices gives the same bound, up to one fixed constant, for each reference edge. If $K$ is a shape-regular affine triangle, $E$ is an edge of length $\ell_E$, and $h_K=\operatorname{diam}(K)$, the transported lift satisfies

$$
|L_Eq|_{H^1(K)}\le C_\gamma\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_\tau q\|_{L^2(E)},\qquad \|L_Eq\|_{L^2(K)}\le C_\gamma h_K\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_\tau q\|_{L^2(E)}.
$$

Consequently continuous polynomial data on the three edges of a triangle, each of degree at most the cell degree, have a polynomial extension of that cell degree. The estimate uses the strong $H^1$ edge norm and asserts no optimal $H^{1/2}$ trace-lifting bound.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T=\{(x,y):x>0,\ y>0,\ x+y<1\}$, let $r\ge5$ be an integer, let $p\ge2r-4$ be an integer, and put $n=\lfloor p/2\rfloor$ and

$$
\eta_{n,r}=\left(\frac{(n-r+3)!}{(n+r-5)!}\right)^{1/2}.
$$

There is a bounded linear map $A_{p,r}:H^r(T;\mathbb R)\to\mathbb P_p(T;\mathbb R)$, where $\mathbb P_p(T;\mathbb R)$ is the restriction of real polynomials in $(x,y)$ of total degree at most $p$. It is explicitly defined in the proof from the reference-simplex extension, a unique moment polynomial, and finite Legendre projections, and satisfies

$$
\|u-A_{p,r}u\|_{H^2(T)}\le C_r\eta_{n,r}|u|_{H^r(T)}.
$$

Here $C_r$ is independent of $p$ and is the product of a fixed reference extension bound, the reference moment-projection bound, and an absolute tensor-projection constant; no useful growth bound in $r$ is asserted. For a shape-regular affine triangle $K$ of diameter $h_K$, affine transport gives

$$
\left(\sum_{j=0}^2h_K^{2j-2}|u-A_{K,p,r}u|_{H^j(K)}^2\right)^{1/2}\le C_{r,\gamma}\eta_{n,r}h_K^{r-1}|u|_{H^r(K)}.
$$

If $p\ge4(r-2)$, then $\eta_{n,r}\le(4/p)^{r-4}$. This is a conservative ordinary Sobolev rate; it is neither an optimal $p^{-(r-1)}$ estimate nor an analytic growth estimate for $C_r$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $1<p<\infty$ and $p'=p/(p-1)$. For each facet $F$ of
$\widehat S_d$, restriction of smooth functions extends uniquely to a
bounded linear trace map
$$\gamma_F:W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R)\to L^p(F;\mathbb R).$$
For real-valued $u\in W^{1,p}(\widehat S_d)$ and
$G\in W^{1,p'}(\widehat S_d;\mathbb R^d)$, the facet traces satisfy
$$\int_{\widehat S_d}u\,\operatorname{div}G+\nabla u\cdot G\,dx =\sum_{F\subset\partial\widehat S_d}\int_F\gamma_Fu\,\gamma_FG\cdot\widehat n_F\,dS.$$
Here $\gamma_FG$ is the componentwise trace and $\widehat n_F$ is the
outward unit normal. The bounded C1-domain trace and Green theorems are not
used for the simplex.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$,
$1\le p<\infty$, and let
$\widehat S_d$ be the reference simplex. Then restrictions of functions
smooth on a neighbourhood of $\overline{\widehat S_d}$ are dense in
$W^{k,p}(\widehat S_d)$ in its Sobolev norm. No density assertion for
$p=\infty$ is made.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $N\in\mathbb N_0$, choose
$x_1,\ldots,x_N\in\overline{\widehat S_d}$, and let
$\ell\ge1$ be an integer. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $\ell>d/p$, then each
point evaluation has a unique continuous-representative value and
$$|u(x_j)|\le C\|u\|_{W^{\ell,p}(\widehat S_d)}.$$
If $p=\infty$, the same conclusion holds for every $\ell\ge1$.
Consequently any finite set of Lagrange nodal evaluations is bounded on
the stated Sobolev space and defines a well-defined degree-of-freedom
functional there. No boundedness at $\ell=d/p$ is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

Assume Countable Choice. On a finite matching affine simplicial mesh or a finite face-to-face affine tensor-box mesh, a piecewise polynomial scalar function whose two traces agree on every interior facet belongs to $H^1(\Omega)$, and its weak gradient equals its ordinary cellwise polynomial gradient almost everywhere. The simplex degrees may vary by cell; the box degrees may also vary.

Let $d\ge2$ and let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of a bounded polyhedral open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ in the sense of [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. A **degree map** is a function $p:\mathcal T\to\mathbb N_0$ with finite values. The broken simplex space associated with $(\mathcal T,p)$ is
$$
V^{\mathrm{br}}(\mathcal T,p):=\{v\in L^2(\Omega):v|_K\in\mathbb P_{p_K}(K)\text{ for every }K\in\mathcal T\},
$$
where $p_K:=p(K)$ and $\mathbb P_m(K)$ denotes restrictions of real polynomials of total degree at most $m$. Its **conforming hp space** is the subspace of functions whose two polynomial traces agree on every interior facet. A **matching affine tensor-box mesh** is a finite face-to-face partition of a bounded polytope into affine images of $[-1,1]^d$, with pairwise disjoint interiors. For a scalar degree $p_K$ on each box, the local tensor space is $\mathbb Q_{p_K}(K)$, the pullback of polynomials of degree at most $p_K$ in each reference coordinate. The conforming box hp space is defined by equality of polynomial traces across every shared face, and its zero-boundary subspace by zero traces on the exterior faces. For a shared face $F=K\cap K'$, set $p_F=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; its common trace lies in $\mathbb Q_{p_F}(F)$ in tangential reference coordinates. On either mesh, **h-refinement** replaces one cell by a finite matching partition of that cell and assigns degrees to the children; **p-refinement** raises at least one cell degree while leaving the mesh fixed; **hp-refinement** performs both operations. A local polynomial basis is **hierarchical** if its ordered degree layers span the nested spaces $\mathbb P_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb P_p$ (or $\mathbb Q_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb Q_p$), with each new layer extending the preceding span. Assume the Axiom of Choice for the ACL and absolutely-continuous
fundamental-theorem interfaces. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open
interval, let $1\le p\le\infty$, let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$,

there is exactly one continuous representative $u^*$ of the class of $u$ on
$I$ that is locally absolutely continuous, that is, absolutely continuous on
every compact interval contained in $I$, and satisfies
$$u^*(x)-u^*(y)=\int_y^xDu(t)\,dt\qquad\text{for every }x,y\in I,$$
where for $x<y$ the right-hand side denotes $-\int_x^yDu$, equivalently
$u^*(y)-u^*(x)=\int_x^yDu$ whenever $x\le y$.

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

derivations.claim: Define $g(x)=(x^2-1)P_p'(x)$; it vanishes at all GLL nodes and has degree $p+1$. For $p\ge2$, divide any polynomial $f$ of degree at most $2p-1$ as $f=gr+s$ with $\deg r\le p-2$ and $\deg s\le p$. Integration by parts gives $\int_{-1}^1gr=-\int_{-1}^1P_p(2xr+(x^2-1)r')=0$, since the boundary term vanishes and the bracket has degree at most $p-1$. The quadrature of $gr$ is also zero because $g$ vanishes at every node, while the interpolatory definition integrates $s$ exactly. Thus $Q_p(f)=\int f$. For $p=1$, interpolatory exactness through degree $p=1$ is the required degree $2p-1=1$.

Divide $P_p^2=gr+s$ with $\deg r=p-1$ and $\deg s\le p$. Since the leading coefficient of $g$ is $p\kappa_p$, the leading coefficient of $r$ is $\kappa_p/p$. Integration by parts as in step 1.1 gives $\int gr=-\int P_p(2xr+(x^2-1)r')$. The bracket has degree at most $p$ and leading coefficient $(p+1)\kappa_p/p$, so it equals $(p+1)P_p/p$ plus a polynomial of degree below $p$; orthogonality [F2] therefore gives $\int gr=-(p+1)\|P_p\|_2^2/p$. Since $Q_p(gr)=0$ and $Q_p(s)=\int s$, it follows that $Q_p(P_p^2)-\int P_p^2=-\int gr=(p+1)\|P_p\|_2^2/p=2(p+1)/(p(2p+1))$.

Write any degree-$p$ polynomial as $f=a_pP_p+r$ with $\deg r<p$. Step 1.1 integrates $r^2$ and $P_pr$ exactly, so step 2.1 gives $Q_p(f^2)=\int f^2+\delta_pa_p^2$, where $\delta_p=2(p+1)/(p(2p+1))>0$. Thus all quadrature weights are positive and the one-dimensional squared norm ratio is between $1$ and $2+1/p\le3$.

u_r}(\xi_r)$, $0\le

finite_smoke.asserts: 1.1 Define $g(x)=(x^2-1)P_p'(x)$; it vanishes at all GLL nodes and has degree $p+1$. For $p\ge2$, divide any polynomial $f$ of degree at most $2p-1$ as $f=gr+s$ with $\deg r\le p-2$ and $\deg s\le p$. Integration by parts gives $\int_{-1}^1gr=-\int_{-1}^1P_p(2xr+(x^2-1)r')=0$, since the boundary term vanishes and the bracket has degree at most $p-1$. The quadrature of $gr$ is also zero because $g$ vanishes at every node, while the interpolatory definition integrates $s$ exactly. Thus $Q_p(f)=\int f$. For $p=1$, interpolatory exactness through degree $p=1$ is the required degree $2p-1=1$. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 Divide $P_p^2=gr+s$ with $\deg r=p-1$ and $\deg s\le p$. Since the leading coefficient of $g$ is $p\kappa_p$, the leading coefficient of $r$ is $\kappa_p/p$. Integration by parts as in step 1.1 gives $\int gr=-\int P_p(2xr+(x^2-1)r')$. The bracket has degree at most $p$ and leading coefficient $(p+1)\kappa_p/p$, so it equals $(p+1)P_p/p$ plus a polynomial of degree below $p$; orthogonality [F2] therefore gives $\int gr=-(p+1)\|P_p\|_2^2/p$. Since $Q_p(gr)=0$ and $Q_p(s)=\int s$, it follows that $Q_p(P_p^2)-\int P_p^2=-\int gr=(p+1)\|P_p\|_2^2/p=2(p+1)/(p(2p+1))$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded open polygonal domain with finitely many straight sides and corner set $\mathcal C=\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}$, with interior angle at each corner strictly between $0$ and $2\pi$. Let $0\le\beta_i<1$ and write $\Phi_\gamma(x)=\prod_{i=1}^m|x-c_i|^{\gamma_i}$ for a vector $\gamma\in[0,\infty)^m$. For integer $k\ge2$, define

$$
\|v\|_{H^{k,2}_\beta(\Omega)}^2=\|v\|_{H^1(\Omega)}^2+\sum_{j=2}^k\sum_{|\alpha|=j}\|\Phi_{\beta+j-2}D^\alpha v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2,
$$

where $(\beta+j-2)_i=\beta_i+j-2$ and a zero exponent contributes the factor one. Let $u\in H^{k,2}_\beta(\Omega)$ for every integer $k\ge2$, with real-valued weak derivatives, and suppose constants $C_u,d_u>0$ satisfy

$$
\left\|\Phi_{\beta+j-2}\sum_{|\alpha|=j}|D^\alpha u|\right\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C_ud_u^{j-2}(j-2)!\qquad(j\ge2).
$$

For each fixed $0<a<\min_i(1-\beta_i)$ there are constants $C,A,R>0$ such that the weak class of $u$ has a unique representative $\widetilde u\in C(\overline\Omega)$, smooth up to every open side away from corners, and for $0<r=|x-c_i|<R$,

$$
|\widetilde u(x)-\widetilde u(c_i)|\le Cr^a,\qquad |D^\alpha\widetilde u(x)|\le CA^{|\alpha|}|\alpha|!r^{a-|\alpha|}\quad(|\alpha|\ge1).
$$

On every compact subset of $\overline\Omega\setminus\mathcal C$, the derivatives satisfy ordinary factorial bounds $|D^\alpha u|\le C_0A_0^{|\alpha|}|\alpha|!$. On every closed nondegenerate shape-regular affine triangle $K\subset\overline\Omega$ with $K^\circ\subset\Omega$ and $K\cap\mathcal C=\varnothing$, whose ratio $h_K/\operatorname{dist}(K,\mathcal C)$ is bounded above and below by fixed positive constants, where $\operatorname{dist}(K,\mathcal C)=\inf_{x\in K,c\in\mathcal C}|x-c|$, set $r_K=\min(R,\operatorname{dist}(K,\mathcal C))$. After subtracting a suitable constant from the pullback $\widehat u$ to the reference triangle of [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], $\|D^\alpha\widehat u\|_\infty\le C A_1^{|\alpha|}|\alpha|!r_K^a$ for every multi-index $\alpha$, with constants uniform over this family. If a closed nondegenerate shape-regular affine triangle $K\subset\overline\Omega$ with $K^\circ\subset\Omega$, diameter $h<R$, has a corner $c_i$ as a vertex, its vertex affine interpolant $a_K$ satisfies

$$
|u-a_K|_{H^1(K)}\le Ch^a,\qquad \|u-a_K\|_{L^2(K)}\le Ch^{a+1}.
$$

Let $S$ be the closed reference triangle $\overline T$, where $T=\{x,y>0,x+y<1\}$, or the closed interval $[0,1]$, and let $f:S\to\mathbb R$ be real-valued. Write $\mathbb P_p(S)$ for restrictions of real polynomials of total degree at most $p$ on the triangle and degree at most $p$ on the interval. Say that $f$ is smooth up to $S$ when every partial derivative on the interior has a continuous extension to $S$. Suppose that for some $M>0$ and $A\ge1$,

$$
\|D^\alpha f\|_{L^\infty(S)}\le M A^{|\alpha|}|\alpha|!\qquad\text{for every multi-index }\alpha.
$$

Use $\|g\|_{W^{1,\infty}(S)}:=\|g\|_{L^\infty(S)}+\sum_{i=1}^{\dim S}\|\partial_i g\|_{L^\infty(S)}$. Then constants $C,b>0$, depending only on $A$ and the fixed reference domain, satisfy

$$
\inf_{q\in\mathbb P_p(S)}\|f-q\|_{W^{1,\infty}(S)}\le CM e^{-bp}\qquad(p\ge1).
$$

For the interval branch there is also an endpoint-preserving polynomial $J_pf\in\mathbb P_p([0,1])$ whose derivative is the $L^2$ orthogonal projection of $f'$ onto $\mathbb P_{p-1}$. It satisfies $\|(J_pf)'\|_2\le\|f'\|_2$ and $\|f-J_pf\|_{H^1}\le CM e^{-bp}$ after changing $C,b$ by constants depending only on $A$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $p\in\mathbb N_0$, let $T=\{(x,y):x>0,\ y>0,\ x+y<1\}$, and let $q$ be a real polynomial of degree at most $p$ satisfying $q(0)=q(1)=0$. Define the polynomial $R(t)=q(t)/t$ by cancellation at $t=0$, and put

$$
Lq(x,y)=q(x)-xR(1-y).
$$

Then $Lq\in\mathbb P_p(T)$, it equals $q$ on $y=0$, and it vanishes on $x=0$ and $x+y=1$. Moreover,

$$
\|Lq\|_{H^1(T)}\le4\|q'\|_{L^2(0,1)},
$$

independently of $p$. Permuting the three vertices gives the same bound, up to one fixed constant, for each reference edge. If $K$ is a shape-regular affine triangle, $E$ is an edge of length $\ell_E$, and $h_K=\operatorname{diam}(K)$, the transported lift satisfies

$$
|L_Eq|_{H^1(K)}\le C_\gamma\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_\tau q\|_{L^2(E)},\qquad \|L_Eq\|_{L^2(K)}\le C_\gamma h_K\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_\tau q\|_{L^2(E)}.
$$

Consequently continuous polynomial data on the three edges of a triangle, each of degree at most the cell degree, have a polynomial extension of that cell degree. The estimate uses the strong $H^1$ edge norm and asserts no optimal $H^{1/2}$ trace-lifting bound.

Let $d\ge2$ and let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of a bounded polyhedral open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ in the sense of [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. A **degree map** is a function $p:\mathcal T\to\mathbb N_0$ with finite values. The broken simplex space associated with $(\mathcal T,p)$ is
$$
V^{\mathrm{br}}(\mathcal T,p):=\{v\in L^2(\Omega):v|_K\in\mathbb P_{p_K}(K)\text{ for every }K\in\mathcal T\},
$$
where $p_K:=p(K)$ and $\mathbb P_m(K)$ denotes restrictions of real polynomials of total degree at most $m$. Its **conforming hp space** is the subspace of functions whose two polynomial traces agree on every interior facet. The zero-boundary hp space further requires the polynomial trace to vanish on every boundary facet. For an interior facet $F=K\cap K'$, its trace degree is $p_F:=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; equality of the two traces means that their common polynomial belongs to $\mathbb P_{p_F}(F)$.

A **matching affine tensor-box mesh** is a finite face-to-face partition of a bounded polytope into affine images of $[-1,1]^d$, with pairwise disjoint interiors. For a scalar degree $p_K$ on each box, the local tensor space is $\mathbb Q_{p_K}(K)$, the pullback of polynomials of degree at most $p_K$ in each reference coordinate. The conforming box hp space is defined by equality of polynomial traces across every shared face, and its zero-boundary subspace by zero traces on the exterior faces. For a shared face $F=K\cap K'$, set $p_F=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; its common trace lies in $\mathbb Q_{p_F}(F)$ in tangential reference coordinates. This definition of tensor boxes does not include curved or non-affine cells.

On either mesh, **h-refinement** replaces one cell by a finite matching partition of that cell and assigns degrees to the children; **p-refinement** raises at least one cell degree while leaving the mesh fixed; **hp-refinement** performs both operations. A local polynomial basis is **hierarchical** if its ordered degree layers span the nested spaces $\mathbb P_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb P_p$ (or $\mathbb Q_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb Q_p$), with each new layer extending the preceding span. For example, pullbacks of reference monomials $\widehat x^\nu$ ordered by $|\nu|$ give such a basis for $\mathbb P_p$, and tensor monomials $\xi^\nu$ ordered by $\max_i\nu_i$ give one for $\mathbb Q_p$. This basis convention does not assert stability of a particular basis or projector.

Assume Countable Choice. On a finite matching affine simplicial mesh or a finite face-to-face affine tensor-box mesh, a piecewise polynomial scalar function whose two traces agree on every interior facet belongs to $H^1(\Omega)$, and its weak gradient equals its ordinary cellwise polynomial gradient almost everywhere. The simplex degrees may vary by cell; the box degrees may also vary.

For $k\ge1$, let a matching triangulation $\mathcal T_k$ of a polygon have at most $C_0k$ triangles. Assign a uniform total polynomial degree $p_k\ge1$ with $p_k\le C_1k$. The algebraic space of continuous piecewise $\mathbb P_{p_k}$ functions has dimension
$$
N_k\le C_2k^3,
$$
where $C_2$ depends only on $C_0$ and $C_1$. The same upper bound holds for any subspace imposing homogeneous boundary traces. This is an upper count only; it asserts no hp approximation rate.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space and let
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ be linear in its first argument, conjugate-linear
in its second, bounded by $M$, and coercive with constant $\alpha>0$:
$$|a(v,w)|\le M\|v\|_V\|w\|_V,\qquad \operatorname{Re}a(v,v)\ge\alpha\|v\|_V^2.$$
Let $F:V\to\mathbb K$ be bounded and conjugate-linear, and let $V_h\subseteq V$
be finite-dimensional. Then there are unique $u\in V$ and $u_h\in V_h$ with
$$a(u,v)=F(v)\quad(v\in V).$$
$$a(u_h,v_h)=F(v_h)\quad(v_h\in V_h).$$
The solutions satisfy
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\frac M\alpha\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_V.$$
The real bilinear case uses linear functionals and reads $\operatorname{Re}$ as
the identity.

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

derivations.claim: Fix $0<a<\min_i(1-\beta_i)$ as in [F1]. Call a cell a cap when its closure contains a corner. Since the corner set is finite and distinct corners have positive separation, for all sufficiently large $k$ each cap contains at most one corner; its diameter is at most $C_1\sigma^k$. On a noncap cell $T$ with $d_T=\operatorname{dist}(T,\mathcal C)<R$, the mesh condition gives $\sigma\le h_T/d_T\le\sigma^{-1}$, so [F1] gives uniform scaled analytic derivative bounds after subtracting a suitable constant. If $d_T\ge R$, the compact-away-from-corners bounds in [F1], together with bounded $h_T$ and the fixed $r_T=R$, give the same conclusion after enlarging constants. Thus each noncap reference pullback has derivative bounds $C r_T^a A_1^{|\alpha|}|\alpha|!$, where $r_T=\min(R,d_T)$.

For every mesh edge incident to a polygon corner, prescribe the linear interpolant of the two endpoint values of the continuous representative of $u$. All cells sharing such an edge are caps. On every other edge $E$, prescribe the single common endpoint-preserving derivative-projection polynomial $g_E$ from [F2], in one globally fixed edge orientation. The edge lies a distance comparable to its length from any nearby corner: for an edge opposite a cap corner this follows from shape regularity and the altitude bound, and for a noncap neighbor it also follows from the mesh ratio condition. Thus [F1]–[F2] give, on each noncap edge, $\|u-g_E\|_{L^\infty(E)}+\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_\tau(u-g_E)\|_{L^2(E)}\le C r_T^a e^{-bp_k}$ for each adjoining noncap cell, with comparable scales on both sides. Here the sup bound follows from the endpoint identity and $\|e\|_\infty\le\|e'\|_{L^1}\le\|e'\|_{L^2}$ for the endpoint-zero reference error; [F6] justifies the last inequality. On an edge incident to a corner, both adjacent cells are caps, its prescribed linear polynomial shares the exact continuous vertex values, and no tangential regularity of $u$ at the corner is used. Every edge polynomial takes the value of $u$ at both endpoints. If $E\subset\Gamma_D$, these endpoint values and the entire prescribed edge polynomial are zero.

Let $T$ be a noncap triangle and choose $q_T\in\mathbb P_{p_k}(T)$ by transporting the analytic approximation [F2] for the scaled pullback, then adding back its subtracted constant. Thus $\|u-q_T\|_\infty+h_T\|\nabla(u-q_T)\|_\infty\le Cr_T^ae^{-bp_k}$. Correct its three vertex values by an affine polynomial to obtain $\widetilde q_T$ matching the prescribed $g_E$ at all vertices; the correction has $H^1$ seminorm at most $Cr_T^ae^{-bp_k}$. On each edge, $g_E-\widetilde q_T|_E$ has zero endpoints, degree at most $p_k$, and strong edge derivative norm at most $Cr_T^ae^{-bp_k}$. Lift these three residuals separately by [F3]. Their sum does not change the other edge traces, so the resulting $v_T\in\mathbb P_{p_k}(T)$ has all three prescribed traces and $|u-v_T|_{H^1(T)}\le Cr_T^ae^{-bp_k}\le Ce^{-bp_k}.$

Let $T$ be a cap at corner $c_i$, with diameter $h_T$; for large $k$ it contains no other corner. Start with the affine interpolant $a_T$ of the three exact vertex values. By [F1], $|u-a_T|_{H^1(T)}\le Ch_T^a$. Its two edges incident to $c_i$ already have the prescribed linear traces. On the opposite edge $E$, every point has distance comparable to $h_T$ from $c_i$, so the gradient bound in [F1] and Cauchy–Schwarz [F6] give $\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_\tau u\|_{L^2(E)}\le Ch_T^a$. The interval derivative projection in [F2] is contractive, and the vertex estimate in [F1] gives the same bound for $g_E-a_T|_E$. This discrepancy vanishes at both endpoints; add its lift from [F3]. The resulting polynomial has all prescribed traces and $|u-v_T|_{H^1(T)}\le Ch_T^a\le C\sigma^{ak}$. No $H^2$ regularity is used on a cap.

Every pair of adjacent local polynomials has common trace $g_E$; the boundary traces vanish on $\Gamma_D$. Thus they assemble to $v_k\in V_k$ by [F4]. Summing squared cell errors from steps 3.1 and 3.2 over at most $C_0k$ cells gives $\|\nabla(u-v_k)\|_2\le C\sqrt{k}\left(e^{-bp_k}+\sigma^{ak}\right)\le C'e^{-\eta k}$ for some $\eta>0$, because $p_k\ge c_0k$ and $0<\sigma<1$. The finitely many earlier meshes are handled by $v_k=0$ and an increase of $C'$. Since $N_k\le C_Nk^3$ by [F4], $k\ge C_N^{-1/3}N_k^{1/3}$ and therefore $\inf_{v\in V_k}\|\nabla(u-v)\|_2\le C e^{-bN_k^{1/3}}$.

Under the additional Galerkin hypotheses, $u$ satisfies $a(u,v)=F(v)$ for every $v\in V$, and the Galerkin solution $u_k\in V_k$ satisfies $a(u_k,v_k)=F(v_k)$ for every $v_k\in V_k$. Thus Céa [F5] applies to this same $u$ and $u_k$. Apply it to the best-approximation estimate of step 4.1. Norm equivalence between $\|\cdot\|_V$ and the gradient seminorm changes only the stated constant, and the actual $M/\alpha$ factor is retained. This proves the energy-error conclusion.

Assume Full Choice. Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching shape-regular affine triangulation in two dimensions, let each cell $K$ have an arbitrary finite total degree $p_K\ge1$, and let $u\in C(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $u|_K\in H^2(K)$ for every cell. For every edge $E$, let $\tau_E$ be either unit tangent direction and write $\partial_{\tau_E}v=\nabla v\cdot\tau_E$. For an interior edge $E=K\cap K'$, set $p_E=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; for a boundary edge of $K$, set $p_E=p_K$. Put $m_K=\min_{E\subset\partial K}p_E$. There is a linear interpolant $I_{\mathcal T,p}u$ in the trace-matching space of [[def-hp-variable-degree-spaces-on-matching-meshes]]. It preserves any zero boundary edge data: if $u$ vanishes on a boundary edge, so does $I_{\mathcal T,p}u$. For every $q\in\mathbb P_{m_K}(K;\mathbb R)$,

$$
|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u|_{H^1(K)}\le |u-q|_{H^1(K)}+C_\gamma\sum_{E\subset\partial K}\left(\ell_E^{-1/2}\|u-q\|_{L^2(E)}+\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_{\tau_E}(u-q)\|_{L^2(E)}\right),
$$

and

$$
h_K^{-1}\|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u\|_{L^2(K)}+|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u|_{H^1(K)} \le C_\gamma\left(h_K^{-1}\|u-q\|_{L^2(K)}+|u-q|_{H^1(K)}+\sum_{E\subset\partial K}\left(\ell_E^{-1/2}\|u-q\|_{L^2(E)}+\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_{\tau_E}(u-q)\|_{L^2(E)}\right)\right).
$$

The constant is independent of the degrees and their ratios. In particular, if integer $r\ge5$, $m_K\ge2r-4$, $n_K=\lfloor m_K/2\rfloor$, and $u|_K\in H^r(K)$, then

$$
|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u|_{H^1(K)}\le C_{r,\gamma}h_K^{r-1}\left(\frac{(n_K-r+3)!}{(n_K+r-5)!}\right)^{1/2}|u|_{H^r(K)}.
$$

For $m_K\ge4(r-2)$ the factorial factor is at most $(4/m_K)^{r-4}$. The effective degree $m_K$ records the lowest degree among the shared edge traces; no rate independent of neighboring trace degrees is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T=\{(x,y):x>0,\ y>0,\ x+y<1\}$, let $r\ge5$ be an integer, let $p\ge2r-4$ be an integer, and put $n=\lfloor p/2\rfloor$ and

$$
\eta_{n,r}=\left(\frac{(n-r+3)!}{(n+r-5)!}\right)^{1/2}.
$$

There is a bounded linear map $A_{p,r}:H^r(T;\mathbb R)\to\mathbb P_p(T;\mathbb R)$, where $\mathbb P_p(T;\mathbb R)$ is the restriction of real polynomials in $(x,y)$ of total degree at most $p$. It is explicitly defined in the proof from the reference-simplex extension, a unique moment polynomial, and finite Legendre projections, and satisfies

$$
\|u-A_{p,r}u\|_{H^2(T)}\le C_r\eta_{n,r}|u|_{H^r(T)}.
$$

Here $C_r$ is independent of $p$ and is the product of a fixed reference extension bound, the reference moment-projection bound, and an absolute tensor-projection constant; no useful growth bound in $r$ is asserted. For a shape-regular affine triangle $K$ of diameter $h_K$, affine transport gives

$$
\left(\sum_{j=0}^2h_K^{2j-2}|u-A_{K,p,r}u|_{H^j(K)}^2\right)^{1/2}\le C_{r,\gamma}\eta_{n,r}h_K^{r-1}|u|_{H^r(K)}.
$$

If $p\ge4(r-2)$, then $\eta_{n,r}\le(4/p)^{r-4}$. This is a conservative ordinary Sobolev rate; it is neither an optimal $p^{-(r-1)}$ estimate nor an analytic growth estimate for $C_r$.

Assume Countable Choice. On a finite matching affine simplicial mesh or a finite face-to-face affine tensor-box mesh, a piecewise polynomial scalar function whose two traces agree on every interior facet belongs to $H^1(\Omega)$, and its weak gradient equals its ordinary cellwise polynomial gradient almost everywhere. The simplex degrees may vary by cell; the box degrees may also vary.

Let $d\ge2$ and let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of a bounded polyhedral open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ in the sense of [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. A **degree map** is a function $p:\mathcal T\to\mathbb N_0$ with finite values. The broken simplex space associated with $(\mathcal T,p)$ is
$$
V^{\mathrm{br}}(\mathcal T,p):=\{v\in L^2(\Omega):v|_K\in\mathbb P_{p_K}(K)\text{ for every }K\in\mathcal T\},
$$
where $p_K:=p(K)$ and $\mathbb P_m(K)$ denotes restrictions of real polynomials of total degree at most $m$. Its **conforming hp space** is the subspace of functions whose two polynomial traces agree on every interior facet. The zero-boundary hp space further requires the polynomial trace to vanish on every boundary facet. For an interior facet $F=K\cap K'$, its trace degree is $p_F:=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; equality of the two traces means that their common polynomial belongs to $\mathbb P_{p_F}(F)$.

A **matching affine tensor-box mesh** is a finite face-to-face partition of a bounded polytope into affine images of $[-1,1]^d$, with pairwise disjoint interiors. For a scalar degree $p_K$ on each box, the local tensor space is $\mathbb Q_{p_K}(K)$, the pullback of polynomials of degree at most $p_K$ in each reference coordinate. The conforming box hp space is defined by equality of polynomial traces across every shared face, and its zero-boundary subspace by zero traces on the exterior faces. For a shared face $F=K\cap K'$, set $p_F=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; its common trace lies in $\mathbb Q_{p_F}(F)$ in tangential reference coordinates. This definition of tensor boxes does not include curved or non-affine cells.

On either mesh, **h-refinement** replaces one cell by a finite matching partition of that cell and assigns degrees to the children; **p-refinement** raises at least one cell degree while leaving the mesh fixed; **hp-refinement** performs both operations. A local polynomial basis is **hierarchical** if its ordered degree layers span the nested spaces $\mathbb P_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb P_p$ (or $\mathbb Q_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb Q_p$), with each new layer extending the preceding span. For example, pullbacks of reference monomials $\widehat x^\nu$ ordered by $|\nu|$ give such a basis for $\mathbb P_p$, and tensor monomials $\xi^\nu$ ordered by $\max_i\nu_i$ give one for $\mathbb Q_p$. This basis convention does not assert stability of a particular basis or projector.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space and let
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ be linear in its first argument, conjugate-linear
in its second, bounded by $M$, and coercive with constant $\alpha>0$:
$$|a(v,w)|\le M\|v\|_V\|w\|_V,\qquad \operatorname{Re}a(v,v)\ge\alpha\|v\|_V^2.$$
Let $F:V\to\mathbb K$ be bounded and conjugate-linear, and let $V_h\subseteq V$
be finite-dimensional. Then there are unique $u\in V$ and $u_h\in V_h$ with
$$a(u,v)=F(v)\quad(v\in V).$$
$$a(u_h,v_h)=F(v_h)\quad(v_h\in V_h).$$
The solutions satisfy
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\frac M\alpha\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_V.$$
The real bilinear case uses linear functionals and reads $\operatorname{Re}$ as
the identity.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, used to invoke the published real and complex
$L^p$ completeness results through their Countable-Choice interface. Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$,
$1\le p\le\infty$, and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, equipped with the displayed norm of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], is a complete normed space over
$\mathbb K$.

Both endpoints $p=1$ and $p=\infty$ are included, as is $k=0$, where the
assertion reduces to the completeness of $L^p$. If $\Omega=\varnothing$, then
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ is the zero space and the assertion is trivial.
The Axiom of Choice is used only to derive Countable Choice for the two
published completeness interfaces; no other selection is made. Representative
selection inside the finitely many coordinate classes is finite and
choice-free.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and bounded in one direction: there are a unit vector $e$ and $a<b$ with $a<x\cdot e<b$ for every $x\in\Omega$. Let $1\le p<\infty$. Then $\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C(p)\,(b-a)\,\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$ for every $u\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $1\le p<\infty$, integer $r\ge1$,
integer $s\ge0$, and real-valued $v\in W^{\max(r,s),p}(\widehat S_d)$.
There is a polynomial $q\in\mathbb P_{r-1}(\widehat S_d)$, chosen by
matching all means $\int_{\widehat S_d}D^\alpha q=
\int_{\widehat S_d}D^\alpha v$ for $|\alpha|\le r-1$, such that:

- if $0\le s\le r$, then
  $\|v-q\|_{W^{s,p}(\widehat S_d)}\le C|v|_{W^{r,p}(\widehat S_d)}$;
- if $s>r$, then
  $\|v-q\|_{W^{s,p}(\widehat S_d)}\le
  C\sum_{j=r}^{s}|v|_{W^{j,p}(\widehat S_d)}$.

The second clause assumes $v\in W^{s,p}$; constants depend only on
$d,p,r,s$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded polyhedral open set with a finite matching
affine simplicial mesh, let $1\le p<\infty$, and let $v$ be a real-valued
conforming piecewise polynomial whose polynomial trace vanishes on every boundary
facet. Then
$$v\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega),\qquad \|v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}.$$
Here $W^{1,p}_0$ is the norm closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$; no C1
trace characterization is used.

derivations.claim: Both norm branches are Hilbert: the Sobolev inner product is complete by [F4], the zero-boundary Sobolev closure is closed, and Poincaré makes its gradient norm equivalent to the inherited complete norm. The finite matching polynomial space is finite-dimensional and conforming by [F3]. The given exact form and load therefore meet Céa's precise hypotheses, giving unique variational solutions and $\|u-u_{\mathcal T,p}\|_V\le(M_a/\alpha_a)\inf_{v\in V_{\mathcal T,p}}\|u-v\|_V$.

The interpolant [F1] belongs to the trace-matching space. In the zero-boundary branch, [F1] also gives zero polynomial traces on every boundary facet. Apply [F6] with exponent $2$ to obtain $Iu\in H_0^1(\Omega)$, so the interpolant is an admissible comparison in either norm branch. No neighboring degree ratio was used.

Sum the squared cell seminorm bounds in [F1], which gives $|u-Iu|_{H^1(\Omega)}^2\le C_\gamma^2\sum_KJ_K(q_K)^2$ by [F3]. The full scaled estimate also gives $\|u-Iu\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\le C_\gamma^2\sum_Kh_K^2R_K(q_K)^2$. Their sum with the exact factor $\chi$ bounds $\|u-Iu\|_V^2$. Use $Iu$ as the admissible comparison in step 1.1 and take square roots to obtain the first displayed Galerkin bound. The local comparisons may be chosen independently because the single interpolant was constructed from common edge traces of $u$, rather than by gluing the $q_K$.

Choose the reference moment polynomial of degree $s_K-1$ from [F5] and transport it to $K$. The degree condition makes it an admissible $q_K\in\mathbb P_{m_K}(K)$. With $w_K=u-q_K$, scaling gives $h_K^{-1}\|w_K\|_2+|w_K|_{H^1}+h_K|w_K|_{H^2}\le C_{s_K,\gamma}h_K^{s_K-1}|u|_{H^{s_K}(K)}$. The value and derivative edge trace bounds proved in [F1] therefore give the same bound for $J_K$ and $R_K$. Substitute into step 2.1 to prove the general integer-regularity h estimate, including $s_K=2$ on every degree assignment.

Under the stronger cellwise assumptions choose $q_K$ from [F2]. The scaled edge trace proved in [F1] gives $J_K(q_K),R_K(q_K)\le C_{r_K,\gamma}h_K^{r_K-1}\eta_K|u|_{H^{r_K}(K)}$: its value-edge term is bounded by $C(h_K^{-1}\|w_K\|_2+|w_K|_{H^1})$, and its derivative-edge term by $C(|w_K|_{H^1}+h_K|w_K|_{H^2})$, so exactly the three scaled norms in [F2] occur. Substitution into step 2.1 proves the second displayed bound with $(1+\chi h_K^2)$. Finally [F2] gives $\eta_K\le(4/m_K)^{r_K-4}$ under the stronger degree threshold. This retains the actual trace-degree and regularity constants and concludes both norm branches.

On a finite matching affine simplicial mesh or a finite face-to-face affine tensor-box mesh, a piecewise polynomial scalar function whose two traces agree on every interior facet belongs to $H^1(\Omega)$, and its weak gradient equals its ordinary cellwise polynomial gradient almost everywhere. The simplex degrees may vary by cell; the box degrees may also vary.

For every $p\ge1$, the one-dimensional GLL rule integrates all polynomials of degree at most $2p-1$ exactly and has positive weights. If $f=\sum_{n=0}^pa_nP_n$, then
$$Q_p(f^2)-\int_{-1}^1f^2= rac{2(p+1)}{p(2p+1)}a_p^2.$$
For every $v\in\mathbb Q_p([-1,1]^d)$,
$$\|v\|_{L^2}^2\le Q_p^{\otimes d}(v^2)\le3^d\|v\|_{L^2}^2,\qquad \|
abla v\|_{L^2}^2\le Q_p^{\otimes d}(|
abla v|^2)\le3^d\|
abla v\|_{L^2}^2.$$
The same inequalities hold on affine boxes under the transported rule. If a pointwise-defined scalar coefficient $a:\overline K	o\mathbb R$ is Lebesgue measurable on $K$ and satisfies $0<\underline a\le a(x)\le\overline a$ throughout $\overline K$, the sampled form $Q_{K,p}(a|
abla v|^2)$ is equivalent to the exact weighted energy $\int_Ka|
abla v|^2$ with lower factor $\underline a/\overline a$ and upper factor $3^d\overline a/\underline a$. These are p-uniform stability bounds; they do not bound the Strang consistency defect or equate quadrature with exact Galerkin assembly.

Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. In the **exact variational problem**, $V$ is a Hilbert space, $a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ is a bounded coercive sesquilinear form (bilinear when $\mathbb K=\mathbb R$), linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second when $\mathbb K=\mathbb C$, and $F:V\to\mathbb K$ is bounded and has the same linearity in its test argument as the second argument of $a$. Exact solutions satisfy $a(u,v)=F(v)$ for every $v\in V$. Boundedness and coercivity have the meanings in [[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]].

For a **conforming perturbed Galerkin problem**, $V_h\subseteq V$ is a finite-dimensional subspace, $a_h:V_h\times V_h\to\mathbb K$ and $F_h:V_h\to\mathbb K$ are the discrete form and load, and $u_h\in V_h$ solves $a_h(u_h,w_h)=F_h(w_h)$. Its discrete coercivity constant is any $\alpha_h>0$ such that $\operatorname{Re}a_h(w_h,w_h)\ge\alpha_h\|w_h\|_V^2$ for every $w_h\in V_h$. For $v_h\in V_h$, define

$$\delta_{a,h}(v_h):=\sup_{w_h\in V_h\setminus\{0\}}\frac{|a(v_h,w_h)-a_h(v_h,w_h)|}{\|w_h\|_V},\qquad \delta_{F,h}:=\sup_{w_h\in V_h\setminus\{0\}}\frac{|F(w_h)-F_h(w_h)|}{\|w_h\|_V}.$$

If $V_h=\{0\}$, both defects are defined to be zero. The load defect $\delta_{F,h}$ includes any source approximation or data oscillation; it is not assumed small or zero without a separate bound.

For a **nonconforming problem**, the exact space $V$ and finite-dimensional trial space $V_h$ need not satisfy $V_h\subseteq V$. Put $X_h:=V+V_h$ and equip it with a norm $\|\cdot\|_h$ whose restrictions to $V$ and $V_h$ are norms. The discrete form $a_h$ is defined on $V_h\times V_h$, and a bounded extension $\widetilde a_h:X_h\times V_h\to\mathbb K$ means $\widetilde a_h=a_h$ on $V_h\times V_h$ and $|\widetilde a_h(z,w_h)|\le M_h\|z\|_h\|w_h\|_h$. For an exact solution $u\in V$, define the nonconforming consistency defect

$$\delta^{\mathrm{nc}}_h(u):=\sup_{w_h\in V_h\setminus\{0\}}\frac{|F_h(w_h)-\widetilde a_h(u,w_h)|}{\|w_h\|_h},$$

with value zero if $V_h=\{0\}$. This residual need not vanish: the exact weak equation is only asserted for tests in $V$.

Geometry and quadrature defects are components of the appropriate form defect when the implemented form is compared with the pulled-back exact form. No exact Galerkin orthogonality is asserted after replacing the form or test space.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, $a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ a bounded coercive form with boundedness constant $M$ and coercivity constant $\alpha>0$, and $F:V\to\mathbb K$ a bounded functional linear in the real case and conjugate-linear in the complex test argument. Let $V_h\subseteq V$ be finite-dimensional, and let $a_h:V_h\times V_h\to\mathbb K$ and $F_h:V_h\to\mathbb K$ be bounded, with $F_h$ having the same test-linearity as $F$, and $a_h$ coercive with constant $\alpha_h>0$ in the inherited norm. Both $a$ and $a_h$ are sesquilinear (bilinear over $\mathbb R$), linear in their first argument and conjugate-linear in their second over $\mathbb C$. There are unique exact and discrete solutions $u$ and $u_h$, and

$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\left((1+M/\alpha_h)\|u-v_h\|_V+\frac{\delta_{a,h}(v_h)+\delta_{F,h}}{\alpha_h}\right),$$

where the defects are those of [[def-variational-crime-error-framework]]. For a family of meshes this is a uniform estimate whenever $\inf_h\alpha_h>0$ and the displayed approximation and defect terms are uniformly controlled. The term $\delta_{F,h}$ retains source approximation and data oscillation.

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

Fix an integer $p\ge1$. Let $\xi_0=-1$, $\xi_p=1$, and let $\xi_1<\cdots<\xi_{p-1}$ be the roots of $P_p'$ in $(-1,1)$; for $p=1$ this interior list is empty. By [[lem-legendre-gauss-lobatto-nodes-are-distinct]] these $p+1$ nodes are distinct. Define $\ell_j(x)=\prod_{0\le i\le p,\ i
e j}(x-\xi_i)/(\xi_j-\xi_i)$, set $w_j=\int_{-1}^1\ell_j(x)\,dx$, and define the **Legendre–Gauss–Lobatto rule** by $Q_p(f)=\sum_{j=0}^p w_jf(\xi_j)$.

On $[-1,1]^d$ its tensor rule is $Q_p^{\otimes d}(f)=\sum_{j_1,\ldots,j_d=0}^p(w_{j_1}\cdots w_{j_d})f(\xi_{j_1},\ldots,\xi_{j_d})$. For an affine box map $F_K(\xi)=b_K+J_K\xi$, define the transported rule by $Q_{K,p}(f)=|\det J_K|Q_p^{\otimes d}(f\circ F_K)$. The nodal basis on $K$ is the pullback of $\prod_{r=1}^d\ell_{j_r}(\xi_r)$. The local mass and stiffness forms are respectively $m_{K,p}(v,w)=Q_{K,p}(vw)$ and $a_{K,p}(v,w)=Q_{K,p}(
abla v\cdot
abla w)$; any sampled coefficient is evaluated at the same quadrature nodes. Global forms are assembled by summing the cell forms.

derivations.claim: Sum [F2] over cells. For every $v_p\in V_p$, $a(v_p,v_p)=\|v_p\|_{H^1}^2$ and $a_p(v_p,v_p)\ge\|v_p\|_{H^1}^2$; Cauchy–Schwarz [F5] for the positive quadrature weights gives $|a_p(v_p,w_p)|\le3^d\|v_p\|_{H^1}\|w_p\|_{H^1}$. Thus the discrete form is bounded and coercive with $\alpha_p\ge1$, and the exact form has $M=1$. The exact load is unchanged on $V_p$, so $\delta_{F,p}=0$.

Apply [F4] with $V=H^1(\Omega)$, the finite-dimensional conforming subspace from [F1], exact bounded coercive form $a$, GLL form $a_p$, and the restricted load. Its bound is $\inf_{v_p\in V_p}((1+M/\alpha_p)\|u-v_p\|+(\delta_{a,p}(v_p)+\delta_{F,p})/\alpha_p)$. Substituting $M=1$, $\alpha_p\ge1$, and $\delta_{F,p}=0$ from step 1.1 yields the stated inequality. Countable Choice is the only axiom used by [F4].

For an integer $d\ge1$, put $w_d(t)=(1-t)^{d-1}$ on $[0,1]$ and, for $n\ge0$, define
$$\phi_n(t):=\frac{(-1)^n}{n!}(1-t)^{-(d-1)}\frac{d^n}{dt^n}\bigl(t^n(1-t)^{n+d-1}\bigr).$$
The quotient extends to a polynomial of degree $n$. These polynomials are pairwise orthogonal in $L^2(w_d\,dt)$, with
$$\phi_n(0)=(-1)^n,\qquad \operatorname{lc}(\phi_n)=\binom{2n+d-1}{n},\qquad \int_0^1w_d\phi_n^2\,dt=\frac1{2n+d}.$$
Consequently, for every $p\ge0$ the squared norm of endpoint evaluation $q\mapsto q(0)$ on $\mathbb P_p([0,1])$ with this weighted $L^2$ norm is exactly $(p+1)(p+d)$.

derivations.claim: For $d=1$, the Rodrigues polynomial in [F1] is $\phi_n(t)=(-1)^nD^n(t^n(1-t)^n)/n!$. Its value at $t=1$ is $1$: writing $s=1-t$, the first nonzero term of $t^n(1-t)^n=(1-s)^ns^n$ is $s^n$, and $D_t^n=(-1)^nD_s^n$. Define $K_{p-1}(t)=\sum_{n=0}^{p-1}(2n+1)\phi_n(t)$. Orthogonality, the norm in [F1], and $\phi_n(1)=1$ give $K_{p-1}(1)=\sum_{n=0}^{p-1}(2n+1)=p^2$, $\int_0^1K_{p-1}=1$, and $\|K_{p-1}-1\|_2^2=p^2-1$.

Put $q_p=(K_{p-1}-1)/2$. Then $\deg q_p\le p-1$, $\int_0^1q_p=0$, $q_p(1)=(p^2-1)/2$, and $\int_0^1q_p^2=(p^2-1)/4$. Define $v_p(x)=1+\int_0^{x+1}q_p(t)\,dt$ on $(-1,0)$ and $v_p(x)=0$ on $(0,1)$. Its cell restrictions have degree at most $p$, its jump is $1$, its left derivative at the interface is $q_p(1)$, and its right derivative is $0$. Therefore the broken derivative energy is $(p^2-1)/4$ and the interface flux term is $-2(q_p(1)/2)(1)=-(p^2-1)/2$. Substituting into the stated form yields $a_h(v_p,v_p)=\eta-(p^2-1)/4$, which is negative whenever $p^2>4\eta+1$. Meanwhile $\sum_K\|v_p'\|_2^2+[v_p]^2=(p^2-1)/4+1>0$. This disproves coercivity for every fixed $\eta$ once $p$ is sufficiently large.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be partitioned by a fixed finite matching affine tensor-box mesh, and let $u\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$ be smooth on each box. For each cell $K$, let $\widehat u_K$ be its pullback to $[-1,1]^d$. Assume that for fixed constants $M>0$ and $R>1$,
$$
\sup_{\widehat x\in[-1,1]^d}|\partial^\nu\widehat u_K(\widehat x)|\le M|\nu|!R^{-|\nu|}
$$
for every multi-index $\nu\in\mathbb N_0^d$ and every cell $K$. Choose any $q$ with $R^{-1}<q<1$. For each common degree $p\ge1$, tensorize the endpoint-preserving integrated Legendre projector of [[def-hp-integrated-legendre-projector]] on each reference cell and transport it to $K$, obtaining $u_p$. Then the cell traces of $u_p$ agree across every shared face and
$$
\|u-u_p\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C_{\mathcal T,d,R,q}M q^p.
$$
The constant may depend on the fixed mesh; the estimate is a p-rate on a fixed mesh and makes no claim about h-refinement.

Assume Countable Choice. On a fixed finite matching affine tensor-box mesh, let $V=H^1(\Omega)$ with its standard norm, let $a(v,w)=\int_\Omega(\nabla v\cdot\nabla w+vw)$, and let $F$ be a bounded linear functional on $V$. Let $u\in V$ solve $a(u,w)=F(w)$ for all $w\in V$, and let $u_p$ be its conforming Galerkin solution in the common-degree trace-matching tensor space of [[def-hp-variable-degree-spaces-on-matching-meshes]]. If the analytic hypotheses of [[thm-hp-analytic-p-convergence-on-fixed-tensor-mesh]] hold with constants $M,R$ and $R^{-1}<q<1$, then
$$
\|u-u_p\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C_{\mathcal T,d,R,q}M q^p.
$$
This is the fixed-mesh analytic branch; it does not assert an h-dependent estimate or an ordinary Sobolev p-rate on simplices.

On $[-1,1]^d$ its tensor rule is $Q_p^{\otimes d}(f)=\sum_{j_1,\ldots,j_d=0}^p(w_{j_1}\cdots w_{j_d})f(\xi_{j_1},\ldots,\xi_{j_d})$. For an affine box map $F_K(\xi)=b_K+J_K\xi$, define the transported rule by $Q_{K,p}(f)=|\det J_K|Q_p^{\otimes d}(f\circ F_K)$. The nodal basis on $K$ is the pullback of $\prod_{r=1}^d\ell_{j_r}(\xi_r)$. The local mass and stiffness forms are respectively $m_{K,p}(v,w)=Q_{K,p}(vw)$ and $a_{K,p}(v,w)=Q_{K,p}(

abla v\|_{L^2}^2\le Q_p^{\otimes d}(|
abla v|^2)\le3^d\|
abla v\|_{L^2}^2.$$

Legendre orthogonality [F3] gives the exact diagonal entries $\int P_0^2=2$, $\int P_1^2=2/3$, and $\int P_2^2=2/5$. Let $d\ge2$ and let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of a bounded polyhedral open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ in the sense of [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. A **degree map** is a function $p:\mathcal T\to\mathbb N_0$ with finite values. The broken simplex space associated with $(\mathcal T,p)$ is
$$
V^{\mathrm{br}}(\mathcal T,p):=\{v\in L^2(\Omega):v|_K\in\mathbb P_{p_K}(K)\text{ for every }K\in\mathcal T\},
$$
where $p_K:=p(K)$ and $\mathbb P_m(K)$ denotes restrictions of real polynomials of total degree at most $m$. Its **conforming hp space** is the subspace of functions whose two polynomial traces agree on every interior facet. The zero-boundary hp space further requires the polynomial trace to vanish on every boundary facet. For an interior facet $F=K\cap K'$, its trace degree is $p_F:=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; equality of the two traces means that their common polynomial belongs to $\mathbb P_{p_F}(F)$.

A **matching affine tensor-box mesh** is a finite face-to-face partition of a bounded polytope into affine images of $[-1,1]^d$, with pairwise disjoint interiors. For a scalar degree $p_K$ on each box, the local tensor space is $\mathbb Q_{p_K}(K)$, the pullback of polynomials of degree at most $p_K$ in each reference coordinate. The conforming box hp space is defined by equality of polynomial traces across every shared face, and its zero-boundary subspace by zero traces on the exterior faces. For a shared face $F=K\cap K'$, set $p_F=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; its common trace lies in $\mathbb Q_{p_F}(F)$ in tangential reference coordinates. This definition of tensor boxes does not include curved or non-affine cells.

On either mesh, **h-refinement** replaces one cell by a finite matching partition of that cell and assigns degrees to the children; **p-refinement** raises at least one cell degree while leaving the mesh fixed; **hp-refinement** performs both operations. A local polynomial basis is **hierarchical** if its ordered degree layers span the nested spaces $\mathbb P_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb P_p$ (or $\mathbb Q_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb Q_p$), with each new layer extending the preceding span. For example, pullbacks of reference monomials $\widehat x^\nu$ ordered by $|\nu|$ give such a basis for $\mathbb P_p$, and tensor monomials $\xi^\nu$ ordered by $\max_i\nu_i$ give one for $\mathbb Q_p$. This basis convention does not assert stability of a particular basis or projector.

Let $V$ be a normed space over $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and let
$W\subseteq V$ be a normed subspace over that same field: use [[def-normed-subspace]] for $\mathbb R$ and [[def-complex-normed-subspace]] for $\mathbb C$. If $W$ admits an ordered basis of finite
length, including length zero, then $W$ is closed in $V$. This holds in ZF,
without a choice axiom; the ambient space need not be complete.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded polygonal open domain with finite corner set $\mathcal C=\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}$ and weights $0\le\beta_i<1$. For $\gamma\in[0,\infty)^m$ define $\Phi_\gamma(x)=\prod_i|x-c_i|^{\gamma_i}$; $\beta+j-2$ means componentwise addition. For integer $k\ge2$, define

$$
\|v\|_{H^{k,2}_\beta(\Omega)}^2=\|v\|_{H^1(\Omega)}^2+\sum_{j=2}^k\sum_{|\alpha|=j}\|\Phi_{\beta+j-2}D^\alpha v\|_2^2.
$$

Let $B^2_\beta(\Omega)$ consist of real-valued functions in every $H^{k,2}_\beta(\Omega)$ for which some $C_u,d_u>0$ satisfy

$$
\left\|\Phi_{\beta+k-2}\sum_{|\alpha|=k}|D^\alpha u|\right\|_2\le C_ud_u^{k-2}(k-2)!\qquad(k\ge2).
$$

Let $(\mathcal T_k)_{k\ge1}$ be nested finite matching shape-regular affine triangulations of $\Omega$, with at most $C_0k$ triangles. Write $h_T=\operatorname{diam}(T)$ and $\operatorname{dist}(T,\mathcal C)=\inf_{x\in T,c\in\mathcal C}|x-c|$. Assume a fixed $0<\sigma<1$ and $C_1>0$ satisfy

$$
\sigma\le\frac{h_T}{\operatorname{dist}(T,\mathcal C)}\le\sigma^{-1}\quad(\overline T\cap\mathcal C=\varnothing),\qquad h_T\le C_1\sigma^k\quad(\overline T\cap\mathcal C\ne\varnothing).
$$

Let $p_k\in\mathbb N$ be uniform total polynomial degrees with $c_0k\le p_k\le c_1k$ for fixed $0<c_0\le c_1$. For a fixed union $\Gamma_D$ of polygon edges, let $V_k$ be the space of broken piecewise-$\mathbb P_{p_k}$ functions whose polynomial traces agree on every interior edge and vanish on the boundary edges in $\Gamma_D$; put $N_k=\dim V_k$. This is the corresponding subspace of the variable-degree space in [[def-hp-variable-degree-spaces-on-matching-meshes]].
For this smoother class, the boundary condition means that the unique continuous representative supplied by [[lem-hp-weighted-analytic-corner-pointwise-control]] vanishes pointwise on the edges in $\Gamma_D$; no zero condition is imposed on the other edges. If $u\in B^2_\beta(\Omega)$ satisfies this boundary condition, then constants $C,b>0$, independent of $k$, satisfy

$$
\inf_{v_k\in V_k}\|\nabla(u-v_k)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le Ce^{-bN_k^{1/3}}.
$$

For a bounded coercive conforming Galerkin problem on a Hilbert space $V\subset H^1(\Omega)$, assume $u\in V$ is its exact variational solution: $a(u,v)=F(v)$ for every $v\in V$, with bounded load $F$. If $V_k\subset V$ and the norm on $V$ is equivalent to the gradient seminorm, Céa's estimate gives the same exponential rate for the energy error, with its actual $M/\alpha$ and norm-equivalence factors included. The constants may depend on the polygon, weights, weighted analytic bounds, mesh shape and grading constants, degree constants, $\Gamma_D$, and the Galerkin coercivity and norm-equivalence constants.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded open polygonal domain with finitely many straight sides and corner set $\mathcal C=\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}$, with interior angle at each corner strictly between $0$ and $2\pi$. Let $0\le\beta_i<1$ and write $\Phi_\gamma(x)=\prod_{i=1}^m|x-c_i|^{\gamma_i}$ for a vector $\gamma\in[0,\infty)^m$. For integer $k\ge2$, define

$$
\|v\|_{H^{k,2}_\beta(\Omega)}^2=\|v\|_{H^1(\Omega)}^2+\sum_{j=2}^k\sum_{|\alpha|=j}\|\Phi_{\beta+j-2}D^\alpha v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2,
$$

where $(\beta+j-2)_i=\beta_i+j-2$ and a zero exponent contributes the factor one. Let $u\in H^{k,2}_\beta(\Omega)$ for every integer $k\ge2$, with real-valued weak derivatives, and suppose constants $C_u,d_u>0$ satisfy

$$
\left\|\Phi_{\beta+j-2}\sum_{|\alpha|=j}|D^\alpha u|\right\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C_ud_u^{j-2}(j-2)!\qquad(j\ge2).
$$

For each fixed $0<a<\min_i(1-\beta_i)$ there are constants $C,A,R>0$ such that the weak class of $u$ has a unique representative $\widetilde u\in C(\overline\Omega)$, smooth up to every open side away from corners, and for $0<r=|x-c_i|<R$,

$$
|\widetilde u(x)-\widetilde u(c_i)|\le Cr^a,\qquad |D^\alpha\widetilde u(x)|\le CA^{|\alpha|}|\alpha|!r^{a-|\alpha|}\quad(|\alpha|\ge1).
$$

On every compact subset of $\overline\Omega\setminus\mathcal C$, the derivatives satisfy ordinary factorial bounds $|D^\alpha u|\le C_0A_0^{|\alpha|}|\alpha|!$. In the polar orthonormal frame the Hessian entries are $u_{rr}=\lambda(\lambda-1)r^{\lambda-2}\sin(\lambda\theta)$, $u_{r\theta}^{\rm orth}=\lambda(\lambda-1)r^{\lambda-2}\cos(\lambda\theta)$, and $u_{\theta\theta}^{\rm orth}=\lambda(1-\lambda)r^{\lambda-2}\sin(\lambda\theta)$. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$ and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Suppose
$u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ vanishes almost everywhere outside a compact
set $K_0\subset\Omega$. Let $E_0u$ denote the extension of a representative of
$u$ by zero to $\mathbb R^n$, and for $|\alpha|\le k$ let
$E_0(D^\alpha u)$ denote the extension by zero of the corresponding
derivative representative. Then
$$E_0u\in W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K),\qquad D^\alpha(E_0u)=E_0(D^\alpha u)\quad\text{almost everywhere, }|\alpha|\le k,$$
and every $L^p$ component norm is preserved:
$$\|E_0(D^\alpha u)\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}=\|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)},\qquad \|E_0u\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}=\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)},$$
so that $\|E_0u\|_{W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n)}=\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$. The case
$k=0$ is included, and complex scalars are handled by the same bilinear
pairing.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p<\infty$ and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then the intersection
$$C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)\cap W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$$
is dense in $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$: for every
$u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and every $\delta>0$ there is a function
$v\in C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with $v\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and
$\|v-u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. No regularity of $\partial\Omega$ and no
extension of $u$ beyond $\Omega$ is assumed. The exponent $p=\infty$ is
excluded, as the companion remark records.

In ZF, for compact $K\subseteq\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $\Omega$ open, there is $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $0\le\chi\le1$ and $\chi=1$ on a neighborhood of $K$. Every open cover of $\Omega$ admits an at most countable locally finite smooth partition of unity with compact supports, each support contained in some cover member. Subordination here asserts existence of such a member for each support; it does not select cover labels.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

derivations.claim: By [F1], $E_0z\in H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ and $E_0z=z$ on $U$, $E_0z=0$ off $U$. By [F2], choose $q_n\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^d)\cap H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ with $q_n\to E_0z$ in $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$. Choose $\chi$ from [F3].

Multiplication by $\chi$ is bounded on $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$. Indeed, for a weak derivative and a test function $\psi$, the weak identity gives $\int \chi q\,\partial_j\psi=\int q\,\partial_j(\chi\psi)-\int q(\partial_j\chi)\psi=-\int(\chi\partial_jq+q\partial_j\chi)\psi,$ so $D_j(\chi q)=\chi D_jq+q\partial_j\chi$; the boundedness of $\chi$ and its derivatives gives the $H^1$ norm bound. Since $\chi E_0z=z$ almost everywhere, $\chi q_n\to z$ in $H^1(U)$. Every $\chi q_n$ is smooth and compactly supported in $U$, so [F4] proves $z\in H^1_0(U)$.

Let $p\in\mathbb N_0$, $n\ge p+1$, and $a<b$. A clamped knot vector is a nondecreasing finite sequence
$$\xi_1=\cdots=\xi_{p+1}=a<\xi_{p+2}\le\cdots\le\xi_n<\xi_{n+1}=\cdots=\xi_{n+p+1}=b,$$
with $\xi_j<\xi_{j+p+1}$ for every $1\le j\le n$. Empty interior ranges are omitted. The multiplicity $\mu(\eta)$ of an interior knot $\eta$ is its number of occurrences among $\xi_{p+2},\ldots,\xi_n$.

Write $\mathcal P_p$ for the real polynomials of degree at most $p$. The degree-$p$ spline space $S_{p,\xi}$ consists of functions that restrict to a member of $\mathcal P_p$ on each nonempty knot interval and whose derivatives through order $p-\mu(\eta)$ agree across each interior knot $\eta$. The convention $C^{-1}$ means that no matching condition is imposed. For this piecewise definition, take knot cells left-closed and right-open; at a knot with no matching condition, the value is the one from the cell on its right, and at $b$ use the left limit. Thus the function value at a discontinuous knot is specified.

For each degree $d\in\{0,\ldots,p\}$, the functions $B_{j,d,\xi}$ are indexed by $1\le j\le n+p-d$. Set
$$B_{j,0,\xi}(x)=\mathbf 1_{[\xi_j,\xi_{j+1})}(x),\qquad 1\le j\le n+p.$$
For $1\le d\le p$ and $1\le j\le n+p-d$, define recursively
$$B_{j,d,\xi}(x)=\frac{x-\xi_j}{\xi_{j+d}-\xi_j}B_{j,d-1,\xi}(x)+\frac{\xi_{j+d+1}-x}{\xi_{j+d+1}-\xi_{j+1}}B_{j+1,d-1,\xi}(x),$$
where a term with zero denominator is defined to be zero. For every degree $d$ and every allowed index $j$, set $B_{j,d,\xi}(b)$ equal to its left limit. In particular, the degree-$p$ family has indices $1\le j\le n$. Its basis and regularity properties are proved in [[thm-spline-polynomial-reproduction]].

Let $p\in\mathbb N_0$ and let $\xi$ be a clamped knot vector as in [[def-b-spline-space-and-basis]]. The recursively defined degree-$p$ B-splines are nonnegative, are supported on $[\xi_j,\xi_{j+p+1}]$, and are piecewise polynomials of degree at most $p$. At a knot of multiplicity $\mu\le p$, each B-spline is $C^{p-\mu}$; multiplicity $p+1$ imposes no continuity requirement. On every nonempty knot interval $[\xi_m,\xi_{m+1})$, the active functions $B_{m-p,p,\xi},\ldots,B_{m,p,\xi}$ form a basis of $\mathcal P_p$ and sum to one. Globally, the $n$ B-splines form a basis of $S_{p,\xi}$. In particular, every $q\in\mathcal P_p$ has a unique expansion $q=\sum_{j=1}^n c_jB_{j,p,\xi}$ on $[a,b]$.

$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p<\infty$ and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then the intersection
$$C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)\cap W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$$
is dense in $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$: for every
$u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and every $\delta>0$ there is a function
$v\in C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with $v\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and
$\|v-u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. No regularity of $\partial\Omega$ and no
extension of $u$ beyond $\Omega$ is assumed. The exponent $p=\infty$ is
excluded, as the companion remark records.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying

abla_xv\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2.$ Thus $\|v\circ F\|_{H^1(\widehat\Omega)}\le j_-^{-1/2}\sqrt{1+L^2}\|v\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$. The same argument applied to $F^{-1}$, whose Jacobian is $J_F^{-1}$ and derivative is bounded by $L$, gives the reverse estimate.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let the reference patch be $\widehat\Omega=(0,1)^d$. For each coordinate $r$, fix a degree $p_r\in\mathbb N_0$, a finite clamped knot vector $\Xi_r$ on $[0,1]$, and its one-dimensional B-spline basis $B^{(r)}_{i_r,p_r,\Xi_r}$ from [[def-b-spline-space-and-basis]]. For a multi-index $\alpha=(i_1,\ldots,i_d)$ in the finite product index set $\mathcal I$, define the tensor-product basis function
$$N_\alpha(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_d):=\prod_{r=1}^d B^{(r)}_{i_r,p_r,\Xi_r}(\xi_r).$$

$$W(\xi):=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}w_\alpha N_\alpha(\xi),\qquad R_\alpha(\xi):=\frac{w_\alpha N_\alpha(\xi)}{W(\xi)},\qquad \mathcal N_h:=\operatorname{span}\{R_\alpha:\alpha\in\mathcal I\}.$$
The corresponding NURBS geometry map is
$$F(\xi):=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}R_\alpha(\xi)P_\alpha.$$
Equivalently, let $\widetilde F(\xi):=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal I}(w_\alpha P_\alpha,w_\alpha)N_\alpha(\xi)\in\mathbb R^{d+1}$ and let $\Pi(y,z):=y/z$ for $z>0$. Then $F=\Pi\circ\widetilde F$ wherever $W>0$.
The basis properties in [[thm-spline-polynomial-reproduction]] give nonnegative tensor factors summing to one. Consequently the weights' convex combination satisfies $W\ge w_->0$; the later item `lem-positive-nurbs-basis-and-quotient-derivative` records the full rational-basis consequences.

An admissible NURBS patch map is a continuous, globally injective, bi-Lipschitz map $F:\overline{\widehat\Omega}\to\overline\Omega$ whose restriction to every nonempty knot cell is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism onto its image. There are constants $0<j_-\le j_+<\infty$ and $1\le L<\infty$ such that, almost everywhere on every cell,
$$j_-\le J_F:=\det DF\le j_+,\qquad \|DF\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L,\qquad \|DF^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L.$$

A finite multipatch geometry consists of finitely many such patch maps with disjoint physical interiors, a connected bounded Lipschitz union, and matching full physical faces wherever two patches meet. Positive weights only define a positive denominator and a convex rational basis; they do not assert global injectivity, positive Jacobian, or interface matching.
